Alarms also by email, if there is an email account configured. Each notice is sent only once and is not repeated for a week.

Check that the email account is configured if you want to receive the alarms.

docs.title: 4. Moving a profile from flexy2022 to skin2026
docs.text:
Updating does not change anyone's skin: every user keeps their profile. New installations start in skin2026, and a new user inherits the skin of whoever creates them. When you decide to move a profile to skin2026, check this:

  1. Your own style sheets. The sheets you registered for the flexy2022 skin in Skins_Css are not loaded in skin2026, and there is no warning. Whatever must be seen in both skins goes to Plugins as CSS (type 1).
  2. Your own interface. skin2026 uses its own menus (Main Menu 2026, Work Area 2026) and has no logo or script of its own. The easy way is to create a 2026 interface copied from the factory one and move your nodes, your logo, your script (the global functions your templates call) and your style to it.
  3. Logo. With the sidebar folded, skin2026 looks for a <name>-mini.<ext> next to your logo; if it does not find one, it uses the logo scaled down. The dark variant is looked for as <name>-dark.<ext>.
  4. Nested CSS. A sheet of yours with nesting (&) works, but it is served unminified. If weight matters, write it without nesting.

docs.title: What also changes in flexy2022
docs.text:
Some pieces were fixed in both skins and now bring out of the box what you may already have done by hand in your sheets. If you see a duplicated border or effect, remove your patch:

Piece What changed Easy info Common card structure; the card is asked for with mode="card" in the module parameters, and values are shown as text (the HTML returned by the SQL is no longer interpreted). See Easy info Calendars FullCalendar 6, with a look similar to the previous one. See Calendars with FullCalendar 6 Lists Group by any column; the actions column stays in front Default record views At the top, the pending decision card, only when the record has one

Easy info: the HTML returned by the SQL is no longer interpreted

An easy info's values are written as text. If the SQL of an existing easy info returns HTML (tags, styles, icons), the code will now show instead of the formatting, and the card can break. Check your easy info SQL before updating: what changes and what to do, in Easy info · When updating a product.

docs.title: 5. For product developers
docs.text:
• Calendars: they move to FullCalendar 6. What changes and how to migrate your own code, with examples, in Calendars with FullCalendar 6.
  • Charts: the ECharts module is the recommended one from now on. Move your charts to it following Charts with ECharts; the old module may be withdrawn in a future version.
What Before Now What to do Forms (only your own code that touches their grid) gridstack 0.2.5 (data-gs-*, $(…).gridstack()) gridstack 12 (gs-x, gs-y, gs-w, gs-h, GridStack.init). Configured forms adapt on their own; below 768 px they go to one column If your code touches the form's grid, look for data-gs-, .gridstack( and gridstack-flexygo Font Awesome 4.5 7 with v4 compatibility: fa fa-* still works Check the CSS that adjusts icon widths (they now have a fixed width) flexygo.debug Reached everyone Designers only Check that it exists before using it: if (flexygo.debug && flexygo.debug.isDevelopMode())

docs.title: 6. Export as project
docs.text:
Export as project (new, administrators only) generates from the installed application a zip with everything needed to keep developing it as a project: configuration, static files and DLLs always travel.

  • custom folder: you choose which folders and files are included, seeing the size of each one. The document and image repositories, the folders the application writes while it runs and anything over 100 MB come unticked to start with.
  • Disk space: the zip is written to the server's disk, and before that it is checked that there is room.

Check the custom selection before clicking Export. The complete guide is in Export the application as a project.

docs.title: Deploying with Docker
docs.text:
Flexygo can easily be deployed in Docker containers using a docker-compose.yml file. The following services are typically involved:

  • flexygo-frontend (web interface)
  • flexygo-backend (Web API)
  • flexygo-db (SQL Server) optional ~ only for demos or quick tests

🧠 Recommendation: for production or serious environments, use SQL Server outside of Docker. You'll gain in performance, tooling, and options.

docs.title: ✅ Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have installed:

  • Docker
  • Docker Compose

docs.title: Docker-compose with a database
docs.text:
Copy this content into a file named docker-compose.yml:

YAML
services:
  flx-frontend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-front-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-front-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
    depends_on:
      - flx-backend

  flx-backend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
      MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: "${SQL_PASSWORD}"
    ports:
      - "60952:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-back-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-back-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
      - flx-back-network
    depends_on:
      flx-db:
        condition: service_healthy

  flx-db:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-db
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ACCEPT_EULA: "Y"
      MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: "${SQL_PASSWORD}"
    networks:
      - flx-back-network
    volumes:
      - flx-db-data:/var/opt/mssql/data/
      - flx-db-log:/var/opt/mssql/log/
      - flx-db-secrets:/var/opt/mssql/secrets/

networks:
  flx-front-network:
    driver: bridge
  flx-back-network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
    flx-front-conf:
    flx-front-custom:
    flx-back-conf:
    flx-back-custom:
    flx-db-data:
    flx-db-log:
    flx-db-secrets:

🔐 Use strong passwords. SQL Server enforces complexity requirements.

The database image already runs SQL Server Express. To use a licensed edition, add MSSQL_PID (for example Standard, Enterprise, or a product key) to the environment of the flx-db service.

docs.title: Connecting to the container's SQL Server from your Management tool (SSMS/Azure Data Studio)
docs.text:
If you want to access the container's database from your machine (SSMS, Azure Data Studio, etc.), publish the container's port:

YAML
  flx-db:
    ports:
      - "14333:1433"   # host:container

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
• Server: localhost,14333
  • User: sa
  • Password: the one set in ${SQL_PASSWORD} in the .env

docs.title: Docker-compose without a database
docs.text:
YAML
services:
  flx-frontend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-frontend
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development
      - MAINT_TOKEN=${MAINT_TOKEN}
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-front-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-front-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
    depends_on:
      flx-backend:
        condition: service_healthy

  flx-backend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development
      - ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString=${ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString}
      - ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString=${ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString}  
      - FLEXYGO_PACKAGES_ROOT=/var/lib/flexygo/packages
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-back-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-back-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
      - flx-back-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://flx-backend:8080/api/backend/Sys/ApplicationStatus || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 3s
networks:
  flx-front-network:
    driver: bridge
  flx-back-network:
    driver: bridge
volumes:
    flx-front-conf:
    flx-front-custom:
    flx-back-conf:
    flx-back-custom:

docs.title: What the .env file is and what it's for
docs.text:
The .env file stores environment variables (VAR=value pairs) so you don't hardcode data in the docker-compose.yml. Docker Compose reads it automatically if it's in the same folder, and it lets you:

  • Reuse values with ${VAR} in the YAML (ports, connection strings, etc.).
  • Change per-environment configuration without editing the compose file (you only change .env).
  • Keep credentials out of the repository (don't push .env to git).

Create a ".env" file in the same folder as your "docker-compose.yml":

Text Only
# Exposed ports
FRONTEND_PORT=3200
BACKEND_PORT=60952

# .NET environment
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development

# DB in container (demos only)
SQL_PASSWORD='<sa password>'

# External DB (if using direct connection strings)
ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString='Server=host.docker.internal;Initial Catalog=DatabaseName_IC;User ID=sa;Password=<SQL Server password>;TrustServerCertificate=True;Encrypt=False;'
ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString='Server=host.docker.internal;Initial Catalog=DatabaseName_I;User ID=sa;Password=<SQL Server password>;TrustServerCertificate=True;Encrypt=False;'

# Maintenance token (needed to update the DB)
MAINT_TOKEN='<maintenance token>'

docs.title: ▶️ Step 3: Bring up the whole environment
docs.text:
In the same directory where you have the docker-compose.yml file, run:

Bash
docker compose up -d

This will download the necessary images and bring everything up automatically.

docs.title: 🧭 Accessing the application
docs.text:
Once startup is finished:

  • Frontend: http://localhost:${FRONTEND_PORT}
  • Backend (API): http://localhost:60952/scalar/v1, the API reference in Scalar (the port is the one you publish for flx-backend)
  • Database (SQL Server): user sa, the password you defined

docs.title: 🧹 Stopping or restarting
docs.text:
To stop and remove all containers:

Bash
docker compose down

To view the backend logs:

Bash
docker compose logs flx-backend

docs.title: 📦 Building and deploying your product's Docker images 10.0+
docs.text: Flexygo's images (flexygo/flexygo-frontend, -backend and -db) and those of a product made with the template work the same way. This section is what you need to know to build them right and deploy them on another machine.

docs.title: Building the images
docs.text:
The database image carries the product version. It is passed when building it:

Bash
docker build --build-arg DAC_VERSION=1.2.3.4 -f <Product>.Conf.Database/Dockerfile .

Without DAC_VERSION the image says 1.0.0.0: the backend thinks the database is out of date and updates the schema on the first start. With the unattended installation it only takes longer; with the wizard it stays on the maintenance page asking for the MAINT_TOKEN.

The template already passes it: tools/build-docker-images.ps1 takes it from -Tag (when it is four numbers) or from -DacVersion, docker compose build reads it from the DAC_VERSION variable, and the GitHub and GitLab pipelines give it the version they work out. The product's DOCKER.md explains it in detail.

docs.title: What deploying them needs
docs.text:
• Container names: <prefix>-frontend, <prefix>-backend and <prefix>-db (in Flexygo, flx-…), or those names as aliases on the network. The images expect the frontend to find the backend at BackendEndpoint and the backend to find the frontend at FrontendEndpoint, and the backend only hands its keys to the FrontendEndpoint host. If the containers have other names, pass those two variables as environment variables.

    Each product's prefix is the one its image carries: flx- in Flexygo, flexygocrm- in CRM and flxsat- in SAT. To see it in any image, look at its FrontendEndpoint:

    Bash
    docker run --rm --entrypoint cat <registry>/<product>-backend:<version> /app/conf/appsettings.json
    - The backend's conf volume must be persistent: it keeps the connection strings, the keys and the installation-done mark. If it is lost, the installation starts from scratch. - Passwords go in a .env next to the compose, out of git, and the compose uses them with ${...}. Never written in the compose. - The database image already runs SQL Server Express. MSSQL_PID is only needed to switch to a licensed edition. - The examples use ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development" for testing. In a real installation set Production and give it the encryption key from the first start (see Additional configuration for production).

docs.title: Backend variables
docs.text:
Variable What for Setup__Unattended, Setup__ProjectName, Setup__AdminPassword Install with no wizard on the first start, only once. If one is missing, the backend stops with an error naming it (Define Setup__AdminPassword.) and, with restart: unless-stopped, retries until it is fixed. ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString Configuration database: complete string, with a SQL Server user. ConnectionStrings__<id> One per active data connection (in Flexygo, DataConnectionString), just as complete. MailSettings__Host, __Port, __Ssl, __From, __UserName, __Password Outgoing mail. Optional.

Each one in detail, in Unattended installation.

docs.title: Example 1: database in a container and unattended installation
docs.text:
Everything in Docker and no wizard: when it comes up, the backend creates the databases, sets the project name and the admin password, and goes straight to the sign-in page. The installer, with the internal database option, sets up a compose like this one, but without MAINT_TOKEN: if you are going to update from the maintenance page, add it yourself.

YAML
services:
  flx-frontend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-frontend:${FLEXYGO_TAG}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
      MAINT_TOKEN: "${MAINT_TOKEN}"
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-front-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-front-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
    depends_on:
      - flx-backend

  flx-backend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-backend:${FLEXYGO_TAG}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
      Setup__Unattended: "true"
      Setup__ProjectName: "${Setup__ProjectName}"
      Setup__AdminPassword: "${Setup__AdminPassword}"
      ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString: "Server=flx-db;Initial Catalog=Flexygo_IC;User ID=sa;Password=${SQL_PASSWORD};Encrypt=False;TrustServerCertificate=True"
      ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString: "Server=flx-db;Initial Catalog=Flexygo_I;User ID=sa;Password=${SQL_PASSWORD};Encrypt=False;TrustServerCertificate=True"
    volumes:
      - flx-back-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-back-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
      - flx-back-network
    depends_on:
      flx-db:
        condition: service_healthy

  flx-db:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-db:${FLEXYGO_TAG}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ACCEPT_EULA: "Y"
      MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: "${SQL_PASSWORD}"
    volumes:
      - flx-db-data:/var/opt/mssql/data/
      - flx-db-log:/var/opt/mssql/log/
      - flx-db-secrets:/var/opt/mssql/secrets/
    networks:
      - flx-back-network

networks:
  flx-front-network:
  flx-back-network:

volumes:
  flx-front-conf:
  flx-front-custom:
  flx-back-conf:
  flx-back-custom:
  flx-db-data:
  flx-db-log:
  flx-db-secrets:
Text Only
FLEXYGO_TAG=10.0.0.19
FRONTEND_PORT=8080
SQL_PASSWORD='<sa password>'
Setup__ProjectName='MyProject'
Setup__AdminPassword='<admin password>'
MAINT_TOKEN='<token for updates>'

In single quotes, Docker Compose takes the value as is, even with $ or # in it. You choose the MAINT_TOKEN: it is the key the maintenance page asks for to start an update.

When it comes up, the backend log (docker compose logs flx-backend) shows Unattended setup started and, when it finishes, completed. The Setup:UnattendedCompleted mark stays in the conf volume and it does not run again on restart.

The backend does not need MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: the password is already in its connection strings.

Not for products whose data is in an ERP (CRM, SAT)

These products query configuration tables (<Product>_IC.dbo.…) from the ERP database, and SQL Server only resolves that when both are on the same server. With the configuration in a container and the ERP outside, the application starts and you can sign in, but modules such as the CRM home dashboard fail ("Invalid object name 'FlexygoCRM_IC.dbo.TRANSLATE'"). Create the configuration database on the ERP's SQL Server, as in example 2.

docs.title: Example 2: SQL Server outside Docker and the wizard
docs.text:
For production, with the database on your own SQL Server. The compose has no connection strings: the first time, the setup wizard opens, asks for them and saves them in the conf volume.

YAML
services:
  flx-frontend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-frontend:${FLEXYGO_TAG}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
      MAINT_TOKEN: "${MAINT_TOKEN}"
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - flx-front-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-front-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
    depends_on:
      - flx-backend

  flx-backend:
    image: flexygo/flexygo-backend:${FLEXYGO_TAG}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: "Development"
    volumes:
      - flx-back-conf:/app/conf
      - flx-back-custom:/app/custom
    networks:
      - flx-front-network
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

networks:
  flx-front-network:

volumes:
  flx-front-conf:
  flx-front-custom:
  flx-back-conf:
  flx-back-custom:
Text Only
FLEXYGO_TAG=10.0.0.19
FRONTEND_PORT=8080
MAINT_TOKEN='<token for updates>'

The wizard suggests host.docker.internal as the server (the machine running Docker) and <Project>_IC as the configuration database; change them if your SQL Server is elsewhere.

Do not pass the connection strings as environment variables with the wizard

An environment variable wins over what the wizard saves: if the compose has ConnectionStrings__…, the value you choose in the wizard is not used.

docs.title: Without the unattended installation: the admin user
docs.text:
• If the wizard creates the configuration database (a new database on your SQL Server, as in example 2), it asks for the project name and the admin password at that point.
  • If the configuration database already exists because it comes in the database image (the compose with a database and without the Setup__… variables, or a product such as CRM or SAT with its configuration database in a container), the wizard skips that step. You sign in with user admin and password -aZ123456, and the application forces a change at the first sign-in.

Products whose data is in an external ERP (CRM, SAT)

The configuration database must be on the same SQL Server as the ERP (see the example 1 warning). With example 2, in the data databases step the wizard suggests the same server you gave for the configuration: the ERP's, as seen from the container (host.docker.internal if it is on the same machine as Docker, or its name or IP on the network).

docs.title: ⚙️ Additional configuration for production
docs.text:
Disable automatic updates in Docker

In production Docker environments, set the AutoUpdateEnable setting to false to avoid unexpected container restarts during an automatic update.

It is not an environment variable, so setting it in docker-compose.yml has no effect: it is a row of the Settings table in the configuration database, and it is changed from the Flexygo settings.

docs.title: Encryption key as a Docker secret
docs.text:
A production container (ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT set to Production or not set) keeps the passwords and keys of its appsettings encrypted. If it is not given a key, it generates one and leaves it in the conf volume, next to what it encrypts. In production, give it as the Docker secret flexygo_config_key:

YAML
services:
  flx-frontend:
    environment:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
    secrets:
      - flexygo_config_key

  flx-backend:
    environment:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
    secrets:
      - flexygo_config_key

secrets:
  flexygo_config_key:
    file: ./flexygo_config_key.txt

Create the file before the first docker compose up, next to docker-compose.yml, with a new base64 key:

Bash
openssl rand -base64 32 > flexygo_config_key.txt

If the file is missing, the application does not start

docker compose up does not fail when flexygo_config_key.txt does not exist: Docker creates an empty folder with that name instead and mounts it as the secret. The application notices and does not start, and the container's log (docker compose logs) says what it found and how to fix it; it never encrypts with a key of its own. To fix it: docker compose down, delete that folder, create the file and start again. The same happens when the file is empty.

  • Every container gets the same secret: the frontend and the backend, and each replica if there are several. A replica with another key cannot read what the others encrypted.
  • Give it from the first start. If a container starts without it, it encrypts with a key of its own in the volume, and once it gets the secret later it can no longer read what it encrypted.
  • Keep a copy of the file off the server and do not commit it to git: without it the encrypted values cannot be recovered.
  • The examples on this page are for testing (Development) and, like the Docker the installer sets up, they do not encrypt and do not need the secret.

Everything else about encryption, in Encrypted appsettings.

docs.title: Deploying with Kestrel
docs.text:
Kestrel is the web server built into .NET. It is lightweight, fast, and cross-platform, making it ideal for development environments, testing, or custom deployments in controlled environments.

Currently, Flexygo can run directly with Kestrel with no additional configuration needed, although at this time we don't have a specific installer for final Kestrel deployments the way we do for IIS.

docs.title: ▶️ Basic run (development mode)
docs.text: To start the frontend and backend applications using Kestrel, you have two options:

docs.title: Option 1: .exe executables
docs.text:
If you published the project with dotnet publish, you'll find .exe files for each application:

  • Double-click Flexygo.Frontend.exe
  • Double-click Flexygo.Backend.exe

In a product they are called {Product}.Frontend.exe and {Product}.Backend.exe.

This will bring up the applications on the ports set in Kestrel:Endpoints in each one's conf/appsettings.json: by default http://localhost:7111 for the Frontend and http://localhost:7110 for the Backend.

docs.title: Option 2: Using dotnet run
docs.text:
Bash
cd Path\To\Project\Frontend
dotnet run

cd Path\To\Project\Backend
dotnet run

This will build and start both applications directly.

The following sections cover the recommended configuration for production environments with Kestrel.

docs.title: 🧠 Current recommendation
docs.text:
• For local development: Kestrel is ideal for its simplicity.
  • For production on Windows: the installer with IIS offers the most guided experience and automatic configuration.
  • For production on Linux or custom environments: Kestrel + nginx is the recommended alternative (see the following sections).

docs.title: Running as a system service
docs.text: For Kestrel to start automatically with the operating system on Linux and restart after failures, configure it as a systemd service. On Windows, use the installer with IIS.

docs.title: Linux (systemd)
docs.text:
The steps are the same for the Backend and the Frontend; the example is the Backend's.

  1. Publish the application for Linux:
Bash
dotnet publish {Product}.Backend/{Product}.Backend.csproj -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained false -o /opt/flexygo/backend
  1. Create the unit file at /etc/systemd/system/flexygo-backend.service:
INI
[Unit]
Description=Flexygo Backend
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=www-data
WorkingDirectory=/opt/flexygo/backend
ExecStart=/opt/flexygo/backend/{Product}.Backend
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
Environment=ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
Environment=Kestrel__Endpoints__Http__Url=http://localhost:7110

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
  1. Enable and start the service:
Bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable flexygo-backend
sudo systemctl start flexygo-backend
sudo systemctl status flexygo-backend

For the Frontend, create flexygo-frontend.service with /opt/flexygo/frontend, the {Product}.Frontend executable and port 7111. The Frontend reaches the Backend through the BackendEndpoint key in its conf/appsettings.json; with both on the same machine, http://localhost:7110/api/backend/.

docs.title: Reverse proxy with nginx
docs.text:
In production, place nginx in front of Kestrel to handle TLS, headers, and load balancing.

Proxy requirements

The headers the proxy must forward, trusted proxies and HTTPS redirection are covered in Deploying behind a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Installing nginx
docs.text:
Bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install nginx -y

docs.title: Virtual host configuration
docs.text:
The browser, the WebAPI (/webapi, /token) and the MCP server (/mcp) only talk to the Frontend, and the Frontend is the one that calls the Backend. So nginx sends everything to the Frontend and the Backend keeps listening on localhost, without being published. Don't rewrite paths: the Frontend serves routes starting with /api/ (api/frontend/..., api/updater/status, api/Sys/...), and the Backend expects its own with the /api/backend/ prefix.

Create the file /etc/nginx/sites-available/flexygo:

Nginx Configuration File
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name your-domain.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass         http://localhost:7111;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header   Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header   Connection keep-alive;
        proxy_set_header   Host $host;
        proxy_set_header   X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header   X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header   X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
    }
}

Enable the configuration and reload nginx:

Bash
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/flexygo /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx

docs.title: TLS with Let's Encrypt (recommended)
docs.text:
Bash
sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx -y
sudo certbot --nginx -d your-domain.com

Certbot will automatically update the nginx configuration to add the listen 443 blocks and the renewable certificate.

Forwarding headers: Flexygo always honours X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For without any setting in appsettings.json. With nginx on the same machine the headers in the example are enough; if nginx runs on another machine, declare its address in ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies. The details are in Deploying behind a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Deployment behind a reverse proxy
docs.text: It is common to place a reverse proxy in front of Flexygo —nginx, IIS ARR, Cloudflare or a load balancer— to terminate TLS, publish several applications under the same domain or distribute load. It is compatible with both deployment modes, IIS and Kestrel, but the proxy must be configured: without that, the application cannot know what the original request looked like and behaves as if all traffic arrived unencrypted.

docs.title: What the proxy must forward
docs.text:
With a proxy in front, the one opening the connection to Flexygo is the proxy, not the browser. As far as the application is concerned, all requests come from the same address and always over http, even if the user is browsing over https. The proxy preserves that information in two headers, and both are required:

Header What it carries What happens if it is missing X-Forwarded-Proto The scheme the browser used (https) Infinite redirect loop. The application believes the request is insecure and redirects to https; the proxy hands it over again via http, and the cycle never ends X-Forwarded-For The real IP address of the client Access auditing and per-user IP restrictions see the proxy's address instead of the user's

docs.title: nginx
docs.text:
Inside the location block that acts as the proxy:

Nginx Configuration File
proxy_set_header Host              $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;

The full example for a Kestrel deployment on Linux is in Deploying with Kestrel.

docs.title: IIS ARR
docs.text: ARR forwards X-Forwarded-For on its own, but does not add X-Forwarded-Proto. You must create an inbound rewrite rule that sets that header from the HTTPS server variable.

docs.title: Cloudflare and managed load balancers
docs.text: They send both headers with no additional configuration.

docs.title: Trusted proxies
docs.text:
X-Forwarded-* headers are text that anyone can send, so Flexygo only accepts the forwarded IP address if the request comes from a declared proxy. Otherwise, someone able to reach the server without going through the proxy could claim any address and bypass IP-based access restrictions.

  • If the proxy runs on the same machine as Flexygo, nothing needs to be declared: local addresses are accepted by default.
  • If the proxy runs on another machine, you must add its address to the appsettings.json of both Frontend and Backend:
JSON
{
  "ForwardedHeaders": {
    "KnownProxies": [ "192.168.1.10" ]
  }
}

It is the address Flexygo sees, not the public one

This is not the site's public IP, but the one from which the proxy opens the connection to the server. In IIS you can read it in the c-ip field of the site log, under C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles.

Without that key the deployment works the same, but the address recorded in the access audit will be the proxy's.

docs.title: HTTPS redirection
docs.text:
When the proxy terminates TLS, the edge already enforces https and the redirection performed by the application is redundant. It can be disabled in the Frontend's appsettings.json:

JSON
{
  "HttpsRedirection": false
}

It is enabled by default and it is best to leave it that way if the server can be reached directly over http: the session cookie is issued as secure, so a user coming in over http would not be able to sign in.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Once the proxy is configured, the application must respond at its public URL without repeated redirects. If there is still a loop, see Troubleshooting: Deployment.

docs.title: Development prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you start working with a product generated by the Flexygo template, make sure you have the following installed:

.NET versions

Flexygo projects require .NET 9 SDK. If you're also going to use the MCP server (flexygo-mcp), it requires .NET 10 SDK — see the MCP › Prerequisites section for more detail.

Download it from dotnet.microsoft.com.

docs.title: SQL Server 2022 or higher
docs.text: You need a local or accessible instance of SQL Server 2022 or higher to deploy and work with the database projects. The free SQL Server Express edition is enough for development environments.

docs.title: Development IDE
docs.text:
VS Code (recommended)Visual Studio 2022

The recommended option for working with Flexygo projects.

A valid alternative for those who prefer Microsoft's full IDE.

docs.title: Required extensions
docs.text:
Install the following extensions from the VS Code Marketplace:

  • C# Dev Kit — full C# support, IntelliSense, and debugging

C# Dev Kit extension

  • SQL Database Projects — database project management and deployment

SQL Database Projects extension

  • Flexygo Developer Tools — tools specific to Flexygo projects

Flexygo Developer Tools extension

docs.title: Node.js (required to build the Frontend)
docs.text:
You need to have Node.js installed on your system.

Global PATH option is mandatory

During the Node.js installation, you must check the option to add Node to the system's global PATH. If this option isn't enabled, the Frontend compiler won't find the Node binaries and the build will fail.

You can verify this by running in a terminal:

Bash
node --version
npm --version
If both commands return a version number, the installation is correct.

Download the LTS version from nodejs.org.

docs.title: Workloads
docs.text: During the installation or modification of Visual Studio, select the following workloads:

docs.title: Individual components
docs.text: Under Individual components, check SDK-style SQL Projects and disable SQL Server Data Tools, since the two are not compatible:

docs.title: Flexygo Developer Tools extension
docs.text:
Install the Flexygo Developer Tools extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace. It provides the same product management tools available in VS Code.

Visual Studio 2026

Visual Studio 2026 does not include the SDK-style SQL Projects feature, so it cannot be used to create or modify Flexygo database projects.

docs.title: Creating a product with Flexygo
docs.text:
The Flexygo template generates a solution that's ready to start development immediately, with all the necessary projects and configurations already integrated.

Recommended way

The simplest way to create a new product is through the Flexygo Installer, which guides the process with a graphical interface and configures everything automatically. Sections 1 and 2 of this page describe the command-line alternative for those who prefer that workflow.

docs.title: Installation and update
docs.text:
To install or update to the latest available version of the template:

Bash
dotnet new install Flexygo.Product.Template --nuget-source https://nuget.ahorabh.com/v3/index.json --force

docs.title: Removing the template
docs.text:
To uninstall it:

Bash
dotnet new uninstall Flexygo.Product.Template

docs.title: 2. Creating a new product (CLI)
docs.text:
Bash
dotnet new flexygoproduct --name CRMCore --output "G:\Proyectos Plantilla\CRMCore" --allow-scripts yes

Replace CRMCore with your product's name and the path with where you want the project generated.

When the product is created, a launch profile is automatically generated in Visual Studio with the same project name you specified. Remember to select that profile at the top of Visual Studio to run the project correctly.

Launch profile selector in Visual Studio

docs.title: 3. Structure of the generated solution
docs.text:
Creating a new product generates a solution organized with the following projects:

Structure of the solution generated by the template

Project Description {Name}.Frontend Client files (JS, CSS, HTML…) served in the browser {Name}.Backend Custom DLLs and the product's business logic {Name}.Processes Custom C# processes for the product {Name}.Conf.Database Configuration database — application metadata {Name}.Data.Database Data database — business tables and objects {Name}.UnitTest Unit tests over the backend logic {Name}.InterfaceTest Automated interface and user-flow tests

The Frontend, Backend, Processes and database projects include a preconfigured .nuspec file to generate the corresponding NuGet packages. Review them and adapt them if you need to add extra dependencies or metadata.

docs.title: NuGet naming convention
docs.text:
For the installer to correctly detect your product's packages, they must follow the same naming convention as the solution's projects:

NuGet package Source project {Name}.Frontend {Name}.Frontend {Name}.Backend {Name}.Backend {Name}.Library {Name}.Processes {Name}.Conf.Database {Name}.Conf.Database {Name}.Data.Database {Name}.Data.Database

With this convention, the installer detects them automatically. If several versions are available, it will show a dropdown list to choose which version to install.

docs.title: 4. Steps to start developing
docs.text:
VS Code (recommended)Visual Studio 2022

  1. Open VS Code and use File > Open Folder to open the project's root folder (the one containing the .gitignore and the docker-compose.yml).

  2. Open the Run and Debug tab (Ctrl+Shift+D) and select the Full Stack profile.

Selecting the Full Stack profile in VS Code

  1. Choose how to configure the project before launching it:

    • With the Configuration Wizard (recommended): press the start button. If no configuration is detected, Flexygo will automatically open the Configuration Wizard, which will publish the databases and adjust the appsettings.json for you.
    • Manually: publish the {ProjectName}.Conf.Database and {ProjectName}.Data.Database projects, fill in the connection strings in the Backend's appsettings.json, and set configured: true in the MailSettings section. Pressing start will take you straight to the login screen without going through the wizard.

  1. Open the generated solution ({ProjectName}.sln) with Visual Studio 2022.

  2. Build the whole solution (Build > Build Solution) to restore packages and verify there are no errors.

  3. Select the generated launch profile in the selector on the top bar.

Launch profile selector in Visual Studio

  1. Choose how to configure the project before launching it:

    • With the Configuration Wizard (recommended): run the project. If no configuration is detected, Flexygo will automatically open the Configuration Wizard, which will publish the databases and adjust the appsettings.json for you.
    • Manually: publish the {ProjectName}.Conf.Database and {ProjectName}.Data.Database projects, fill in the connection strings in the Backend's appsettings.json, and set configured: true in the MailSettings section. Running the project will take you straight to the login screen without going through the wizard.

Next steps

See Product Management to understand the NuGet structure, versioning, and the product's lifecycle.

docs.title: Installing and using Flexygo Product Tools
docs.text:
Flexygo Product Tools is a set of utilities that let you manage and maintain your Flexygo products easily. With them you can generate your own custom NuGet packages, package your product's addons, update your solution to new versions, and automatically sync resources and configuration.

CLI is optional

Using the command-line tool is optional. The same operations are available from the Flexygo Installer, the Visual Studio 2022 extension (see more), and the Flexygo Developer Tools extension for VS Code (see more), without needing to use the terminal.

Important

Do not update the solution's projects manually, since the updater performs additional actions that are necessary for the system to work correctly.

docs.title: 1. Installing the tool
docs.text:
The tools are distributed as a .NET Global Tool and are installed by running the following command in a terminal:

Bash
dotnet tool install --global Flexygo.Tools.Product

This makes the flexygo-product command globally available on your system.

Note: If you need parameter autocompletion support in the console, you can also install:

Bash
dotnet tool install --global dotnet-suggest

docs.title: 2. Basic usage
docs.text: The main command is flexygo-product, which has three subcommands: nuget, update, and addon.

docs.title: a) Generate a custom NuGet
docs.text:
Lets you generate your solution's NuGet packages.

Bash
flexygo-product nuget -s "PATH_TO_YOUR_SOLUTION" -v VERSION [-c CONFIGURATION] [--include-addons]
  • -s: Path to the solution (required)
  • -v: Version to generate for the NuGet (required)
  • -c: Configuration (Release or Debug, defaults to Release)
  • --include-addons: Also packages the solution's addons (optional, see Packaging addons)

docs.title: b) Update your Flexygo product
docs.text:
Updates your Flexygo solution to the latest version (or to a specific version if you provide one).

Bash
flexygo-product update -s "PATH_TO_YOUR_SOLUTION" [-v VERSION] [-n NAMESPACE]
  • -s: Path to the solution (required)
  • -v: Version to update to (optional; if not specified, it updates to the latest available)
  • -n: Namespace of the product whose NuGets to update, e.g. Flexygo or flxSAT (optional; see Non-Flexygo products)

This automatically does the following:

  • Searches for the solution's Frontend, Backend, Processes, and Conf.Database projects.
  • Checks and updates the {Product}.Frontend, {Product}.Backend, {Product}.Library, and {Product}.Conf.Database NuGet packages to the requested version or the latest available.
  • Replaces the conf/appsettings.json and conf/appsettings.Development.json files of the Frontend and Backend with those from the updated NuGet.
  • Pins the exact version of the parent package in your product's .nuspec and, if it exists, in the Directory.Packages.props.

What's kept from your appsettings and what isn't

In the Backend, the appsettings are replaced with those from the NuGet, and afterwards only three of your own sections are restored: DatabaseNuget, ConnectionStrings, and MailSettings. Any other custom key you added to those files is lost.

In the Frontend they are overwritten directly, with nothing preserved.

If you have your own configuration, keep it outside those files or make a copy before updating.

Version channel (prereleases)

If the version you have installed is a prerelease — it contains a hyphen, like 1.5.0-beta.9 —, the "latest version" search automatically includes prereleases and you stay on your channel. If you're on a stable version, only stable versions are considered.

If your solution has addons, update also updates the {Product}.Library package consumed by each addon's Processes, and if the addon's .nuspec declares that dependency, it syncs its pinned version.

docs.title: Non-Flexygo products
docs.text:
By default the tool detects the product's namespace on its own, by reading the PackageReference of your solution's *.Frontend.csproj files. You only need -n if detection fails because it finds none or finds several different ones. To see the officially supported namespaces:

Bash
flexygo-product products

docs.title: c) Packaging addons
docs.text:
An addon is an extension that is installed on top of an already-deployed Flexygo product. It's distributed as its own NuGet and has its own version cycle, independent from the product's. A product can have several addons.

They're created with the template, by running the command from the folder that contains the product's .sln:

Bash
dotnet new flexygoaddon --name Facturacion --allow-scripts yes

Each addon lives in its own folder with a config/module.json and a single .nuspec at its root. Those two files are what the tool uses to detect it, so the addon's name is free and doesn't have to be derived from the product's name.

Bash
flexygo-product addon -s "PATH_TO_YOUR_SOLUTION" [-a NAME] [-v VERSION] [-c CONFIGURATION]
  • -s: Path to the solution (required)
  • -a: Name of the addon to package (optional, repeatable; if not specified, all detected addons are packaged)
  • -v: Addon version (optional; if not specified, the one already declared in its .nuspec is used)
  • -c: Configuration (Release or Debug, defaults to Release)

Examples:

Bash
# All addons, each with the version from its own .nuspec
flexygo-product addon -s "C:\Proyectos\CRMCore"

# Just one
flexygo-product addon -s "C:\Proyectos\CRMCore" -a Facturacion

# Several specific addons
flexygo-product addon -s "C:\Proyectos\CRMCore" -a Facturacion -a Portal

# Bump an addon's version and package it
flexygo-product addon -s "C:\Proyectos\CRMCore" -a Facturacion -v 2.0.0.5

When you specify -v, the version is written into the addon's .nuspec and stays there for subsequent runs, so remember to commit that change. Since each addon has its own cycle, -v is only accepted when you've selected a single addon with -a; to bump several, run the command once per addon.

Order matters

The nuget subcommand clears the publish\nuget folder before generating. If you're going to generate the product and addons separately, always run nuget before addon, or you'll lose the addon packages already generated.

Product and addons in a single pass

For the release flow, flexygo-product nuget -s "PATH" -v 1.2.3 --include-addons generates the product's packages and then those of all the addons. Addons never inherit the version specified in -v: each is packaged with the one from its own .nuspec. To change it, use the addon subcommand with -v.

If an addon fails to build or package, the rest are not aborted: the other addons and the product's packages are still generated, the failed ones are listed in the final summary, and the command exits with code 3.

Database projects are always built in Release

The .nuspec generated by the addon template takes the .dacpac files from bin\Release. That's why its database projects are built in Release even if you specify -c Debug — otherwise, an outdated .dacpac would be packaged or packaging would fail. The -c option does apply to the addon's Processes project.

docs.title: 3. Available options
docs.text:
You can see all the options at any time with:

Bash
flexygo-product --help

And the specific help for each subcommand, which documents its behavior in detail:

Bash
flexygo-product update --help
flexygo-product nuget  --help
flexygo-product addon  --help

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Useful if you integrate the tool into a CI pipeline:

Command Code Meaning update 0 Everything OK update 1 Error; the command aborts on the first failure nuget 0 Everything OK nuget 2 Error generating the product's packages nuget 3 The product was generated, but some addon failed addon 0 Everything OK addon 3 At least one addon failed

docs.title: 4. Important notes
docs.text:
• It's advisable to back up your solution before updating packages and resources, especially if you have manual modifications in the wwwroot folders.
  • After updating, review the appsettings file in case you want to adjust any new setting.

NuGet naming convention

For the installer to correctly detect your product's packages they must follow the standard naming convention. See the NuGet naming convention section in the product creation guide.

docs.title: IDE Extensions
docs.text:
The Flexygo Developer Tools extension is available for VS Code and Visual Studio 2022. From the IDE, without using the command line, it lets you generate and publish your product's NuGet packages and update it to new Flexygo versions. The VS Code one also covers the whole development cycle: creating the product, configuring and publishing its databases, debugging, working with Docker and deploying it.

VS Code (recommended)Visual Studio 2022

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code.
  2. Go to the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  3. Search for Flexygo Developer Tools and click Install.

Flexygo Developer Tools extension in the VS Code marketplace

The extension activates when you open a folder that contains a solution (.sln). It needs the .NET SDK: with it, it installs and updates the tools it uses on its own (Flexygo.Tools.Product and SqlPackage), so you don't have to install them by hand. To open the databases from the panel you also need Microsoft's SQL Server (mssql) extension.

docs.title: The Flexygo panel
docs.text:
Everything is done from the Flexygo panel, which opens from the fl icon in the Activity Bar (on the left). What it shows depends on the open folder:

  • A Flexygo solution (with *.Backend, *.Frontend and *.Conf.Database projects): the project status and every action, as explained below.
  • An empty folder: the button to create a new product.
  • A Flexygo project for .NET Framework: a warning that it uses an outdated version and the button to migrate it.
  • Any other folder: a warning that it is not a Flexygo project.

Flexygo panel: project status at the top and the actions grouped below

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
The top part sums up the state of the solution. Each line has a coloured dot: green when it's fine, yellow when it's worth a look and red when there is a problem. It refreshes on its own when the appsettings files change; the icon in the top corner checks again by hand.

Line What it shows Flexygo version The product and the Flexygo version the solution uses. Green when it's the latest stable; yellow for a pre-release (beta), with the latest stable next to it; red when a new version is available. When there is a newer one, the Update button appears. Branch The git branch and whether there are uncommitted changes or commits ahead or behind. Clicking it opens the Source Control view. Databases One line per connection string (ConfConnectionString and DataConnectionString), with the server and the database. It is checked with a real connection: green when the database exists, yellow when the server responds but the database doesn't exist yet (it needs publishing) and red when it isn't configured or can't connect. Active origin The active origin of the Origins table in the configuration database: green for Product, yellow for Project and red for System or User.

Next to each database there are two icons:

  • Open in SQL Server view: opens the database in the SQL Server (mssql) extension, already connected with the Backend's connection string.
  • Edit connection string: asks in four steps for the server, the database, the user and the password, and saves the connection string in appsettings.Development.json. It suggests the values already there; when there are none, localhost, sa and the solution name (<Prefix>_IC for the configuration database).

First of the four steps: the SQL Server host

The Change button of the active origin lists the origins in the Origins table and activates the one you pick, the same as the origin selector of the application's develop mode. If the data database also has its own Origins table, it is kept the same as the configuration one.

The ticked origin is the active one

docs.title: Run actions
docs.text:
Debug (also F5) starts the application with the debugger. Before launching it:

  1. If a connection string is empty, it asks for its details.
  2. If the server responds but the database doesn't exist, it creates it.
  3. It checks that the Backend and Frontend ports are free. If one is taken, it offers to move it to the next free port and updates the appsettings of both projects so they keep finding each other.
  4. It launches the compound configuration in .vscode/launch.json (for example, Launch Full Stack). If there is none, it lets you pick one of the individual configurations.

Publish Databases builds the database projects (*.Conf.Database.sqlproj and *.Data.Database.sqlproj) and publishes them with SqlPackage to the database the Backend's connection string points to. There is one button to publish them all and one for each.

If the database already exists, it asks what to do with it:

  • Overwrite: drops it and creates it again from scratch.
  • Keep Data: publishes only the changes and keeps what is already there.

Question before publishing over a database that already exists

Overwrite deletes all the data

With the Overwrite databases without asking switch on, the extension no longer asks: it drops and recreates every database it publishes, and all their data is lost. Leave it off except for test databases.

docs.title: Deploy actions
docs.text:
Generate NuGets creates the product's NuGet packages. It asks for the package version (for example 1.2.3, 1.2.3.4 or 1.2.3-beta.1) and builds the packages in Release with flexygo-product nuget. The Flexygo Core output channel says which folder they were written to.

Version of the packages to generate

If the solution has the <Prefix>-version.json file of the product templates, it suggests the same version continuous integration would calculate for the branch: X.Y.0.N on main or master, X.Y.N-beta.1 on develop and -alpha on the rest.

Pre-release versions

A version with a suffix (-beta, -alpha) must have three numbers: 1.0.5-beta.1, not 1.0.5.1-beta. With four numbers the build fails, and the extension warns about it before starting.

Update Flexygo Version updates the solution to another Flexygo version with flexygo-product update. It lists the stable versions in the feed, newest first, and asks for confirmation before starting.

Available versions; the first option is always the latest

Clear NuGet Cache deletes every local NuGet cache (dotnet nuget locals all --clear), after you confirm it. It helps when a package you just published isn't downloaded or an old version sticks around.

Confirmation before clearing the cache

Build & Run Docker asks for a Docker Compose project name and runs docker compose -p <name> up in a VS Code terminal, which shows the log as it goes. To stop it, stop it from that terminal.

Docker Compose project name

docs.title: Publish actions
docs.text:
Generate & Publish NuGets generates the packages the same way as Generate NuGets and pushes them to a NuGet feed. It asks for everything up front, so a build of several minutes isn't interrupted later:

  1. The package version.
  2. The feed URL (.../v3/index.json). It suggests the last one used.
  3. The feed's API key. It can be saved for next time; it is stored encrypted in the operating system's credential store.

Second step: the NuGet feed the packages are published to

Build & Publish Docker Images builds the images of the docker-compose services that have a build section and pushes them to a registry. It asks for the registry URL (docker.io by default, optionally with the repository path), the user, the password or token and the image tag, which defaults to the product version. The credentials can also be saved encrypted.

First step: the registry the images are published to

To delete the saved API key and credentials, use the Flexygo: Forget Saved Publish Credentials command from the Command Palette. When the extension uses saved credentials, it says so and offers to forget them in case they are no longer valid.

Deploy Product (beta) registers the solution as a product in the Cenit platform, so it can be deployed from there. It is done in a window with three steps, and nothing is sent until you review the product and click Accept and publish:

  1. Connection: the platform host (for example, cloud.mydomain.com) and the Cenit token. The token can be remembered, encrypted in the credential store.
  2. Review the product: name, description, logo, website, version (the image tag), the variables asked for when deploying and the docker-compose template, generated from the solution's own. Each variable has a mode: Text (visible and editable), Secret (editable and masked), ReadOnly (visible and fixed) or Hidden (invisible and fixed). This is also where you choose whether to build and push the images, whether to generate and publish the database NuGets and whether to run a test deployment. Under Advanced you can change the registry and the NuGet feed; by default they are Cenit's.
  3. Publish: shows the progress of each step. If a test deployment was requested, it creates a test customer and application, waits for them to install and lets you open the application to check it; Clean up and finish deletes them afterwards.

First step: connection to the Cenit platform

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text:
At the bottom of the panel there are three buttons:

  • Help: opens this help.
  • Support: opens the support portal.
  • Check Updates: opens a window with the installed version of the extension and of the tools it uses (Flexygo.Tools.Product and flexygo-mcp), with a button to update each tool. When there is an update, the button shows an orange dot.

Installed and available versions of the extension and its tools

docs.title: Create a new product
docs.text:
With an empty folder open, the panel offers Create New Product:

With an empty folder, the panel only offers to create a product

  1. Pick the product template. The list comes from the templates published in the NuGet feed, with their version.

    Available product templates

  2. Type the product name: letters, numbers and _, starting with a letter. By default it suggests the folder name.

    Product name

  3. The extension installs or updates the template (dotnet new install) and generates the product in the open folder.

docs.title: Migrate an old project
docs.text:
If the open folder is a Flexygo product for .NET Framework (with the Flexygo package in a packages.config), the panel shows the version it uses and offers Migrate to Flexygo Core:

Outdated version warning, with the project's Flexygo version

The button opens a window with two paths:

  • With AI (Claude Code): the extension installs the flexygo-migrar-core skill in Claude Code's skills folder (~/.claude/skills). The skill does the whole migration: it creates the branch, updates the Flexygo NuGet, runs the installer, places the new solution in the repository, validates and fixes it, and writes a report, with one commit per phase. Copy the /flexygo-migrar-core command and paste it in Claude Code, or use Open Claude Code in a terminal.
  • Without AI: download the Flexygo installer and follow the steps the window shows, with this project's path. The installer's migration mode is explained in Installer: Migration Mode.

The two ways to migrate: with Claude Code or with the installer

Minimum version to migrate

The installer requires the project to be on Flexygo 9.2.0.1 or later. If it's older, the window says so: first update the Flexygo NuGet package from Visual Studio and check that the solution builds.

docs.title: Other ways to run the commands
docs.text:
Every action is also in the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), starting with Flexygo:. Some are only there, such as Forget Saved Publish Credentials.

Flexygo commands in the Command Palette

The most common ones are also in the Explorer's context menu (right-click on any folder or file):

Flexygo commands at the end of the context menu

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
In the VS Code settings (Ctrl+,), Flexygo section:

Setting What it's for flexygo.productNamespace The product namespace (for example, Flexygo or flxSAT). When empty, it is detected from the solution's package references; if there are several, the extension asks which one to use. flexygo.helpUrl Page the Help button opens. By default, https://ayuda.ahora.es. flexygo.supportUrl Page the Support button opens. By default, https://flexygodesk.ahora.es.

Everything the commands do is logged in the Flexygo Core output channel (View → Output and pick Flexygo Core in the list). If something fails, the full error is there.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Open Visual Studio.
  2. Go to the Extensions menu and select Manage Extensions.
  3. In the search box, type Flexygo Developer Tools.
  4. When the extension appears in the results, click Download.
  5. Restart Visual Studio to complete the installation.

Once installed, you'll find the toolbar under View → Toolbars → Flexygo Tools Product.

Toolbar with the update and generate NuGets buttons

Update button (left) and generate NuGets button (right)

docs.title: Updating the product
docs.text:
1. Click the update button on the toolbar.
  2. Select the version you want to update to; the latest available is shown by default.
  1. Confirm the update in the confirmation window.
  1. Follow the progress in the output tab.

docs.title: Generating NuGets
docs.text:
1. Click the generate NuGets button on the toolbar.
  2. Enter the version of the NuGet package you want to generate.
  1. Confirm the generation in the confirmation window.
  1. Follow the progress in the output tab. When finished, the folder with the generated packages will open.

docs.title: Asset Customization
docs.text: Flexygo lets you customize the product's visual appearance at every level without modifying the platform's core. Customizations are done through asset files — CSS, JS, favicon, PWA manifest, and theme variables — that survive application updates.

docs.title: Customization levels and priority
docs.text:
Flexygo resolves assets through a 3-level chain. Each level can provide its own version of any supported file. Higher levels take priority.

Priority Level Path root Who uses it 1 (highest) Installation custom/ End-customer installations 2 Product {product-folder}/ Product branding / white-label 3 (lowest) Flexygo (wwwroot root) Flexygo's native defaults

How priority works:

  • For CSS/JS files, every level containing the file is emitted on the page, in order from lowest to highest priority. The browser's CSS cascade and the script execution order let the higher-priority customizations win.
  • For single files (manifest.json, favicon.ico), only the file found at the highest priority is used (first-found-wins).

docs.title: Automatic discovery of the product folder
docs.text:
The product folder is discovered automatically when the application starts — you don't need to configure its name. The system scans the subdirectories of wwwroot and treats as the product folder the first one that contains the marker file css/theme.less. The first match wins.

css/theme.less is the product folder marker

A wwwroot folder is only detected as a product folder if it contains css/theme.less. The file can be empty, but it must exist. Without it, the folder is ignored entirely and all your product-level customizations (CSS, JS, favicon.ico, manifest.json…) will have no effect, degrading the system to the 2-level chain (Installation → Flexygo).

theme.less is NOT created by default

The project template does not include css/theme.less, on purpose. You must create it (together with the product folder) only when you actually want to customize something at product level.

Since it acts as the product folder marker, it only makes sense to create it once there is something to customize.

Valid folder names

The product folder's name can only contain the characters [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+. Other characters will be rejected for security reasons.

docs.title: Product level ({product-folder}/)
docs.text:
Text Only
wwwroot/
  my-product/                        ← Your product folder (any valid name)
    manifest.json                    ← PWA manifest
    favicon.ico                      ← Product favicon
    css/
      theme.less                     ← Product folder marker (create it when you customize; can be empty) + theme variables
      views/
        account/
          account.css                ← Generic account CSS
          login/login.css            ← Page-specific CSS
          register/register.css
          forgot/forgot.css
          authentication/authentication.css
          manage-password/manage-password.css
    js/
      views/
        account/
          account.js                 ← Generic account JS
          login/login.js             ← Page-specific JS
          register/register.js
          forgot/forgot.js
          authentication/authentication.js
          manage-password/manage-password.js

docs.title: Installation level (custom/)
docs.text:
Text Only
wwwroot/
  custom/
    manifest.json                    ← PWA manifest override
    favicon.ico                      ← Favicon override
    css/
      theme.less                     ← Installation theme variables
      views/
        account/
          account.css                ← Generic account CSS
          login/login.css
          register/register.css
          ...
    js/
      views/
        account/
          account.js                 ← Generic account JS
          login/login.js
          register/register.js
          ...

Compatibility note: There's a legacy flat path custom/css/account.css for the Maintenance view. The AssetOverrideResolver system uses the nested structure custom/css/views/account/ documented here. Plan a future migration if you currently depend on the flat path.

docs.title: manifest.json — PWA Manifest
docs.text:
Resolution: First-found-wins (only the highest-priority file is used).

Level Path Installation custom/manifest.json Product {product}/manifest.json Flexygo manifest.json

Example — Product-level manifest:

JSON
{
  "name": "MyProduct",
  "short_name": "MyProduct",
  "start_url": "/",
  "display": "standalone",
  "icons": [{
    "src": "assets/icon/icon192.png",
    "sizes": "192x192",
    "type": "image/png"
  }, {
    "src": "assets/icon/icon512.png",
    "sizes": "512x512",
    "type": "image/png"
  }],
  "background_color": "#1a1a2e",
  "theme_color": "#e94560"
}

Place this file at wwwroot/{product}/manifest.json.

docs.title: theme.less — Theme Variables and CSS Properties
docs.text:
Purpose: Receive product-specific values from the database, assign them to Less variables, and expose them as custom CSS properties (--*).

Dual role: it's also the product folder marker

The presence of {product}/css/theme.less is what makes Flexygo recognize {product}/ as the product folder. It is not created by default: create it when you want to apply product-level customizations. Once you have a product folder with customizations (CSS, JS, favicon, manifest…), it must exist, even as an empty file, if you're not going to define your own theme variables.

Resolution: The 3 levels are concatenated (Flexygo → Product → Installation). The ReplaceLessVars pipeline processes the theme.less of each level: the dbColor()/dbSize() placeholders are replaced with values calculated from the database, and the Less variables are turned into CSS properties via :root { --*: @variable; }.

Level Path Installation custom/css/theme.less Product {product}/css/theme.less Flexygo css/theme.less

Structure of a theme.less file:

LessCss
/* === STEP 1: Map database values to Less variables === */
@header-color: dbColor(HeaderColor);
@menu-color: dbColor(MenuColor);
@bg-color: dbColor(bgColor);
@primary-color: dbColor(PrimaryColor);
@danger-color: dbColor(DangerColor);
@small: dbSize(small);
@large: dbSize(large);
/* ... additional variables ... */

/* === STEP 2: Expose as custom CSS properties === */
:root {
    color-scheme: light dark;

    &:has(body[mode="light"]) { color-scheme: light; }
    &:has(body[mode="dark"])  { color-scheme: dark; }

    --header-color: @header-color;
    --menu-color: @menu-color;
    --bg-color: @bg-color;
    --primary-color: @primary-color;
    --danger-color: @danger-color;
}

Product-level example — adding your own brand colors:

LessCss
/* my-product/css/theme.less */

/* Add DB-mapped Less variables */
@brand-accent: dbColor(BrandAccent);
@brand-bg: dbColor(BrandBg);
@brand-text: dbColor(BrandText);

/* Expose brand CSS properties */
:root {
    --brand-accent: @brand-accent;
    --brand-bg: @brand-bg;
    --brand-text: @brand-text;
    --brand-radius: 12px;
    --brand-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
}

Only two block types allowed

theme.less only supports two kinds of blocks: (1) @variable: dbColor()/dbSize() definitions, and (2) the :root { --*: @variable; } block. Don't add mixins, CSS rules, or other constructs — those belong in separate .less files.

New variables in the database

dbColor(Name) and dbSize(Name) are replaced at runtime with values from the configuration database. If you introduce new keys, register them in the Skins_Variables table from the application's Skins section, or directly in the database. Remember to include these variables in the project's scripts ({Name}.Conf.Database) so they aren't lost in other environments.

docs.title: favicon.ico — Browser Tab Icon
docs.text:
Resolution: First-found-wins.

Level Path Installation custom/favicon.ico Product {product}/favicon.ico Flexygo favicon.ico

Place an .ico file at the desired level. The standard sizes (16×16, 32×32, 48×48) are recommended.

docs.title: account.css — Generic Account Page Styles
docs.text:
Resolution: The 3 levels are emitted as <link> tags in order: Flexygo → Product → Installation. The browser's cascade lets later rules override earlier ones.

Level Path Installation custom/css/views/account/account.css Product {product}/css/views/account/account.css Flexygo css/views/account/account.css

Product-level branding example:

CSS
/* my-product/css/views/account/account.css */

/* Replace the product logo */
:root {
    --product-logo: url(my-product-logo.svg);
    --product-background: url(my-product-background.svg);
}

/* Style the account card */
.account-card {
    border-radius: 16px;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(233, 69, 96, 0.15);
}

/* Style the login button */
.account-card .account-button {
    background-color: var(--brand-accent, #e94560);
    color: #fff;
    font-weight: 600;
    border-radius: 8px;
    transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
}

.account-card .account-button:hover {
    background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand-accent, #e94560) 80%, black);
}

/* Focus ring on inputs */
.account-card-body .cell:focus-within {
    outline-color: var(--brand-accent, #e94560);
}

/* Page background */
body {
    background-color: #0f0f1a;
    background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a1a2e 0%, #16213e 100%);
}

Available CSS variables (defined in Flexygo's account.css):

Property Purpose --product-logo Logo image in the icon header --product-background Background image behind the login card --card-color Account card background --border-card-color Card border color --bg-color Page background color --bg-color-light Input field background --bg-color-dark Button background --bg-color-dark-2 Button hover background --txt-color Text color --primary-color Focus ring, loading bar, accents --danger-color Validation error color --outstanding-color Scrollbar, highlights --success-color Success indicators --account-card-height Card height (default: 600px) --account-card-width Card width (default: 440px) --input-height Input/button height (default: 50px) --input-margin Horizontal padding on inputs --font-size-1 Large text (3em) --font-size-2 Normal text (1em) --font-size-3 Small text (0.9em) --placeholder-color Placeholder text --outline-size Focus ring thickness --login-font Font family for account pages

docs.title: account.js — Generic Account Page Scripts
docs.text:
Resolution: Same as account.css — the 3 levels are emitted in source order.

Level Path Installation custom/js/views/account/account.js Product {product}/js/views/account/account.js Flexygo js/views/account/account.js

Idempotent scripts

Override scripts must be idempotent: they run alongside the native script, not in its place. Use event listeners instead of replacing global functions.

docs.title: Page-Specific CSS and JS
docs.text:
Each Account page supports its own CSS and JS overrides. The pattern is identical to account.css/account.js.

Page CSS path JS path Login css/views/account/login/login.css js/views/account/login/login.js Register css/views/account/register/register.css js/views/account/register/register.js Forgot password css/views/account/forgot/forgot.css js/views/account/forgot/forgot.js MFA css/views/account/authentication/authentication.css js/views/account/authentication/authentication.js Manage password css/views/account/manage-password/manage-password.css js/views/account/manage-password/manage-password.js

All of them follow the same {level}/{path} structure. Example for product-level login CSS:

Text Only
wwwroot/my-product/css/views/account/login/login.css

docs.title: Quick Reference: All Supported Paths
docs.text:
Text Only
{level}/manifest.json
{level}/favicon.ico
{level}/css/theme.less
{level}/css/views/account/account.css
{level}/css/views/account/login/login.css
{level}/css/views/account/register/register.css
{level}/css/views/account/forgot/forgot.css
{level}/css/views/account/authentication/authentication.css
{level}/css/views/account/manage-password/manage-password.css
{level}/js/views/account/account.js
{level}/js/views/account/login/login.js
{level}/js/views/account/register/register.js
{level}/js/views/account/forgot/forgot.js
{level}/js/views/account/authentication/authentication.js
{level}/js/views/account/manage-password/manage-password.js

Where {level} is:

  • Installation: custom (e.g. custom/favicon.ico, custom/css/views/account/account.css)
  • Product: the name of your product folder (e.g. my-product/favicon.ico, my-product/css/views/account/account.css)
  • Flexygo: empty / root (e.g. favicon.ico, css/views/account/account.css)

docs.title: Limitations and Degradation Behavior
docs.text:
• Product folder detection runs only once at startup. The product folder is identified by the presence of the marker file css/theme.less in a subdirectory of wwwroot. If no folder contains that file, the system degrades to a 2-level chain (Installation → Flexygo).
  • Missing css/theme.less in your product folder causes the entire folder to be ignored — not just the theme, but also the views' CSS/JS, favicon.ico, and manifest.json at the product level. It is not part of the template: create it (even if empty) when you start customizing.
  • Multiple product folders (several subdirectories with css/theme.less) generate a warning in the log; only the first folder found is used.
  • Missing files at any level are silently skipped — only the files that exist are emitted.
  • manifest.json and favicon.ico use the first-found-wins pattern; Flexygo's native fallback is always available.
  • View overrides (.cshtml files) are not supported in the current version. CSS/JS overrides cover most customization needs.
  • Hot reload of customization files is not supported; an application restart is required after deploying new assets.

docs.title: Create an addon
docs.text: An addon is an extension installed on top of an already-deployed Flexygo product, with its own version cycle independent of the product (see Packaging addons). You can create a new addon directly from the Flexygo Installer, without having to use the command-line template (dotnet new flexygoaddon).

docs.title: 1. Create the addon from the Installer
docs.text:
In the Installer, go to the Development section and select Create addon.

On the Create addon screen, fill in:

  • Product folder: the root folder of the product on which the addon will be created.
    • If the folder already contains a product, the installer adds the addon to that existing product.
    • If the folder is empty, the installer first creates the product and then the addon, all in a single pass.
  • Addon name: the addon's identifier (for example, AddonFlexy). It must be different from the product name, use only letters, numbers and underscores, and cannot start with a number. This identifier is what's always used to refer to the addon — for example, in the Backend's custom/AddonName path, or when activating it during development (see below).

Click Create Addon. The installer automatically generates all the necessary projects (database configuration, data model, processes), already wired together and to the product's template — there's no need to create or configure them by hand.

Where the addon's files go

When an addon is installed, it's placed at the custom/{AddonName} path. So any file that's part of the addon (JS, CSS, DLL, etc.) must be placed inside that same folder, and the paths used in the project must reference it.

Since the product is now split into Frontend and Backend, that custom/{AddonName} folder exists in both, depending on the type of file:

  • Backend: this is where the addon's DLLs go.
  • Frontend: this is where the addon's CSS, JS and other assets go.

docs.title: 2. Check the Processes project's output path
docs.text:
The generated {AddonName}.Processes project already includes, by default, an output path (OutputPath) that points to the product's Backend custom/{AddonName} folder, so that all of the addon's DLLs end up together in that folder:

XML
<!-- All the addon's DLLs in a single custom/<Addon>/dll folder -->
<OutputPath>..\..\{Product}.Backend\custom\{AddonName}\dll\</OutputPath>

Check that this path actually points to custom/{AddonName} inside your product's Backend project — especially if the product or addon name don't match what the default template generated, or if you move the addon to a different folder.

docs.title: 3. Develop the addon
docs.text: The rest of the setup (database projects, project references) is handled automatically by the installer. The only thing left for you to do is develop the addon itself.

docs.title: Activate Addon mode
docs.text:
To develop the addon, first select the origin you want to work on and choose the Addon option.

Then enter the Origin Addon Id (your addon's identifier, for example AddonFlexy) and click Activate.

With Addon mode active, you can develop as usual: everything you create or modify will be recorded under your addon's origin.

docs.title: Generate the addon's scripts
docs.text:
Once development is complete, generate the addon's database scripts by clicking the database icon in the top bar, visible while Addon mode is active (the ADDON MODE indicator).

With the scripts generated, continue with Packaging the addon as a NuGet to prepare the addon's manifest and .nuspec.

docs.title: 4. Packaging the addon as a NuGet
module.json file
docs.text:
Inside your addon's config folder you'll find the module.json file, where the actions to perform when installing the addon are defined.

Its definition is the same as always, with one new addition: a resource's scope can now also be backend, which is where the addon's DLLs go.

General

Attribute Example Description name "AddonFlexy" Our addon's identifier. description "Description." Brief description of the addon's purpose or functionality. type "Flexygo" Currently always Flexygo. flexygoVersionMin "10.0.0" Minimum Flexygo version required to install the addon. flexygoVersionMax "10.9.0" Maximum Flexygo version the addon can be installed on. It is optional: if the installed version is higher, the installation is rejected. productVersionMin "4.0.0.6" Minimum product version required to install the addon. productVersionMax "8.4.0.6" Maximum product version required to install the addon. resources [ ... ] List of resources included in the addon and how they should be handled. postProcess [ ... ] List of processes that will run after installing the addon.

resources

Attribute Example Description path "content/sql/AddonFlexy.Data.Database.dacpac" Path of the resource within the NuGet package. targetConnectionString "DataConnectionString" Name of the connection string the resource will be applied to (only if scope is database). uninstallPrefix "AddonFlexy_" Prefix used to identify and remove objects (tables, views, stored procedures, functions) when uninstalling the addon. scope "database" / "backend" / "frontend" Defines the resource's installation scope:• database: applies a .dacpac file to the database.• backend: copies the addon's DLL to the custom/{AddonName} folder of the Backend.• frontend: copies the files to the client environment (JS, CSS, images, etc.).

postProcess

Attribute Example Description processName "pPostNuget" Name of the process (defined in Flexygo) that will run once the addon's installation finishes. params { "Param1": true, "Param2": "2025-09-25", ... } Process parameters defined in Flexygo. order 0 Execution order of the processes.

docs.title: .nuspec file
docs.text:
Your addon's project already includes an automatically generated .nuspec file with the files and paths needed for packaging: the module.json manifest, the databases' .dacpac files, the Backend DLL and, if your addon ships static assets, the Frontend section (commented out by default).
