Step What it does Stop the application Stops the Frontend and the Backend that were started. It always runs, also when an earlier step failed, so the application is not left running on the agent.

The step names above describe each step; in TeamCity the template names them in Spanish, for example «Restaurar paquetes NuGet» or «Detener aplicación».

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
The configuration collects:

  • publish\<ProductName>.v<build number>.zip, the published product;
  • publish\DockerCompose<build number>.zip, to deploy it with Docker;
  • <ProductName>.InterfaceTest\bin\Debug\net9.0\tracing, the interface tests' traces, to see what happened when one fails.

They are downloaded from each build's Artifacts tab.

docs.title: Build number and trigger
docs.text:
• Build number: 1.0.%build.counter%.1. It is the version of everything the build produces: the assemblies, the dacpacs and the NuGets.
  • Trigger: VCS. Every push to the ProductBranch branch starts a build.

docs.title: Build features
docs.text: Feature What it does AssemblyInfo patcher Sets the build number as the assemblies' version. File content replacer on **/*.sqlproj Sets <DacVersion> to the build number, so the dacpacs carry the same version as the rest. Performance monitor Records the agent's CPU, memory and disk use during the build.

docs.title: What the agent needs
docs.text:
• The .NET 9 SDK, to build and publish, and the .NET 6 SDK, for the test steps.
  • Node.js, for the Frontend's TypeScript.
  • sqlpackage, to publish the databases.
  • A SQL Server where the test databases are created.
  • NuGet.CommandLine 6.12.2, to generate the NuGets.

docs.title: GitHub Actions and GitLab CI
docs.text:
The product template ships the pipelines for GitHub Actions and for GitLab CI, ready but disabled. Each has two workflows: one generates the product's NuGets and the other its Docker images. Both tools do the same, with the same version.

The steps follow the same order as the TeamCity template: restore, publish, databases, tests and NuGets; these pipelines add the release and the Docker images. The differences are in Differences from TeamCity. For the general idea of the pipeline, see the overview.

Project names

The examples use <ProductName> as the product's name: the prefix of the solution's projects (<ProductName>.Frontend, <ProductName>.Backend, <ProductName>.Conf.Database, <ProductName>.Data.Database…). In your product, the template has already replaced it.

docs.title: Enabling them
docs.text:
The files come with the .disabled extension so a new product does not start builds until you decide. To enable them, remove that extension:

Tool Files What to rename GitHub Actions .github/workflows/<ProductName>-nugets.yml.disabled and <ProductName>-docker.yml.disabled Remove .disabled from both, or only from the one you want. GitLab CI .gitlab-ci.yml.disabled, which includes .gitlab/workflows/<ProductName>-nugets.yml and <ProductName>-docker.yml Remove .disabled from .gitlab-ci.yml. To keep only one of the two workflows, remove its include line.

docs.title: When they run
docs.text:
• GitHub Actions: on every push to any branch, on every v* tag and by hand (Run workflow).
  • GitLab CI: on every pipeline of the project, for any branch.

What gets published depends on the branch:

Branch NuGets Release Publishes the NuGets Publishes the images main or master Yes Yes Yes Yes develop Yes Yes No No Any other Yes No No No

On every branch, the NuGets and the images are kept as artifacts of the run.

docs.title: The version
docs.text:
The version comes from <ProductName>-version.json, which holds the major and the minor:

JSON
{
  "major": 1,
  "minor": 0
}

The pipeline works out the rest by counting commits since the last one that touched that file:

Branch Package version Example main or master Major.Minor.0.N, with N = commits since the last version change + 1 1.0.0.7 develop Major.Minor.N.1-beta, with N = commits since the last version change 1.0.23.1-beta Any other Major.Minor.N.1-alpha.K, with N = the commits develop had where the branch left it and K = the branch's own commits 1.0.23.1-alpha.4

To raise the version, change the major or the minor in the file: the counter starts again by itself. The assemblies, the dacpacs' DacVersion, the NuGets and the images carry the same number; the assemblies, without the -beta or -alpha suffix.

Both workflows need the full git history to count: GitHub fetches it with fetch-depth: 0 and GitLab with GIT_DEPTH: "0".

docs.title: The steps
docs.text: The NuGets workflow runs steps 1 to 6; the images one, step 7.

docs.title: 1. Restore
docs.text:
dotnet restore <ProductName>.sln, with the sources in the product's nuget.config: nuget.org and Flexygo's two feeds, the stable and the beta one.

DevExpress packages

The template's nuget.config does not include the DevExpress feed. If your product needs its packages, add its source before restoring, with the key kept as a secret (for example DEVEXPRESS_API), never written in the file.

docs.title: 2. Publish
docs.text:
dotnet publish in Release of the Frontend and the Backend to publish/<ProductName>/, with the version, the file version and the informational version (the package's plus the commit). It produces the DLLs the NuGets package.

Node.js

The Frontend compiles TypeScript with node. GitHub's runners (ubuntu-latest) already have it; the GitLab workflow installs it in its before_script. Without it, publishing the Frontend fails with MSB6003.

docs.title: 3. Databases
docs.text: dotnet build of <ProductName>.Conf.Database.sqlproj and <ProductName>.Data.Database.sqlproj in Release, with -p:NetCoreBuild=true and /p:DacVersion=<version>. It produces the dacpacs the database NuGets package.

docs.title: 4. Tests
docs.text: These pipelines run no tests: they go from the databases straight to the NuGets. See Tests.

docs.title: 5. NuGets
docs.text:
One dotnet pack of tools/pack.csproj per product .nuspec, to publish/nuget: Frontend, Library, Backend, Conf.Database and Data.Database. tools/pack.csproj builds nothing: it only exists because dotnet pack needs a project.

Bash
dotnet pack tools/pack.csproj -o publish/nuget -p:NuspecProperties="version=<version>" \
  -p:NuspecFile=$PWD/<ProductName>.Frontend/<ProductName>.Frontend.nuspec \
  -p:NuspecBasePath=$PWD/<ProductName>.Frontend

The .nupkg files are kept as an artifact of the run on every branch.

docs.title: 6. Release and publishing
docs.text:
On main, master and develop a v<version> release is created:

  • GitHub: with generated notes and the .nupkg files attached.
  • GitLab: with glab release create. If the release already exists, for example when the pipeline is run again, it is updated instead of failing.

Then the NuGets are published, only on main or master:

  • GitHub: to the repository owner's GitHub Packages.
  • GitLab: to the project's Package Registry.

If the package already exists with that version, it is skipped.

docs.title: 7. Docker images
docs.text:
It builds three images with the same version as the NuGets: frontend, backend and db, the database with both catalogues. Each one:

  1. is built with its version's tag; the db one also gets that version as DAC_VERSION, so the backend does not update the schema on the first start;
  2. is exported with docker save to publish/docker/<ProductName>-<image>-<version>.tar.gz and kept as an artifact of the run;
  3. on main or master, is pushed to the registry with its version and with latest: GHCR (ghcr.io/<owner>/…) on GitHub and the project's Container Registry on GitLab.

On GitLab, if the instance does not have the Container Registry enabled, the push is skipped and the rest carries on. This workflow creates no release: the NuGets one already does.

To build the same images on your computer: pwsh tools/build-docker-images.ps1.

docs.title: Differences from TeamCity
docs.text: GitHub Actions and GitLab CI TeamCity Enabling .disabled files in the product; enabled by removing the extension Configuration created from the Template flexygo products core template Version <ProductName>-version.json and the branch: Major.Minor.0.N, -beta or -alpha.K 1.0.%build.counter%.1 Restore The sources in the product's nuget.config Four sources, DevExpress included Databases Only built Built and published to test databases with sqlpackage Tests None Starts the application and runs the core's, the product's and the interface tests NuGets dotnet pack of tools/pack.csproj per .nuspec NuGet Pack with NuGet.CommandLine 6.12.2 Release Yes, on main, master and develop No Docker images Frontend, backend and db, published on main or master Not built

docs.title: Secrets and variables
docs.text:
No secret has to be set up to publish:

  • GitHub uses GITHUB_TOKEN, which the run creates itself, with the packages: write permission.
  • GitLab uses CI_JOB_TOKEN, which is also generated by itself.

What does have to be prepared:

  • GitLab: enable the Package Registry and, for the images, the Container Registry under Settings › General › Visibility, project features, permissions. The images workflow needs a docker executor in privileged mode, because it uses the docker:dind service.
  • The keys you add, such as DevExpress's: as a secret on GitHub, which masks it by itself, or as a Masked variable on GitLab. A normal variable shows as it is in the log.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
These pipelines do not run tests today: they build, pack and publish. The unit tests are run on your computer against the product's database image:

PowerShell
pwsh tools/run-tests-with-db.ps1 -Version 1.0.1.1

The script starts the database image, waits for it to answer, points the tests at it, runs them and cleans everything up at the end, also when they fail. The container's sa password is taken from the SQL_PASSWORD environment variable, and SQL_PORT changes the port if 1433 is already taken by a SQL Server on your computer. It needs Docker.

pwsh tools/dev-pipeline.ps1 chains restore, publish, the database image, the tests and packing locally, without publishing anything.

On Windows without PowerShell 7, replace pwsh with powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File.

docs.title: Troubleshooting: Deployment
docs.text: Diagnostic guide for the most common problems when configuring and starting up Flexygo.

docs.title: The Frontend cannot connect to the Backend
docs.text:
Symptom: The Frontend application loads but shows no data. API requests return network errors (Failed to fetch, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED) or CORS errors.

Cause: The backend URL configured in the Frontend's appsettings.json is incorrect, points to a host that is not reachable, or is missing the protocol (http://).

Solution:

  1. Open the Frontend's conf\appsettings.json in the installation directory.
  2. Locate the BackendEndpoint key and verify that it points to the correct Backend URL, ending in /api/backend/: JSON
    {
  "BackendEndpoint": "http://localhost:7110/api/backend/"
}
  3. Make sure the URL includes the protocol (http:// or https://) and the virtual path, if any. If the Frontend and the Backend are on the same server, use a local address (localhost), not the public domain.
  4. If you use HTTPS, verify that the SSL certificate is valid and trusted.
  5. Restart the Frontend's application pool in IIS.

Configuration wizard

You can use the built-in configuration wizard to set the backend URL without manually editing appsettings.json. See the deployment configuration guide.

docs.title: The Backend does not start: database error
docs.text:
Symptom: The Backend returns HTTP 500 on every request. The IIS logs or Event Viewer show messages such as Cannot open database, Login failed for user, or A network-related error occurred.

Cause: The SQL Server connection string in the Backend's appsettings.json is incorrect: the server name is misspelled, the credentials are wrong, or the database does not exist.

Solution:

  1. Open the Backend's conf\appsettings.json in the installation directory.
  2. Locate the ConnectionStrings.ConfConnectionString (configuration database) and ConnectionStrings.DataConnectionString (data database) keys and check each part: JSON
    {
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "ConfConnectionString": "Data Source=SERVER_NAME;Initial Catalog=CONF_DATABASE;User ID=USER;Password=PASSWORD;Encrypt=False;Trust Server Certificate=True",
    "DataConnectionString": "Data Source=SERVER_NAME;Initial Catalog=DATA_DATABASE;User ID=USER;Password=PASSWORD;Encrypt=False;Trust Server Certificate=True"
  }
}
    In IIS and in a production container the connection strings are encrypted (they start with enc:v1:). To read or change them, decrypt them with Flexygo.Backend.exe config decrypt, edit them and restart; they are encrypted again on startup. See How do I decrypt and re-encrypt the configuration? and Encrypted appsettings.
  3. Check that you can connect with those credentials from SQL Server Management Studio or sqlcmd.
  4. If you use Windows authentication, make sure the application pool account has access to the database.
  5. Restart the Backend's application pool.

docs.title: Changes to appsettings.json have no effect
docs.text:
Symptom: appsettings.json is edited but the application keeps behaving the same way. The changes are not reflected.

Cause: The application has the file cached in memory. IIS does not automatically detect the change in every environment.

Solution:

  1. In IIS, select the corresponding application pool.
  2. Right-click → Recycle.
  3. If the problem persists, stop and restart the application pool.

docs.title: Infinite redirect loop behind a reverse proxy
docs.text:
Symptom: The application never loads and the browser keeps redirecting. Inspecting the request shows a 307 response whose location header is identical to the requested URL. No error appears anywhere: not in the Event Viewer, not in the application logs, not in the IIS logs.

Cause: There is a reverse proxy in front (nginx, ARR, a load balancer) that terminates TLS and hands the request to Flexygo over http without forwarding the X-Forwarded-Proto header. The application then believes the request is insecure and redirects to https; the proxy hands it over again via http and the cycle never ends. A 307 is a valid response, which is why it is not logged anywhere.

Solution:

  1. Configure the proxy to forward the original scheme. In nginx, inside the location block: Nginx Configuration File
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  2. Reload the proxy and test again.
  3. If you cannot change the proxy right away, disable the redirection in the Frontend's appsettings.json and recycle the application pool: JSON
    {
  "HttpsRedirection": false
}

Full configuration

The requirements for a deployment with a proxy in front are in Deployment behind a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Access auditing always records the same IP
docs.text:
Symptom: All sign-ins appear with the same IP address, or the per-user IP restrictions block people they should not.

Cause: There is a reverse proxy in front and the application sees its address instead of the client's. Flexygo only accepts the forwarded IP when the request comes from a declared proxy.

Solution:

  1. Find out which address the proxy uses to open the connection to the server. In IIS it is the c-ip field of the site log, under C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles.
  2. Declare it in the appsettings.json of both Frontend and Backend: JSON
    {
  "ForwardedHeaders": {
    "KnownProxies": [ "192.168.1.10" ]
  }
}
  3. Check that the proxy forwards the X-Forwarded-For header.
  4. Recycle the application pools.

Proxy on the same machine

If the proxy runs on the same server as Flexygo, nothing needs to be declared: local addresses are accepted by default.

docs.title: VS Code does not recognize the project (IntelliSense does not work)
docs.text:
Symptom: VS Code shows reference errors in .cs files. IntelliSense offers no suggestions or shows "Unable to resolve...". The C# Dev Kit extension shows warnings in the status bar.

Most common cause A: The required .NET SDK is not installed, or the version is incorrect.

Most common cause B: VS Code was opened in a parent directory instead of the root directory of the project/.sln solution.

Solution A — Check the SDK:

Bash
dotnet --version
dotnet --list-sdks

The Flexygo project requires .NET 9 for the backend/frontend. The MCP server requires .NET 10. If either is missing, download it from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download.

Solution B — Open the correct directory:

  1. In VS Code, use File → Open Folder and select the folder that contains your solution's .sln file.
  2. Alternatively, open the solution directly from Visual Studio 2022.
  3. Reload the window with Ctrl+Shift+P → Developer: Reload Window.

Visual Studio 2022

To work with database projects (.sqlproj), Visual Studio 2022 is required. VS 2026 Insiders does not support SDK-style database projects. See the product requirements.

docs.title: Docker: the container does not start or keeps restarting in a loop
docs.text:
Symptom: When running docker compose up, one or more containers enter the Restarting state. The logs show connection errors or undefined environment variables.

Most common cause: Environment variables not defined in the .env file, or an incorrect connection string.

Solution:

  1. Check the container logs: Bash
    docker compose logs flx-backend
  2. Check that the .env file exists next to docker-compose.yml and defines all the required variables (at minimum SQL_PASSWORD and FRONTEND_PORT/BACKEND_PORT).
  3. Make sure the ports are not already in use by another process: Bash
    netstat -ano | findstr "8080"

docs.title: Troubleshooting: MCP
docs.text: Diagnostic guide for the most common problems with the flexygo-mcp server in Claude Code.

docs.title: Claude Code cannot find the server
docs.text:
Symptom: When you type /mcp, the flexygo server does not show, or it shows with an error. The agent uses no Flexygo tool.

Cause A: Claude Code is not open in the project's root folder, which is where .mcp.json lives.

Cause B: The project's server has not been approved.

Cause C: The flexygo-mcp tool is not installed (see the next section).

Solution:

  1. Open Claude Code in the project's root folder, the one that holds .mcp.json and the .claude folder.
  2. Check that .mcp.json has the flexygo entry with "command": "flexygo-mcp". See the server configuration.
  3. If Claude Code asked whether to use the project's server and you said no, turn it on from /mcp.
  4. Open a new chat.

docs.title: flexygo-mcp is not recognized as a command
docs.text:
Symptom: When you run flexygo-mcp in the terminal you get the error:

Text Only
'flexygo-mcp' is not recognized as an internal or external command
or in PowerShell: Text Only
The term 'flexygo-mcp' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function...

Cause A: The .NET 10 SDK is not installed.

Cause B: The flexygo-mcp global tool is not installed, or the installation failed.

Cause C: The .NET global tools directory is not in the system PATH.

Solution:

  1. Check that the .NET 10 SDK is installed:

    Bash
    dotnet --list-sdks
    If no 10.x.x version shows, download it from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download.

  2. Check whether the tool is already installed:

    Bash
    dotnet tool list -g
    Look for flexygo-mcp in the list.

  3. If it is not there, install it manually:

    Bash
    dotnet tool install -g flexygo-mcp

  4. If the command is still not recognized, add the .NET tools directory to the PATH:

  5. Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.dotnet\tools
  6. Linux/macOS: ~/.dotnet/tools

Automatic installation

When you create a new product from the Installer, flexygo-mcp is installed automatically. If the error happens after a manual installation, follow the steps above. See the MCP prerequisites.

docs.title: The /flx-* commands do not show
docs.text:
Symptom: The server is connected, but typing /flx- shows no command.

Cause: The server installs the commands in the project when it starts, and the chat was opened before that.

Solution: Open a new chat in the project. If they still do not show, ask the agent to sync the Flexygo commands and open a chat again.

docs.title: The tools fail with database errors
docs.text:
Symptom: The tools show, but all of them return connection errors or say there are no connection strings.

Cause A: The Backend's appsettings has no ConfConnectionString and DataConnectionString.

Cause B: The server reads another appsettings file. The ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT variable in .mcp.json decides which: with Development, appsettings.Development.json.

Solution: Type /flx-setup: it checks which databases exist, publishes the missing ones and writes the connection strings. See The databases.

docs.title: What the agent just created does not show in the application
docs.text:
Symptom: The agent created an object or changed a property, but the application does not show it, a list answers with a 500 error, or The given key was not present in the dictionary appears.

Cause: The running application keeps the object definitions in memory and does not read them again. What the agent writes is in the database, but the application does not see it yet. It is not a configuration error.

Solution:

  1. The first time, the agent asks for your Flexygo password to reload the cache. It is kept in memory only, for that session, and from then on the cache reloads by itself after each change.
  2. If the Backend is on another computer, the agent tells you its name and asks before sending your credentials to it. See Security checks.
  3. If you would rather not give the password, use the Reload Cache button in the users list, or restart the Backend.
  4. If you had the screen open in the browser, load it again.

docs.title: The Flexygo panel does not show
docs.text:
Symptom: You see neither the band above the chat nor the side pane.

Cause A: The one-time step flexygo-mcp --enable-panel has not been run on this computer.

Cause B: The chat was opened before turning it on: the panel shows when you open a new chat or session.

Cause C: The project has the panel turned off in its .claude/settings.json.

Cause D: You are using Claude Code with no interface (claude -p), where there is no panel.

Solution: See How to turn on the panel and the board.

docs.title: After an update, the agent does not see what is new
docs.text:
Symptom: You updated the server with dotnet tool update -g flexygo-mcp, but the agent does not use the new tools or parameters.

Cause: A chat already under way keeps the list of tools it received when it started.

Solution: Open a new chat.

docs.title: Try it: an AI assistant working with your application (MCP) 10.0+
Try it: an AI assistant working with your application (MCP) 10.0+
docs.text:
In about fifteen minutes you will have Claude (or another assistant) connected to a Flexygo application with your user: you will ask it about your data in plain language —"how many orders are there by status?", "show me customer 1", "build me a sales dashboard"— and it will answer by reading the application with your permissions, not one more. At the end you will see every question logged in the application itself and you will know how to cut the connection.

This page is the short path to try it. What each piece does, all the settings and the security are in the reference: AI assistants (MCP).

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: A version 10 Flexygo application A local development installation is fine. Log in with an administrator user. An object with data Any one you already have (orders, customers, incidents…). In the examples on this page it is an Order object with its status and its total. An assistant that speaks MCP The quickest way to try it locally is Claude Code. Claude (web or desktop) and ChatGPT also work, but they need to reach the application over the internet with HTTPS (step 5).

docs.title: 1. Turn on the web API and MCP
docs.text:
In the control panel, Security → WebAPI area, turn on Enable WebAPI and Enable MCP. They are off by default.

Check: your profile menu shows Connect an assistant and Connected assistants. If they do not appear, log out and back in.

docs.title: 2. Give yourself permission to connect an assistant
docs.text:
On the same screen, Authorized People panel, Authorized Roles tab: tick the robot column for your role (for example Admins). It is a permission separate from the web API one (the eye): for this test you do not need the eye.

Check: Connect an assistant opens a page with your application's address to copy. If it says you do not have permission, the robot is missing from your role (or from your user, Authorized Users tab).

docs.title: 3. Show the assistant what it can use
docs.text:
In the Authorized Data panel, Authorized Objects tab, tick the eye (view a record) and the list (view the collection) on your object. If you want it to be able to modify too, tick create or edit; for a first test reading is enough.

What you do not tick does not exist for the assistant. This is how you decide which part of the application is within the AI's reach.

docs.title: 4. Explain what your application is
docs.text:
The assistant is only as accurate as the descriptions are good. For the test, two minutes:

  • Settings → ApplicationDescription: what the application is and your business vocabulary. For example: "Sales management: orders (statuses Draft, Confirmed, Shipped, Invoiced, Cancelled) and customers. "Revenue" is the sum of the Total of non-cancelled orders."
  • The object's AI description (AI description, on the object's form) and, on coded fields, their Description in API ("Order status: DRAFT, CONFIRMED, SHIPPED, INVOICED or CANCELLED").

It works without this too, but the assistant guesses what your columns mean. The full list of what it reads, with its table and column, and a prompt for an AI to propose it to you from your configuration database, is in What to fill in.

docs.title: 5. Connect the assistant
docs.text:
Open Connect an assistant and copy the address (your application's address ending in /mcp).

Claude Code (local)Claude web or desktopOthers (ChatGPT, Gemini…) Bash
claude mcp add --transport http miapp http://localhost:7111/mcp

Replace the address with the one you copied. Inside Claude Code, type /mcp, choose miapp and press Authenticate: the browser opens.

Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, with a name and the address. It needs the application to be visible from the internet with HTTPS (the one connecting is Anthropic's servers): in a local test, a tunnel (ngrok or similar) to the Frontend. See Reverse proxy.

In their connectors, the same address. Any MCP client with streamable HTTP and OAuth works: it registers itself when connecting.

In the browser you log in with your usual user and see the consent page: who is asking, with which user and what is granted. Press Allow (you can untick Modify data so that it only reads).

Check: the assistant says it is connected (in Claude Code, /mcp shows it as connected).

docs.title: 6. Ask it
docs.text:
Some questions to see each thing, with your names instead of the ones in the example:

Question What should happen "What is in this application?" It reads the catalog and summarizes your objects with your descriptions. If it only sees the object you ticked in step 3, security works. "How many orders are there by status?" It gives you a count by status. Compare it with the list in the application: it must match. "How much have we invoiced?" It sums the Total of the non-cancelled ones, if you explained it in step 4. "Show me order 1" The form with its fields and a link to open it in the application. "Build me a sales dashboard" Figures, breakdowns and a table. In Claude web or desktop it appears as an interactive dashboard; in the others, as text and tables. "Change the status of order 1 to Confirmed" If you did not tick edit in step 3, or you unticked Modify data when connecting, it refuses and tells you why.

docs.title: 7. See what happened
docs.text:
In the control panel, Environment area:

  • MCP usage: calls per day (answered and rejected), per tool and per person, and the reason for each rejection.
  • MCP sessions: your live connection, with whom, since when and what it can do.

docs.title: 8. Cut the connection
docs.text:
Profile menu → Connected assistants → Revoke on the row. The assistant's next question gets a refusal. To come back, connect again (step 5).

And if you turn off Enable MCP (step 1), /mcp stops existing for everyone immediately.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text:
What you see Why What to do The assistant does not connect and the address returns 404 Enable MCP (or Enable WebAPI) is off Step 1 The connect page or the consent page says you do not have permission The robot is missing from your role or your user Step 2 The assistant says the object does not exist It is not ticked in Authorized Data Step 3 It answers, but mixes up fields or statuses Descriptions are missing Step 4 Claude web or desktop does not reach the application It is not accessible from the internet with HTTPS Step 5: tunnel or reverse proxy Writes are rejected No edit/create in Authorized Data, or Modify data unticked when connecting This is expected: tick it and reconnect if you want to try them The assistant does not appear as approved in MCP assistants MCP_RequireApprovedClients is on Approve it in MCP assistants

For everything else —call limits, prompts, auditing, best practices— see the reference: AI assistants (MCP).

docs.title: AI assistants connected to the application (MCP) 10.0+
AI assistants connected to the application (MCP) 10.0+
docs.text:
New in version 10.0

From the profile menu, you can connect an assistant and choose whether it can only read data or also make changes. Connected assistants lets you review and disconnect connections. An administrator enables Enable WebAPI and Enable MCP in Administration > Security > WebAPI, and assigns the MCP permission to the authorized users or roles. The assistant's tools indicate whether they read data, make changes, or allow retries.

Processes that take more than ten minutes are also supported. Assistant registration uses its metadata to avoid duplicates and keeps dynamic client registration available.

Since version 10, every Flexygo application is also an MCP server: an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude Code or any other client that speaks the Model Context Protocol) connects to the application with the usual user and sees and does exactly what that user can see and do, nothing more. Nothing has to be programmed in the application: the assistant reads the objects, views, processes and reports that already exist, with their descriptions, and works with them in the user's language.

Want to try it in fifteen minutes? Try it: an AI assistant working with your application.

This is not the builder's MCP server

The MCP section of this documentation describes the server that builds applications from Claude Code. This page describes the opposite: the already built application, exposed to its users' assistants.

flowchart LR
  A[Assistant\nClaude, ChatGPT, Gemini…] -- OAuth 2.1 + MCP --> F[Frontend\n/mcp]
  F --> B[Backend]
  B --> S[(User security\nroles, objects, views, processes)]
  S --> D[(Application data)]

docs.title: 1. What an assistant can do
docs.text:
Everything goes through the security of the user who connected: their roles, the objects and views they can see, the processes they can run and what the application exposes in its web API. An object the role cannot see does not exist for the assistant; a write the role cannot perform is rejected with a sentence in the user's language.

What the person asks What the assistant does With what "What is in this application?" Reads the catalog: objects, views and processes with the descriptions the team wrote, and the business vocabulary (what "overdue", "not invoiced"… mean). flexygo_catalog, flexygo_schema "Search for García" / "What do we have on Acme?" Searches the text across all objects with the application's global search (the fields and lookups the team configured in each generic search), grouped by object and with the link to each record. It is the first thing it does when the person names someone or something rather than the object. flexygo_search "Give me García's overdue invoices" List with field filters, paging and sorting; lookup fields come with their text (_flxtext), not just the id. flexygo_list "Show me order 1020" The full record with its children (lines, deliveries…) and the link to open it in the application. flexygo_get "How much have we invoiced this month by payment method?" Totals, counts, averages and breakdowns by a field, or by period (day, week, month). If there is a view that already calculates it, it uses it first. flexygo_measure "Build me a sales dashboard" A dashboard with figures, breakdowns, series and tables; in clients that render MCP Apps (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) it appears as an interactive widget with click-through to the list, CSV export and "Open in Flexygo". flexygo_dashboard "Download the invoice as a PDF" The object's report (DevExpress or Crystal) as PDF or Excel, and the link to the application's viewer. flexygo_report "Mark invoice 3 as paid" Runs the object's process with its parameters; if any is missing, it asks for it. flexygo_exec "Change customer 5's phone number" / "Create a delivery for order 10" Modifies or creates records, only in the objects the web API exposes for editing or creating. flexygo_update, flexygo_create

In addition, the assistant receives:

  • Resources: the application description (flexygo://application), each object's schema (flexygo://{objeto}/schema) and any record (flexygo://{objeto}/{id}).
  • Prompts: the typical tasks the team writes in the MCP prompts screen ("customer summary", "pipeline of the month"…), which the client offers as shortcuts.
  • Autocompletion of object, view and process names.

The assistant is as good as the descriptions

What governs the model is the metadata: each object's AI description (AI description), each property's description for the API (Description in API, and Show values in API so coded values travel with their text), the descriptions of views and processes, and the ApplicationDescription setting (what this application is, and for whom). An object without a description is used badly or not at all.

docs.title: 1 bis. What to fill in so the assistant gets it right
docs.text:
The assistant does not see the screens: it sees the configuration metadata. These are the ones it reads, from most to least important. The ones at the top are, in practice, mandatory.

What Table · column Where it is filled in What the assistant uses it for Essential What the application is, for whom, and its vocabulary Settings · SettingValue of ApplicationDescription Settings, WebAPI group It is the first thing it reads when connecting (initialize instructions, flexygo://application resource and flexygo_catalog header). This is where the business definitions go: what "revenue", "overdue", "active customer" mean Essential Which objects it sees and what it can do with them WebAPI_Objects (CanView, CanViewCollection, CanInsert, CanEdit, CanDelete, CanPrint), WebAPI_Views and WebAPI_Processes · CanView WebAPI tool, Authorized Data What is not exposed does not exist for the assistant Essential What each object is Objects · AIDescrip (if empty, it uses Descrip) Object form, AI description Choosing the right object for each question. One sentence with what it stores, what statuses it has and how it relates Highly recommended What each coded field means Objects_Properties · DescriptionInApi Property form, Description in API Filtering and explaining fields such as StateId or Type: the possible values and what they mean Highly recommended That codes travel with their text Objects_Properties · ShowValuesInApi Property form, Show values in API For combos, the assistant receives the allowed values with their text and answers "Invoiced" instead of "INV" Highly recommended What each view is for Objects_Views · Descrip View form Using a view that already calculates what was asked (totals, pending items) rather than adding it up itself Highly recommended What each process does and its parameters Processes · ProcessDescrip; Processes_Params · Label and DescriptionInApi Process form and its parameters Knowing when to run it and what to ask the person Recommended What each report is Reports · ReportDescrip Report form Choosing the report when asked for a PDF or an Excel file Recommended How each object is searched by text Objects_Search (Generic = 1) and Objects_Search_Properties The object's generic searches flexygo_search ("search for García") only finds results in objects with a generic search Recommended Fields that must not be shown Objects_Properties · WebApiHidden Property form What is hidden is neither listed nor described to the assistant Optional Typical tasks, as shortcuts MCP_Prompts (PromptName, Title, Descrip, Template) MCP prompts The client offers them as buttons: "monthly summary", "customer at risk" Optional Readable labels Objects · Descrip; Objects_Properties · Label Object and property forms What it sees in the results instead of the technical names

All of this is product configuration: it is written with the project origin active so that it travels in its scripts. ApplicationDescription is a core setting, and it travels as an UPDATE in the exported project's config.sql (Export as project).

docs.title: A prompt for an AI to fill it in
docs.text:
Filling in these fields by hand in an application with dozens of objects takes time. An assistant with read access to the configuration database (for example, the builder's MCP in Claude Code, or a SQL query) can propose them. This prompt tells it what to look at, where it is and how to work out what the application is for; what it returns is a script for you to review, not changes already made.

Text Only
You are an analyst preparing a Flexygo application to be used by AI assistants through MCP.
Work ONLY by reading the configuration database (ConfConnectionString) and the data database (DataConnectionString),
and give me a SQL script for me to review. Do not execute any write.

1. Find out what the application is for:
   - Objects (ObjectName, Descrip, TableName, ConnStringID) with OriginId = the project origin
     (SELECT dbo.funNet_GetOrigin()): the product's own objects.
   - Navigation_Nodes (Title, ObjectName, PageName): how the menu is organized.
   - Objects_Properties (ObjectName, PropertyName, Label, TypeId, SQLSentence): the fields and their combos.
   - Objects_Objects (the relationships between objects), Processes (ProcessName, ProcessDescrip) and Reports.
   - In the data database, the tables of those objects: TOP 20 rows of each and the distinct values of
     the status or type columns, to understand the real vocabulary.
2. Write Settings.ApplicationDescription (SettingName = 'ApplicationDescription'): 4-8 sentences with what it is,
   for whom, the main objects and the business definitions you can deduce (what counts as
   invoiced, open, overdue…). Mark with [review] anything you cannot confirm with the data.
3. For each object exposed in WebAPI_Objects: Objects.AIDescrip, one sentence with what it stores, its statuses
   and what it relates to.
4. For each coded property (combo, status, type, foreign key) of those objects:
   Objects_Properties.DescriptionInApi with the values and their meaning, and ShowValuesInApi = 1.
5. Objects_Views.Descrip of each view in WebAPI_Views; Processes.ProcessDescrip and
   Processes_Params.DescriptionInApi of each process in WebAPI_Processes; Reports.ReportDescrip of the
   reports of the objects with CanPrint.
6. Propose 3 MCP_Prompts rows with the tasks that make the most sense for these users.

Script rules:
- Only UPDATE (and INSERT in MCP_Prompts), one per row, with N'...' and quotes doubled.
- Never touch rows with OriginId = 0 except the ApplicationDescription setting.
- Do not change a value that is already filled in: propose it in a comment next to it.
- In English if the application is in English; otherwise in the language of its labels.
- At the end, a list of what you could not deduce and need me to confirm.

docs.title: 2. Setting it up (administrator)
docs.text:
1. Enable the web API and the MCP endpoint in the WebAPI tool (Security area of the control panel): the Enable WebAPI and Enable MCP switches, which are the WebAPI_Enabled and MCP_Enabled settings (also in Settings, WebAPI group). Both are off by default: exposing the application to assistants is a team decision. Without MCP_Enabled, the /mcp route and its discovery documents return 404, as if they did not exist; the change takes effect immediately, without restarting. They are separate on purpose: the web API serves integrations (an ERP, an app, another system with its token) and MCP serves people's assistants, which is a different audience; you can have the first without the second, not the other way round.

    Enable MCP, next to Enable WebAPI 2. Grant the MCP permission to the roles or users who may connect an assistant: in the WebAPI tool (Security area of the control panel), Authorized People panel, the robot column. It is a permission separate from the web API one (the eye column): a role can have assistants without the REST API, or the API for its integrations without assistants. As always, the user overrides their role. Removing the permission instantly cuts that person's live connections; a user without permission sees the refusal when trying to connect.

    Per role (or per user, in the other tab): the web API and the assistants, each with its own switch 3. Expose the objects in the web API (WebAPI objects): which objects, views and processes the assistant sees, and whether it can edit, create or print each object. What is not exposed does not exist for it. 4. Write the descriptions (see the note above) and, if desired, the prompts in the MCP prompts screen. 5. Review the generic searches of the objects (those of the application's global search): they are the ones the assistant uses to search for text; an object without a generic search does not appear in flexygo_search. 6. Optional: adjust the limits (§5).

The application must be reachable by the assistant: for claude.ai or ChatGPT this means the Frontend exposed on the internet with HTTPS (with a reverse proxy in front, as described in Reverse proxy); for Claude Desktop or Claude Code it is enough for the user's computer to reach the application.

docs.title: 3. Connecting an assistant (user)
docs.text:
With MCP_Enabled on, each person's profile menu has two new entries: Connect an assistant and Connected assistants.

The two entries only appear if the installation has the MCP endpoint turned on

Connect an assistant opens the /mcp/setup page: the application's address ready to copy, who the assistant will log in as and what it will be able to do, and where to paste it in each assistant (Claude, Claude Code with the command line already written, ChatGPT, Gemini and any other). If the person does not have the MCP permission, the page says so and does not show the address.

The page speaks the browser's language Without the MCP permission: the refusal and whom to ask

The URL given to any assistant is the application's plus /mcp:

Text Only
https://<tu-aplicacion>/mcp
Client Where the URL is pasted claude.ai (web and mobile) Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector: name and the URL. Claude Desktop Settings → Connectors, same as on the web. Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http <nombre> https://<tu-aplicacion>/mcp ChatGPT Settings → Connectors. The server also serves the two tools ChatGPT requires of a connector (search and fetch, in the shape OpenAI asks for) to accept it outside developer mode and in deep research; they are aliases of the search and the record, and the other assistants keep using the flexygo_* ones. Any other MCP client Streamable HTTP transport with OAuth 2.1; the client introduces itself with its card (CIMD) or registers itself (dynamic registration) and discovers the rest. See How assistants register.

When connecting, the assistant opens the browser on the application. The person logs in with their usual user (with whatever SSO and two-step verification they have configured) and sees the consent page:

The consent page: who is asking, as whom, where the access goes and what is granted

What the page says, and why:

  • Who is asking and as whom: the assistant's name and the user it is going to work as.
  • Where the access goes: the domain to which the assistant receives the authorization (claude.ai, chatgpt.com, localhost for a client on the computer itself). It is the only thing a client cannot make up: it gives itself its own name when registering; the access only travels to the domain it registered. The assistant's branding is chosen by that domain, never by the name.
  • What is granted: Read data always; Modify data (run processes, edit and create records) only if the assistant asked for it, and the person can untick the box. A read-only connection rejects any write with a clear sentence and keeps working for everything else.
If the name passes itself off as a known assistant and the access would go elsewhere, the page says so and Deny becomes the main button

After Allow, the assistant is connected: the access lasts 8 hours and renews itself while it is used; a connection unused for 30 days expires and you have to connect again.

To disconnect, the person has Connected assistants in their profile menu: their connections (only theirs), with the assistant, when it connected, the last time it was used, when it expires and what it can do; Revoke, in the row menu, cuts it. The connector can also be removed in the assistant itself, and an administrator can revoke any session (§6).

Each person sees and cuts their own connections

Confirmation of writes

Before running a process or changing a record, the application can ask the person for a confirmation inside the assistant, with the exact process, record and parameters. It is off by default: Claude Desktop declares that it handles that dialog and does not, and the call is left waiting. With the dialog off, the guarantee is the chat itself: the assistant says what it is going to do and does it when the person confirms. It is turned on, if the client handles it, with the environment variable FLEXYGO_CONNECT_DIALOG=1 on the Backend.

docs.title: 4. Security
docs.text: Measure What it does OAuth 2.1 with the application as authorization server Its own login (SSO and 2FA included), explicit consent, mandatory PKCE, 8-hour tokens with rotating refresh. The tables store only the hash of the tokens: a copy of the database does not open any session. Its own permission Connecting an assistant requires the MCP permission of the user or their role, separate from the web API one (§2). Removing it, or blocking the assistant in MCP assistants, instantly cuts live connections. The user's security, always Every call runs as the user who consented: roles, objects, views, processes, security filters. MCP adds no permissions. Bounded filters An SQL filter from the assistant can only name tables of objects the role can see; anything else is rejected in words. Read and write scopes flexygo:read and flexygo:write; the person decides on the consent page. Per-session limits Calls per minute and per day (§5); when exceeded, a refusal with the seconds to wait. Per-query limit Seconds each query may take (§5); when it runs out, "narrow the filter, the period or the fields", never a server error. IP lockout Client registrations, failed token exchanges and calls without a session feed the application's greylist; too many in one minute from one address blocks it on the MCP routes (MCP scope in IP lockout), without affecting the rest of the application. Checked origin A browser request with an Origin that is neither the application's nor one of those allowed by WebApiOrigins (the web API's CORS policy, in the Frontend's appsettings.json) is rejected: protection against DNS rebinding. With WebApiOrigins set to *, any browser origin gets in, as in the web API. Logging Every call is recorded in the web API log (§6). Consent that cannot be spoofed The access domain, the branding chosen by that domain and the security alert (§3).

docs.title: 5. Settings
docs.text:
All in Settings, WebAPI group:

Setting Default What it does MCP_Enabled false Opens the /mcp endpoint to assistants. Also requires WebAPI_Enabled. It is the Enable MCP switch of the WebAPI tool. MCP_RequireApprovedClients false With true, each assistant that registers starts unapproved and nobody can connect it until an administrator ticks Approved in MCP assistants (§6). With false, an assistant is approved when it registers and can be blocked afterwards. MCP_CallsPerMinute 60 Tool calls a session can make per minute; 0 = no limit. MCP_CallsPerDay 0 The same per calendar day; 0 = no limit. MCP_QueryTimeoutSeconds 30 Seconds a tool query may take; 0 = SQL Server's. MCP_ClientPurgeDays 30 Days without use after which the ClearMcpClients job (at 1:00) deletes a registered client and its sessions. ApplicationDescription empty What this application is and for whom, in the team's words: it is the first thing the assistant reads. WebAPILog_Enabled, ClearWebApiLogDays the web API's Call logging and its purge (§6).

docs.title: 6. Logging, sessions and auditing
docs.text:
• Log: every tool call and every resource read is recorded in WebAPI_Logs with PetitionType = MCP: user, tool (FunctionName), object, arguments (Body), status (200; 403 refusal by role or scope; 404 record that does not exist; 400 argument, filter or query timed out; 429 call limit; 500 failure) and duration. It is purged with ClearWebApiLogDays, like the rest of the log. The administration screens are in the Environment area of the control panel (in flexy2022, Admin Work Area › Environment): MCP assistants, MCP sessions, MCP prompts and MCP usage.

MCP assistants: the assistants that have registered in the application (they register themselves the first time they connect; MCP_Clients table; those using CIMD take a single row per product, see How assistants register), with their redirect domains, registration date, live sessions and the Approved switch. Removing Approved blocks the assistant instantly: its sessions stop working on the next call and nobody can connect it again until it is approved again. Deleting an assistant takes its sessions with it. With MCP_RequireApprovedClients on (§5), each new assistant appears here unapproved and is approved manually before anyone uses it.

An approved assistant with one live session and another one blocked

MCP sessions: all live connections (MCP_Sessions table): who, with which assistant, when they connected, the last time it was used, when it expires and what it can do. Revoke, in the row menu, cuts it: the assistant gets a refusal and the person has to connect again. Sessions are not created or edited manually.

Revoke cuts the connection without touching anything else

MCP usage: what is done with the assistants, read from the log: calls per day (answered and rejected), per tool and per person, with the average and worst duration, and the latest refusals with their reason.

A slow or frequently rejected tool means a missing view or description

MCP prompts (sysMcpPrompt object, MCP_Prompts table): name, description, arguments and the text of each prompt the assistant offers as a shortcut.

docs.title: 7. Best practices
docs.text:
• Describe before exposing. An AI description on each exposed object, the business properties with their description and values, and ApplicationDescription with the team's vocabulary. This is what makes the assistant choose the right tool and not make things up.
  • Expose just what is needed. Only the objects an assistant needs; editing and creating only where it makes sense; the rest, read-only.
  • Let people untick Modify data. For most uses (asking, summarizing, dashboards) reading is enough.
  • Watch the usage. The MCP usage screen (or WebAPI_Logs with PetitionType = MCP) tells you what people ask, what is rejected and how long it takes; a query that hits the limit is a missing view.
  • In Claude Desktop, no confirmation dialog until the client handles it; and bear in mind that Desktop keeps the tool list each chat was born with and caches the widget: after a change on the server, you have to remove and re-add the connector.

docs.title: Approving decisions from the chat 10.0+
docs.text:
The decisions the application asks of a person (approve an order, a holiday, a credit note…) can be taken from the AI assistant that person already works with: Claude, ChatGPT or any other MCP client connected to the application. Ask it "what is waiting for me?" and the assistant shows the decisions with their context. The person approves or rejects, and has one minute to undo it before anything happens.

The rules are the application's: only the decisions that person can take show up, with the same options, the same required comment and the same log as in the inbox or on the record.

Assistant What it looks like Claude (claude.ai web, desktop and mobile) A widget inside the chat: the list, the card with its buttons and the countdown with Undo. ChatGPT (Codex too) The same widget. Tested with Codex connected through CIMD (How assistants register). Claude Code and other clients without widgets A numbered list in text: "approve 1", "reject 3 because…". The answer says until when it can be undone. Copilot (Microsoft 365 chat) Pending: it needs its own agent pointing at the application's MCP.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: The application's MCP switched on Enable WebAPI and Enable MCP in the WebAPI tool, and the MCP permission (the robot) on the person's role. The steps are in Try it. Open decisions The ones opened by decision rules, by processes or by an orchestrator through the API (Decisions and webhooks). Nothing else has to be exposed in the web API: the decision tools read the tasks with the person's security. The application reachable For claude.ai or ChatGPT, the Frontend on the internet with HTTPS (Reverse proxy).

docs.title: 1. Add the connector
docs.text:
The address is the application's, ending in /mcp (Connect an assistant, in the profile menu, copies it).

Claude (claude.ai, desktop)ChatGPTCodex (command line)Claude Code

Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector: a name and the address. Then Connect.

Settings → Apps & Connectors: create a connector with the address (on the accounts that ask for it, with developer mode on). Then Connect.

Bash
codex mcp add myapp --url https://<your-application>/mcp
Bash
codex mcp login myapp
Bash
claude mcp add --transport http myapp https://<your-application>/mcp

Inside Claude Code, /mcp, pick myapp and Authenticate.

docs.title: 2. Sign in and leave writing ticked
docs.text:
The application opens in the browser. You sign in with your usual user and see the consent page.

Leave Change data ticked. Seeing the decisions only needs reading, but taking them is writing. With the box cleared, the assistant shows the list and any approval or rejection is refused with a sentence that explains why. To fix it, remove the connector and connect again with the box ticked.

Codex says 127.0.0.1

Codex receives the access on a port of your own computer, so the consent page shows 127.0.0.1 as the destination. That is right: the access does not leave your machine. Claude shows claude.ai and ChatGPT chatgpt.com.

docs.title: 3. Ask for the list
docs.text:
Write, in your own words: "What decisions are waiting for me?", "is there anything I have to approve?".

  • At the top: how many are waiting and how many are overdue (or applying).
  • Mine: the ones assigned to you. My role's: the ones assigned to a role you hold, with the role's name. No others show up.
  • Order: urgent and high-priority ones first, then by due date. The priority shows in the coloured dot and in the label ("High priority", "Urgent", "Overdue").
  • The open card: what is asked, who asked, when it is due and what will happen once it applies. It may run a process of the application, tell an external system (a callback webhook) or both, and neither can be undone afterwards. Open the record takes you to the record in the application.
  • Click another decision to open it. Only one is open at a time.

docs.title: 4. Approve or reject
docs.text:
Write the comment if needed and click Approve or Reject. Telling the assistant works too ("reject the transport one, we are waiting for January's offer"): the assistant decides only with the option you choose.

  • Required comment: if the decision or that option asks for one, the field says so ("Comment (required)") and, if it is empty, a warning shows under the field and nothing is sent.
  • The options are the decision's: Approve and Reject by default, or the rule's own (up to three).

docs.title: 5. One minute to undo
docs.text:
Taking the decision does not apply it yet: it stays applying for 60 seconds.

  • The black strip says what you chose (green ✓ for approve, red ✕ for reject), how long is left, and has Undo.
  • Within the minute nothing has happened: not the process, not the call to the external system, not the log. Undo puts it back to pending, as if it had not been touched, and it can be decided again.
  • Only whoever took it (or an administrator) can undo it.
  • While it applies, nobody else can decide it: on the record in the application it shows as "Approve by person · Applies in a minute".
  • If you close the chat or the widget, the time keeps running on the server: the decision applies all the same. In assistants without the widget, ask "undo the last one" within the minute.

docs.title: 6. "Applied"
docs.text:
Once the minute is over (plus a few seconds at most, what the flxTaskApply job takes, which runs every 15 seconds), the decision applies:

  1. The task becomes resolved with your option, your comment and your user, and it stays in its history.
  2. Its process (OnResolveProcess) runs, if it has one, only once.
  3. The callback to the system that asked for it (CallbackUrl) is queued, if it has one.
  4. The bell notice goes away for everyone.

Applied means exactly that: it has happened and cannot be undone. The button goes away, and if someone tries (for example, by reopening an old card in the chat), the server refuses it. Turning it around takes another decision or fixing the record in the application.

docs.title: In the application, the same minute
docs.text:
The window is not only the chat's. The Pending decision card on the record (in both skins) works the same way: approving shows "Approve by admin · Applies in a minute" with Undo, and a notice reminds you.

Whoever decides through the API (sysTaskResolve) waits that minute too, and can undo with sysTaskUndo within it. The statuses and processes are in Decisions and webhooks.

docs.title: The MCP tools
docs.text:
For whoever wants to know what the assistant calls, or to try it from another client:

Tool What it does Kind flexygo_decisions The person's pending decisions (mine and my role's), with options, required comment, due date and effects. Read-only flexygo_decide Takes a decision: taskId, outcome (the option's id) and comment. It leaves the decision applying for 60 seconds. Write; reaches outside if the decision has a callback flexygo_decide_undo Undoes it while it has not applied. Write, idempotent

All three also return the text for clients without the widget, and every call shows up in MCP usage like the rest.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text: What you see Why What to do The list is empty and the application has decisions They are not assigned to you or to a role of yours That is expected: the assistant shows what you can decide Approving or rejecting is refused: the connection is read-only You connected without Change data Remove the connector and connect again with the box ticked "Write a comment first" The decision or the option asks for a comment Write it in its field Undo is gone The minute is over: it has applied It can no longer be undone It says the task is no longer pending Someone in your role took it first (or it was cancelled) Ask for the list again: it shows as applying or it is gone The widget is in another language The widget uses the assistant's language and, failing that, your user's Change the assistant's language or your user's

docs.title: How assistants register (CIMD) 10.0+
docs.text:
When an AI assistant connects to the application's MCP, the application has to know who it is: its name, where to send the access back and whether an administrator lets it in. There are now two ways to introduce itself, and the application accepts both:

CIMD (Client ID Metadata Document) Dynamic registration (DCR) How it introduces itself With its own https address that publishes its card: name and redirect addresses It registers when connecting and gets a new identifier Who uses it Claude (web, desktop and mobile), Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex… Clients that do not use CIMD yet (MCP Inspector, in-house developments…) Rows in MCP assistants One per product, always the same One per registration: a client that registers on each connection leaves a row each time

Assistants that can use CIMD choose it on their own: the application announces that it supports it, and there is nothing to configure or change in the assistant.

docs.title: What changes for the administrator
docs.text:
One row per assistant, not per connection. Before, Claude created a new client every time someone connected from scratch, and the MCP assistants list filled up with repeated "Claude" rows. Now Claude is a single row, Codex another and Claude Code another, whoever connects and however many times.

In the picture, Claude and Codex came in with CIMD: they have the redirect addresses their card publishes (claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback; 127.0.0.1 and localhost for Codex, which receives the access on the person's own computer). MCP Inspector registered when connecting.

So:

  • Approving or blocking applies to the whole product. Clearing Approved on the Claude row cuts Claude off for everyone (web, desktop and mobile share the row), on the next call. Claude Code has its own row and is not affected.
  • With MCP_RequireApprovedClients on, each assistant is approved once. Before, every new registration of Claude had to be approved.
  • The purge does not delete CIMD rows. The ClearMcpClients job still deletes dynamic-registration clients unused for MCP_ClientPurgeDays days, but it leaves CIMD ones alone: deleting them would let a blocked one back in, approved, the next time it connects.
  • Each connection still belongs to one person: MCP sessions shows who, with which assistant and with which permissions, and Revoke cuts only that session.

docs.title: Telling a CIMD row apart
docs.text:
The screen does not show the client's identifier. It is in the MCP_Clients table, ClientId column:

Assistant ClientId (CIMD) Redirects to Claude (web, desktop, mobile) https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback Claude Code https://claude.ai/oauth/claude-code-client-metadata the computer's localhost / 127.0.0.1 ChatGPT https://chatgpt.com/oauth/client.json https://chatgpt.com/connector_platform_oauth_redirect Codex https://chatgpt.com/oauth/codex/client.json the computer's localhost / 127.0.0.1 Dynamic registration 32 hexadecimal characters, no https:// whatever it declared when registering SQL
SELECT ClientId, ClientName, Approved,
       CASE WHEN ClientId LIKE 'https://%' THEN 'CIMD' ELSE 'DCR' END AS Kind
FROM MCP_Clients

docs.title: What the person connecting sees
docs.text:
Nothing new: they sign in with their user and see the consent page, with the assistant's name and the site the access goes to. With CIMD, that site comes from the assistant's card:

  • claude.ai for Claude and chatgpt.com for ChatGPT.
  • 127.0.0.1 or localhost for clients that live on the person's own computer (Claude Code, Codex). That is right: the access does not leave that person's machine.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
An assistant's card is an internet address, so the application fetches it carefully:

  • Only after the person has signed in to the application. Nobody anonymous can make the server go and fetch an address.
  • https only, with a path and no user or password in the address. An address that resolves to a private, loopback or reserved address is refused. Redirects are not followed, and the download stops at 5 seconds or 64 KB.
  • The card must carry its own address as client_id, a name and the redirect addresses. The redirect the assistant asks for must be in that list. For clients on the person's own computer (localhost, 127.0.0.1) the port does not count, because it changes on every connection.
  • The card is kept in memory for as long as its Cache-Control says (between 5 minutes and 24 hours; one hour if it says nothing). Each connection refreshes the row's name and redirect addresses, but never Approved: a blocked assistant stays blocked.
  • Authorization responses also carry the iss parameter with the application's address. The assistant checks it so it does not mistake this application for another. There is nothing to configure.

The Backend must be able to reach the internet

The one that fetches the card is the application's Backend, over https, to the assistant's domain (claude.ai, chatgpt.com…). If a firewall or a proxy does not let it out, a CIMD assistant's connection fails on the consent page with the reason ("The client's metadata document could not be fetched…"). Dynamic-registration clients do not need it.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text:
What you see Why What to do The consent page says the client's card could not be fetched The Backend cannot reach the assistant's domain Open the Backend's https egress to that domain The consent page says the redirect address is not in the card The assistant asks to return to an address its card does not declare It is a protection: tell the assistant's vendor An assistant shows up unapproved MCP_RequireApprovedClients is on and it is the first time it connects Approve it once in MCP assistants Repeated rows of one assistant keep appearing That assistant uses dynamic registration, not CIMD They are purged on their own after MCP_ClientPurgeDays days unused

Settings, the call log and the other screens are in the reference: AI assistants (MCP).

docs.title: Information
docs.text: An addon is an additional feature of the tool that can be installed separately and used in different applications.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.text:
From the marketplace located inside flexygo in the control panel, Other tools area → Addons (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Other Tools > Addons) you can install the available addons.

License maybe needed

You may need to acquire the corresponding license module from AHORA Business Hub in order to use it.

docs.title: How do I develop an addon?
docs.text: To develop an addon, you can find the necessary information here.

docs.title: Videotutorial
docs.text: If you prefer to undestand how to work with addons with a video take a look at this one:

docs.title: WhatsApp 9.1+
docs.text:
WhatsApp Business (Cloud API) is an official Meta tool that allows you to integrate WhatsApp messaging into your business solutions.

By following these steps, you will be able to integrate it with Flexygo, add contacts, send and receive messages, and even automate conversations with AI agents.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Find and install the WhatsApp addon from the marketplace located inside Flexygo.

Before being able to use it, you will need to create:

  • Purchase the FlxWhatsapp license module through the ABH portal.
  • A secure HTTPS domain.
  • A developer account on Meta.
  • An application on Meta with the WhatsApp Business product added.
  • A business portfolio for your company on Meta.

In the prerequisites section and in the first step of the official documentation they explain in detail how to complete this process.

On development

While configuring and developing, we recommend keeping the application in development mode (a mode in which messages cannot be sent) and using the test number provided by WhatsApp.

Once the configuration is complete, you can switch to production mode, verify your business, add your phone number, and start using WhatsApp Business from FlexyGo.

docs.title: Application Configuration
docs.text: Once you have completed the prerequisites, continue with the following steps:

docs.title: 1. Add Domains
docs.text:
First, add your domains in the application configuration.

Enter them in the Basic Information section within the Application Settings of your WhatsApp Business application:

Privacy policy

You must provide a URL for the Privacy Policy and the Terms of Service.

docs.title: 2. Webhooks Endpoint
docs.text:
Add the Webhooks product to your application and configure the endpoint for WhatsApp Business Account.

Complete the following fields:

  • Callback URL: Your domain + /webhook/guest/FlxWhatsapp
  • Verification Token: Enter a password that we will use later. (Explained in the next section)

Make sure you are subscribed to the messages field.

Flexygo configuration

Before clicking Verify and Save, complete the Flexygo configuration first, and once finished you can verify it.

docs.title: Flexygo Configuration
docs.text: Open the WhatsApp Business settings in Flexygo and complete the following fields:

docs.title: Default User
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsApp_DefaultAnswerUser)

Filling this field determines which user will be assigned by default to contacts created from now on. It is used to determine the language for system messages and AI execution. Leaving it empty means:

  1. The system will search for the first user with the same phone number as the contact.
  2. If found, that user will be assigned.
  3. If not found, the guest user will be assigned.

docs.title: Default AI Assistant
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsApp_DefaultAssistantAI)

Filling this field determines which AI assistant will be assigned by default to contacts created from now on. Leaving it empty means:

  1. The system will search for the default assistant of the assigned user's role.
  2. If found, it will be assigned.
  3. If not found, the AI will not be able to respond to this contact.

docs.title: Access Token
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppAccessToken)

Token required to send messages.

  • Generate a System User Access Token from Meta Business Suite, in the System Users section.

docs.title: Application ID
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppAccountId)

Required to refresh the token via OAuth.

docs.title: Client Secret
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppClientSecret)

Required to verify webhook signatures. This and the previous value can be found in the Basic Information section within the Application Settings of your WhatsApp Business application:

docs.title: Account ID and Phone ID
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppApplicationId and WhatsAppPhoneId)

Required to send messages. In your application, go to Products > WhatsApp > API Setup.

docs.title: Verification Token
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppVerificationId)

Required to verify your Webhook endpoint with WhatsApp. It must be the same value you entered in the Webhooks section.

docs.title: Signature Verification
docs.text:
(Identified as WhatsAppVerifySignature)

When enabled, this option rejects all requests made to the Webhooks endpoint and only accepts those coming from Meta servers.

It is enabled by default and should only be disabled to send test requests to your endpoint.

docs.title: Integration Effects
docs.text:
Once you complete the WhatsApp Business configuration in Flexygo, refresh the cache and reload the page. The integration between WhatsApp Business and Flexygo will be activated. This will trigger the following:

  • In skin 2026, WhatsApp will appear as a group of the notification bell in the top bar, with the latest unread messages (only for users with the sysFlxWhatsapp faculty). In the flexy2022 skin, a WhatsApp icon button will appear in the top navigation bar. Clicking the group header or the button will take you directly to the WhatsApp page in Flexygo.

  • The Cron task WhatsAppActivateInactiveConversations will be activated. Each day it will look for conversations whose last message is older than 24 hours, have an AI assistant assigned, and are in manual mode. These will be switched to automatic mode.

  • It is recommended to enable the Cron task RefreshWhatsAppAccessToken so you don't need to manually generate new tokens. Check the duration of your Access Token, and adjust the execution frequency accordingly. For example, if the token lasts 60 days, run it every 59 days, because if it expires, the refresh will not work.

  • The WhatsApp_ClearLogs cron job will be activated to delete old logs from the table and free up memory. The default retention period is 60 days, but this can be changed using the ClearWhatsAppLogDays setting.

  • The WhatsApp_ClearMessages cron job will be activated to delete old messages from the table and free up memory. The default retention period is 60 days, but this can be changed using the ClearWhatsAppMessageDays setting.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Once configured, you can send and receive messages from WhatsApp page in Flexygo.

  1. Navigation bar options. You can open the help section, create a new contact, and switch between active and archived conversations.
  2. Conversation list to switch between conversations.
  3. Toggle button between manual mode (off) and automatic mode (on).
  4. Messages of the selected conversation.
  5. Text box to write messages.
  6. Sending options. Includes buttons to attach files, send text messages, and other message types.

docs.title: Automatic and Manual Mode
docs.text:
A conversation can be in two modes: automatic or manual. You can switch between modes at any time using the toggle button in the conversation list.

  • In manual mode: Messages can only be sent from the interface.

  • In automatic mode:

    1. If an AI assistant is assigned and enabled, it will respond to each incoming message.
    2. If not, predefined messages will be sent asking the user to wait until someone responds. (The assigned user's language will be used.)

docs.title: Contacts / Conversations
docs.text:
There are 2 ways to create a new contact:

  1. Receive a message from a new number, in which case a contact will automatically be created with that number.
  2. Manually, in which case you must specify a number, a name, and a message template (because WhatsApp Business only allows starting a conversation by sending an approved template).

Once created, you can archive the conversation or edit the contact:

docs.title: Message Types
docs.text: WhatsApp supports multiple message types, grouped below by usage pattern. We can divide them into 4 types:

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Sent using the attach files button. The following extensions are allowed:

Type Extensions Images .jpeg, .png Documents .txt, .xls, .xlsx, .doc, .docx, .ppt, .pptx, .pdf Audio .aac, .amr, .mp3, .mp4, .ogg Video .3gp, .mp4

docs.title: Messages Without Body
docs.text: Messages that do not contain an array of elements. You simply fill in the required fields and send them. You also have the option to create the message as an object so it can be reused easily. (Text, URLs, Location, Location Request, and Contact).

docs.title: Messages With Body
docs.text: Messages that do contain an array of elements. In addition to filling in required fields, you must add one or more elements to their body. For this type of message, it is mandatory to create it as an object before sending. (Lists and Reply Buttons)

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Predefined messages that must be created in Meta Business Suite and approved by Meta.

Some accept variables, which must always be completed before sending.

docs.title: Basic Flow
docs.text:
Receiving messages:

flowchart LR
    A[WhatsApp] --> B[Endpoint Webhook]
    B --> C[Flexygo]

Sending messages:

flowchart LR
    A[Flexygo] --> B[WhatsApp Cloud API]
    B --> C[WhatsApp]

docs.title: Rules and Limitations
docs.text:
• When a message is sent manually, the conversation is always switched to manual mode.
  • AI assistants within the WhatsApp scope:
    • Automatically gain the ability to generate supported message types.
    • Can detect when the user prefers to speak with a human and auto-disable themselves. A notification is sent when the user prefers to speak with a human.
  • When archiving a conversation, it is always switched to automatic mode and its AI assistant is activated (if assigned).
  • To manually start a conversation, only templates can be sent.
  • If more than 24 hours have passed since the user's last message, only templates can be sent until they reply.
  • Sending and receiving messages is subject to Meta's WhatsApp Business pricing.

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• Never share or expose any token, ID, or secret.
  • Keep Signature Verification enabled in the Flexygo configuration when not testing.
  • Carefully review which sensitive information and processes AI assistants can access before assigning them to a conversation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If at any point you are unable to receive/send messages, check the following:

  • Make a GET request to the following URL to check your account status. If any issue is indicated, it must be resolved.

https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0/{{Account ID}}?fields=health_status

Your Account ID

Replace Account ID with the appropriate value.

  • Check in your WhatsApp Business application under Products > WhatsApp > API Setup > Webhook Events which webhook events are being received related to your activity.

Common causes of send/receive failures:

Error Quick check Expired token Regenerate the token or run the token refresh Cron task. Webhook not verified Verify callback URL and verification token match your configuration. Incorrect ID Confirm Account ID and Phone ID values in settings. Invalid signature Check Client Secret and keep signature verification enabled. Number not approved Ensure the sender number is approved in Meta. Business not verified Complete business verification in Meta Business Suite. Account blocked Review account health status and restrictions in Meta.

Remember that you can always contact official WhatsApp Business support.

For more technical information, consult the official WhatsApp Business documentation.

docs.title: Administrator home screen (skin2026) 10.0+
docs.text:
In skin2026 the administrator lands on a home screen of their own: twelve cards that show at a glance how the application is doing —errors, scheduled jobs, users, version, licence, health, origin, activity— and take you with one click to where you need to look.

The administrator home screen in light skin2026, at 1920 px

docs.title: 1. Who sees it
docs.text:
It is the home page of the Administrator 2026 profile (2026admin), and only administrators can open it: any other user who requests it by name is denied. The User 2026 profile (2026) starts on whatever page the administrator sets for it.

When updating

An installation that already had users with the 2026 profile stops sending them to this screen. Its administrator has to switch to the Administrator 2026 profile to have it as their home page.
