docs.title: 2. The cards
docs.text:
Each card gives its figure and, at the bottom, the links to what lies behind it.

Card What it says Links Errors Errors in the period, how many distinct causes and how many users they affect. The 24 h / 7 d / 30 d toggle changes the period and is remembered Sentinel Jobs Scheduled jobs failed in 7 days, how many are enabled out of how many, which is next and when, and the slow ones in 24 h Jobs, Failed runs, Slow runs Users Users, how many have logged in today, rejected logins in 7 days and locked users Users, Roles, Security, Rejected logins Modules not placed Modules not on any page, out of how many there are, with their bar, and pages without modules Modules, Empty pages Version The installed version and, if there is one, the new version available What is new, Update Licence The licence status, its type, the users and the expiry date Licence Health The worst state of the health panel (alarm, warning or correct), how many notes the panel has, free memory, the fullest disk and how SQL Server is doing Health and resources Origin The active origin and how many objects, pages, modules and processes it has, each figure with its link Change origin, Generate scripts Latest logins The last five logins: who, when, from where and with which browser See all Activity Actions and errors for each day of the last two weeks, in a chart Recently changed The last five configuration changes (objects, pages, modules…): when, of what type, which one and who See all Integrations The WebAPI (calls in 24 h, average time, authorized applications, exposed objects and processes) and the offline app (synchronizations in 24 h, failed and unfinished ones, active applications and the latest one) Configuration, Logs · Offline app, Synchronizations

docs.title: 3. Each administrator arranges it to their liking
docs.text:
The page lets each user move the cards, without enabling anything:

  • Move: grab a card by its header and drop it somewhere else; the others rearrange themselves. It is saved on drop, for that user: the others keep seeing their own order.
  • Pin: the pin in the header (Pin this module here) keeps a card in place; the others move around it. It is released with the same pin.
  • Reset: as soon as something has been moved, Put the modules back as the administrator arranged them appears at the bottom of the page, which restores the original layout.

There is no separate edit mode: the screen is always ready for dragging.

docs.title: 4. On narrow screens and on mobile
docs.text:
The desktop layout needs room. Below 1280 px wide, the cards regroup so that none is narrower than half the screen, and on mobile they stack one below the other, at full width. At those sizes dragging is not available and the pins are not shown, but the cards appear in the order the user saved.

The change happens instantly: when the window is narrowed the screen reorganizes without reloading, and when it is widened again dragging is possible once more.

The same screen on a mobile phone (390 px): stacked cards, no pins

docs.title: Control panel 10.0+
docs.text:
In skin2026 the control panel is a single screen with everything an administrator needs to maintain the application: which origin they are working in, how much there is of each thing, the configuration tools grouped by area, the maintenance actions and the latest things they have touched.

The control panel: status and shortcuts at the top, actions, areas with their tools and, on the right, recent work

docs.title: 1. Where it is
docs.text: In the left rail, under Administration → Control panel. The entry is visible with development mode turned on (Develop Mode, at the bottom of the same rail).

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
• Active origin: the origin you are working in (whatever is created gets this origin, and it is what Generate scripts and Export as project export).
  • Licence → View status: opens the licence status.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
A row of shortcuts to the most used lists, each with its figure:

Shortcut Figure Objects (with + to create one with the wizard), Pages, Modules, Processes Those of the active origin / the total. 555/578 in Modules: 555 belong to the active origin out of 578 in total No list template Objects of the active origin without a list template / objects of the active origin Users, Roles, Templates, App offline How many there are AI agents No figure: takes you to the configured AI agents WebAPI on (in green) if the installation's WebAPI is enabled, off (neutral) if not. Takes you to its configuration

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: The maintenance actions Action What it does Reload cache Reads the system configuration again Convert to dev database Converts the database into a development one: deletes the licence and locks users. It carries the warning triangle Preview Shows the page as a phone or tablet would see it, and rotates it Minify JS/CSS Toggle: serves compressed files Diagnostics Environment check Table changes What has changed in the data model Generate scripts The MERGE scripts of the active origin Export as project Converts the application into a project of the product template (Export the application as a project) Translate Translates the database texts into another language

docs.title: Areas
docs.text: On the left, the configuration areas —Pages and modules, Objects, Security, Logic and rules, Reports, Environment, Other tools, Offline app, Connectors—, each with the number of tools it contains. The number counts what the user can see: with different security, a different number. When you choose an area, its tools appear to its right; Environment contains, for example, the health panel.

docs.title: Your recent work
docs.text: On the right, the latest records the user has touched: which one, of what type (user, view, page…), what they did (creation, change, deletion, process) and when.

docs.title: Health panel 10.0+
docs.text:
Health and resources brings together the state of the installation on one screen: the machine, the Backend and Frontend processes, SQL Server, each connected database and how much space the history takes up. It only reports what it has been able to measure, and when something is wrong, why it matters.

The panel with one alarm (the database disk almost full) and four warnings, each with its explanation below

docs.title: 1. Where it is and who sees it
docs.text:
• In the control panel, Environment area → Health and resources.
  • From the administrator home screen, the Health card → Health and resources (Administrator home screen).

It is an administrators' screen: the data is only served to a user with the administrator role. The control panel entry is in skin2026.

docs.title: 2. What you see
docs.text:
At the top, the summary: how many alarms and warnings there are, how many connected users, whether Frontend, Backend and SQL Server are on the same machine or on several, and the Alert history link (4). The panel refreshes itself every 30 seconds, and Refresh does it immediately.

Below, one card per component. Each row gives its figure and, if it is wrong, carries the Alarm or Warning mark and a line explaining what happens if it is left as is.

Card What it says The machine Processors, free memory and each disk, with how much free space is left. If SQL Server is on that machine, the disk holding the database files is flagged: if it fills up, the database stops Backend / Frontend The process memory and what share of the machine it is, the CPU as an average over the last few seconds (it says how many), threads and handles, and how long it has been running. The Frontend also says how many connected users there are and how many open connections (a user with two tabs is two connections) Configuration The Frontend address the Backend uses and the mail account, with a warning if either does not respond SQL Server Edition, memory in use and how much of it is in RAM (not paged), how long it has been running, connections to the server (to this database and from how many machines) and who makes the backups, according to the server's own history Configuration / Data One per connected database: whether it responds, the size of the data and of the transaction log, the recovery model, what the log is waiting for before it can be reused, the last full backup and how it grows History and retention How much space the history tables take compared to the real tables, and how many cleanup jobs are enabled

At the bottom there may be a note with things worth knowing even if they are not an alarm, for example which cleanup jobs are disabled.

If permissions are missing, it says so

Part of the SQL Server data (memory, CPU, connections and disk space) requires the VIEW SERVER STATE server permission for the user the application uses to log in to SQL Server. If it does not have it, the panel does not make up those figures or set them to zero: it says so, naming the missing permission. Each database's data is read with the normal permissions on it.

In skin2026 the panel only flags what needs looking at —alarms and warnings—: what is correct carries no mark, because when nothing shows up, everything is fine. In flexy2022 it also counts what is correct and does not have the Alert history link.

docs.title: 3. Warnings arrive on their own
docs.text:
You don't need to have the panel open. Every quarter of an hour the installation checks the same things the panel shows, and for each new alarm or warning:

  • it notifies administrators in the notification bell, with the title (what and where) and the reason; clicking it opens the panel;
  • if it is an alarm and the application mail is configured, it also sends an email to each administrator with an email address.

Each problem notifies once: it is not repeated every quarter of an hour while it persists.

docs.title: 4. The alert history
docs.text:
Alert history opens the notification list filtered to health notifications: every alarm and warning that has been raised, with its reason and when.

Alert history: the installation's health alarms and warnings, with pending ones highlighted

docs.title: What's new in the skin2026 interface 10.0+
What's new in the skin2026 interface 10.0+
docs.text:
The skin2026 (Flexygo 2026) is a complete redesign of the whole application: every screen, menu, list, form, dashboard and dialog has a new design, with a side navigation that groups the menus, a new typeface, new colours and spacing, and redrawn controls. The light and dark themes already existed, and both have been redesigned with it; each user switches the theme from their menu, at the bottom of the side navigation: Light, Dark or System, which follows the device's appearance.

To switch it on, open the profile's interface and set its Skin field to Flexygo 2026.

The Control panel with skin2026

What changes for those who use and those who administer an application with the skin2026 skin: lists, search, notifications, mobile, the offline app and the side menu. Except where stated, flexy2022 stays as it was.

The screenshots are taken in light mode; everything works the same in dark mode.

docs.title: 1.1 Sort and group by any column
docs.text:
The default list of any object can be sorted and grouped by any of its columns, without configuring anything. This is done from the module menu (the three dots in the header), Sort and group…: the Sort tab for the order and Groups for the groups, with Add a field to choose each column. Several levels can be chained.

Each grouping level is a column of the list

Each group starts with a band that shows the column and the value. When scrolling, the band of the group being read sticks below the column header, and with several levels they stack, one per level; the next one pushes the previous one out. Above the list, a pill reminds you how it is grouped (Grouped by Culture › Area_1). Sorting by a group's column reverses the group. Grouping also works in flexy2022, with its colors.

Scrolled halfway: the column header and the bands of both levels stay in view

docs.title: 1.2 The column header, always in view
docs.text: In the default list, the row of column titles stays at the top while the page scrolls. Columns are widened by dragging their border in the header (the first one too), and if the table is wider than its card, the horizontal scrollbar stays at the bottom of the window.

docs.title: 1.3 The row opens the record; everything else, in its menu
docs.text:
In lists with the default template, clicking a row opens the record. The rest of the actions (view, edit, delete, open in another window, clone, configure the object and the processes) are in the row menu: with a right click on it or with the three dots that appear on hover (on touch devices they are always visible). The selection checkbox goes at the start of the row.

Right click on the row

Cells are rendered according to their content: a checkbox for yes/no values, a swatch for colors, fixed-width digits so that numbers and dates line up, and a dash in empty ones.

docs.title: 1.4 Presets as pills, and how many records the filter lets through
docs.text:
An object's presets (named saved filters) appear as pills above the list, with Show all first; the active one is highlighted.

One tap switches preset

With a filter applied, next to the list title it shows how many records it lets through (out of the real total, not out of the page).

docs.title: 1.5 Filter chips
docs.text:
The list filter is shown as chips, one per field. In dropdown fields with several values chosen, the chip shows the ones that fit and all its values appear on hover, one per line.

The "Profile" chip with two values chosen

docs.title: 2. Search: the Ctrl K palette and the search manager
docs.text:
Ctrl K (or the search box in the top bar) opens the global search palette. When empty, it already tells you where it searches: each object with a configured search and by which fields. Those marked Develop mode are only visible in development mode; a normal user sees their own.

Before you type anything, the palette tells you what it can find

The gear at the bottom of the palette opens the search manager (Filter Manager). With no object chosen it shows the summary of what is already configured: each search, its object, its fields and whether it is development mode only; clicking one edits it. With an object chosen, its properties are on the left and the search fields on the right.

The summary of the configured searches

docs.title: 3. Notifications: the bell
docs.text:
The bell in the top bar opens in one piece, grouped by source (Application, Mail…), with the number of unread items in each group, the three latest notifications and Mark all as read. Opening an unread notification marks it as read, and after Mark all as read the three latest stay in view. It closes by clicking the bell again. It has its own sound when a notification arrives; pop-up messages no longer make a sound.

On mobile it appears as a sheet from the bottom and closes by swiping it

docs.title: 4. Mobile and tablet
docs.text:
On a phone, skin2026 has its own bar: the menu (hamburger), the logo, search and the bell. The side menu slides in as a sheet over the page, with the desktop bar links inside; the profile menu opens upwards from the user. Controls are finger-sized.

The phone bar · The menu, as a sheet · The bell, as a sheet

Lists switch to card rows when they do not fit (in administration lists, below 1100 px): each row is a card with its title at the top and the rest as "label value". Module tabs are the desktop ones, with an arrow and a fade at the edge when there are more than fit. A calendar opens in its list view on the phone.

Dropdowns open their mobile panel: the strip at the top with what is chosen, the ✕ to clear and the ✓ to close, and finger-sized options. The search manager stacks its two panels, each with its own scrolling.

Card rows · A dropdown's panel · The search manager, stacked

docs.title: 5. Offline app: synchronizations, retrying and correcting what was sent
docs.text:
On each offline app's screen, the Synchronisation tab lists what the devices have sent and received:

  • Chips All, Errors, Sent and Received with their count, and a search by type, user, error, id or date.
  • Retry on each failed submission, and Retry failed · n for all of them, one after another.
  • Each row expands with its detail, and Open data opens what the device sent.
  • The app header tells you if it sends data without a return process (no return process): those submissions cannot be applied.
Three failed submissions, each with its Retry

The editor of what was sent shows the device's JSON as a table, table by table and paged, with the status of each row (Inserted, Updated, Deleted). At the top, the full error and where it has been located: the column it names, the rows that carry the value, Go to row N and 1 of N to jump from one to another. Values can be corrected and rows removed from the submission; nothing is saved until you press Save, and Retry runs it through the return process again. Raw JSON shows the submission as is.

The date conversion error, with the table, the row and the field it names

docs.title: 6. The side menu
docs.text: Out of the box it comes with Default Objects, Control panel, Help and Develop Mode; the rest is added by each application. A Group Node node is a section with its nodes, and it can be collapsed if the node says so: the node's Collapsible column.

docs.title: 6.1 Objects and master tables, in development mode
docs.text: In development mode, the Objects node gives quick access to any object: System with the product's ones (when working on origin 0) and Solution with the project's ones (origin 1 or higher). Each object opens its list. Inside each one, Master Tables: in System by groups, in Solution the project's ones; a master table with an object opens that object's list and the rest, the table editor. Unregistered users see neither Objects nor Control panel.

docs.title: 6.2 The menu search box
docs.text:
The search box at the top of the menu finds any node, including those in Objects:

  • Accent-insensitive and in any order: "sécurity" finds Security; "users object" finds titles containing both words.
  • With the keyboard: ↑ ↓ move the highlight between results and Enter opens the highlighted one.
  • If there is nothing, it says so: Nothing matches that.
  • Matches are highlighted with a tint of the accent color, and long titles end in an ellipsis.

A master table found from the search box · Accent-insensitive, with the match highlighted · No results, it says so

docs.title: 7. Ordering a page's modules
docs.text:
If the administrator allows it on a page, you can put its modules in the order you prefer. It only changes for you.

  • Move: take a module by its header and drop it where you want it. On a tablet, keep your finger on the header for a moment before dragging.
  • Pin: the pin in the header (Pin this module here) keeps it still, and the others move around it. Unpin this module frees it.
  • Go back: at the foot of the page, Put the modules back as the administrator arranged them leaves everything as it was.

Each change is saved when you drop the module. You can move the modules, but not change their size or show or hide any. At mobile width there is no ordering: the modules stack. How to switch it on: letting each user order the modules.

docs.title: 8. For product developers
docs.text:
• New columns in configuration tables: they go at the end of the table's own columns and before the reserved ones (flxInsertedBy, flxUpdatedBy, flxInsertedDate, flxUpdatedDate, OriginAddonId, OriginId). Version 10 rearranges Pages, Pages_Modules, Modules, Navigation_Nodes and Charts_Settings this way; when upgrading an existing database, those five tables are rebuilt once.
  • Easy info: the misspelled column warning is now an icon next to the title; see Easy info.

docs.title: Security: how Flexygo decides who can do what 10.0+
Security: how Flexygo decides who can do what 10.0+
docs.text:
In version 10 all of the application's security is managed from one screen, Security: a table with one row for each thing (object, property, process, menu entry, page…) and one column for each permission (view, delete, run…). One click on a cell writes the rule straight away.

This page explains the ideas underneath: who can have rules, what happens when there are none, and how they combine. The other pages of this section cover the rest:

Page What you will find The security screen Every part of the screen, its buttons and its warnings Rules, one by one Each kind of rule: what it is for, how to set it and how to check it The web API and AI assistants Who gets into the API and who connects an AI assistant, and what they can read or change Try it: a «Sales rep» role in 15 minutes A full walk-through on your own application Common mistakes and how to check What confuses people most and how to find out

docs.title: 1. Who can have rules: role, user and faculty
docs.text:
What it is When to use it Role A group of users who do the same job (Sales rep, Accounts, Technician). Each user has one role. Almost always. It keeps security tidy: you set it once and it applies to everyone in the role. User One specific person. For the exception: «this person can also…» or «this person cannot…». Faculty An ability given to individual users, of any role. A user can have several. For what cuts across roles: «can see the North zone», «can approve quotes».

And the profile? A profile is not security. It decides how the application looks and starts for the user: the look (the 2026 skin or the classic one), the start page, the language and the mail account. Two users with the same profile and different roles see different things; two users with the same role and different profiles see the same things, with a different look.

docs.title: The roles that come out of the box
docs.text: Role What it is for Admins Administrators. They can do everything: security does not apply to them. That is why you never test security signed in as an administrator. All Users Everybody, signed in or not. A rule here applies to everyone. Registered Users Everybody who is signed in. The roles you create hang from this one. Not Registered Whoever comes in without signing in (public pages). Users A sample role for ordinary users.

docs.title: 2. What is not written is allowed
docs.text:
A new application has no rules, and with no rule, it is allowed: a freshly created role can view, create, edit, delete and print everything there is. Security means writing the exceptions: what that role must not see or must not do.

The one exception is Not Registered: whoever is not signed in can do nothing that has not been granted explicitly.

Two ways to start a role

  • Allow everything and take away what does not belong: the natural choice for a trusted role.
  • Start read-only: with Set business objects to read-only… (the ⋮ menu of the screen), the role can view and list the business objects but not create, edit or delete. Then you open up what it needs. See The security screen.

docs.title: 3. How rules combine
docs.text:
When a user tries something, Flexygo looks for rules in this order. The last layer that has a rule for that thing is the one that decides:

  1. The default policy: allowed (denied for whoever is not signed in).
  2. The All Users role.
  3. The Registered Users role.
  4. The user's role.
  5. Their faculties, if any. If several faculties have a rule, one allowing it is enough.
  6. The user themself.

Two consequences worth keeping in mind:

  • The user's rule wins over the role's, and the role's over the general ones. That is how you make an exception for one person without touching anyone else.
  • The deciding layer replaces the whole row, not permission by permission. If the role has a rule for Customers with «Delete» denied and you write a user rule for Customers so they can print, that user rule must also have «Delete» denied; otherwise the user will be able to delete. The screen says so in Diagnosis with the sentence «The layer that decides replaces the whole row».

Administrators do not go through this chain: they can do everything.

The Diagnosis tab shows a user's chain on an object, and marks the layer that decides

docs.title: 4. When a change applies
docs.text: Straight away. Each click on the screen is saved on the server, and the application reads the security again. The user affected notices it on their next action: nothing needs restarting. The exception is module conditions, which apply from each person's next sign-in.

docs.title: 5. How to reach the screen
docs.text:
Only administrators can change security. You can open it from several places, and they all lead to the same screen, with the subject already chosen when it is known:

From What to click The administrator home screen On the Users card, the Security link. See Administrator home screen. A role's record The Permissions card already shows the role's rules and you can work in it. Open in Security takes it full screen. A faculty's record The same as a role's. A user's record The Permissions tab. An object's workbench In the Open block, Security (Roles, users and faculties). It opens the screen with that object as the subject. A module's ⋮ menu (develop mode) Module security. A property's or a process's record The Permissions button on its security card. The control panel Security area: Users, Roles, Faculties and Profiles lead to their lists; from each record, as above. WebAPI is the setup of the API and of AI assistants (page 4). The role's record: its members on the left and its rules on the Permissions card The Security link on the home screen

docs.title: 6. Where to find now what used to be in…
docs.text:
For whoever knew the screens before version 10:

Before Now The security tab of a role's, user's or faculty's record, with one list per kind of thing The Permissions card or tab of that record, and the Security screen with one family per kind of thing Object Security, Object Process Security, Property security and Module security in the develop menus The same entries open the new screen, already on the object or the module Checking role by role to see who can do what on an object The Object subject: one row per role, user and faculty The Import security process of a role or a user Start from another role… / Start from another user… in the ⋮ menu Process security only inside its object Also the Processes (global) family: by name, with or without an object, and with an SQL condition Working out by hand why someone does not see something The Diagnosis tab The shield of the Menus section of the Offline App Still there: offline app menus are not on this screen Security › WebAPI Still its own screen: Control panel › Security › WebAPI

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• The security screen
  • WebAPI security
  • AI assistants (MCP)
  • Did you know you can apply an object's security to a combo?

docs.title: The security screen 10.0+
docs.text:
This page walks through the Security screen from top to bottom: what each part is, what each button does and what you see afterwards. For the ideas underneath (role, user, faculty, what happens with no rules), read Security: how Flexygo decides who can do what first.

The screen with a role chosen: the subject at the top, the families and the table below

docs.title: 1. At the top: the subject
docs.text:
The subject is whose rules you are looking at.

  1. Choose the kind with the four buttons: Role, User, Faculty or Object.
  2. Choose which one in the drop-down next to them (Choose one…).

The screen's title changes to the name chosen. The screen remembers the last subject for the rest of the session.

The fourth kind, Object, turns the question around: instead of «what can this role do?», it answers «who can do what with this object?». See section 6.

docs.title: 2. The tabs: Rules and Diagnosis
docs.text:
• Rules is where rules are seen and written. It is the working tab.
  • Diagnosis answers «why does this user not see this?». It only reads. See section 7.

docs.title: 3. The families
docs.text:
Below the tabs, a row of buttons splits the rules by family: the kind of thing they are written on. Each button says how many rules the subject has in that family.

Family One row for each… Columns (permissions) Objects object View, View collection, Insert, Edit, Delete, Print Menu entries entry of the side menu Show in the menu Properties field of an object, grouped by object Visible, Editable Modules module Show the module Pages page Open the page Templates template Use the template Reports report Print the report Processes process linked to an object (the object + process pair) Run the process Processes (global) process, by its name, with or without an object Run the process

What each one means and how to use it, in Rules, one by one.

docs.title: 4. The table
docs.text: The table is a catalogue: it shows every thing of the family (every object, every property…), with a rule or without one. Next to the name there may be tags that help you recognise the row: collection, the module's or the page's type, a process's menu text, inactive…

docs.title: Search and filter
docs.text:
• The search box (Search an object…, Search a property…) filters the rows as you type.
  • Only with rules keeps only the rows that have a written rule, and says how many there are. It is the quick way to review what a role has.

docs.title: What each cell means
docs.text:
What you see What it means ✓ grey No rule: the default policy applies, which is to allow. ✗ grey No rule, and the default policy is to deny. It only happens with the Not Registered role. ✓ green There is a rule and it grants that permission. ✗ red There is a rule and it denies that permission. A dot next to the mark That permission has a condition: it is only granted when it holds.

Hovering over a cell, its description says the same in words, and the full condition if there is one.

The «Customer» row has a rule (green and red, with a dot on «View collection»); the row below has none (grey)

docs.title: Changing a permission: one click
docs.text:
One click on a cell writes the rule straight away. There is no Save button.

  • On a grey cell: the row's rule is created with that permission changed, and the others as they were (allowed).
  • On a green or red cell: only that permission changes.

While saving, the row stays busy for a moment. If something fails, the row itself says so; if it says the rule was created but not left as you wanted, click the cell again.

docs.title: Each row's actions
docs.text:
Hovering over a row shows its buttons (they can also be reached with the keyboard):

Button What it does Block Sets every permission of the row to denied, in one click. Condition Opens the wizard so that a permission is only granted when something holds. Only in Objects and Modules, and on rows that already have a rule. See Conditions. SQL Only in Processes (global): the process only runs while a query returns 1. See Processes (global). Remove rule Deletes the row's rule, after asking for confirmation. The row goes back to the default policy (grey). By object › Jumps to the same thing seen from the Object subject, to see who else has rules on it. «Remove rule» asks for confirmation under the row

docs.title: 5. The ⋮ menu
docs.text:
The ⋮ button next to the subject's drop-down has three actions that work on many rules at once.

The ⋮ menu with a role chosen

docs.title: Start from another role… / Start from another user…
docs.text:
Copies another subject's rules to this one, without overwriting the ones it already has: it only brings what is not written here. Use it to create a new role similar to an existing one.

  1. Choose the source in From this role.
  2. The screen says how many rules it will bring and from which families («Brings 16 rules to Sales rep»). It also brings rules this screen does not show: master tables, offline menus, WebAPI and page modules.
  3. Click Bring in N rules, or Cancel.

Only for roles and users.

Before bringing anything, the screen says how many rules and from which families

docs.title: Set business objects to read-only…
docs.text:
Only for roles. It deletes every object rule of the role (with its conditions) and writes view and list on the business objects. System objects are left with no rule. It is the «read-only» starting point mentioned on page 1.

It cannot be undone, and the screen says so in red: to go on you must tick I understand the existing rules will be lost and click Delete and rewrite.

The box must be ticked before «Delete and rewrite» does anything

docs.title: Remove all rules of … in …
docs.text:
Deletes all the subject's rules in the family you are looking at (for instance, in Pages), conditions included. Everything goes back to the default policy. You must tick I understand these rules will be lost and click Remove them.

It only affects the family on screen

docs.title: 6. The Object subject: who can do what with one thing
docs.text:
With Object at the top, the table turns around: one row for each role, user and faculty, and the columns are that object's permissions. The families come down to three: Permissions (the object's six), Properties and Processes. The search box looks for roles, users or faculties.

It is the view that answers «who can delete customers?» at a glance. Each row has By role ›, By user › or By faculty › to jump to that subject.

The Customer object: only the Sales rep role has a rule (delete denied and a condition on «View collection»); Not Registered shows a grey ✗ because the default policy denies it

Each row is a layer, not the final result

A user's row shows their own rules, not what they end up being able to do. In the picture, the Sales rep user is grey because they have no rules of their own, even though their role cannot delete. The final result is in Diagnosis.

docs.title: 7. Diagnosis
docs.text:
The Diagnosis tab answers «why does this user not see this?» on an object:

  1. Choose the user.
  2. Type the object.
  3. Click Explain.

You will see the whole chain in the order the server resolves it (default policy, All Users, Registered Users, their role, their faculties, the user themself), each layer with what it says, the one that decides marked, and below it the final result permission by permission, with its conditions.

It only reads: it changes nothing. Today it covers the Objects family.

The Sales rep role decides: the user can view, list with a condition, insert, edit and print, but not delete

docs.title: Rules, one by one 10.0+
docs.text:
One section for each family of the Security screen: what it is for, how to set it and how to check it works. They are all written the same way: choose the subject at the top, the family, find the row and click the cell (see The security screen).

The examples use a Sales rep role and a customers object (Customer, with its list Customers) that has a cost field (Cost). In your application they will be your roles and your objects.

How to check any rule

Sign in as a user of that role in a private window of the browser (so you do not close your administrator session) and look at the screen affected. Do not check it as an administrator: security does not apply to them. To find out why a result is what it is, use Diagnosis. More in Common mistakes and how to check.

docs.title: Objects: view, list, create, edit, delete, print
docs.text:
What for: deciding what the role can do with an object's records.

Permission What it controls View Opening a record. View collection Seeing the list of records (and what relies on it: combos, searches, the API's list). Insert Creating records: the New button. Edit Saving changes to a record. Delete Removing records: the Delete option. Print Printing the object's reports.

How: Objects family, find the object and click the permission's cell. For instance, so that Sales rep cannot delete customers, the Delete cell of the object's row.

One click on «Delete» creates the rule: the rest stays granted (green) and delete, denied (red)

The row that counts is the object's, not the collection's

Each object appears twice: the object (Customer) and its collection, tagged collection (Customers). Write the rules on the object's row, View collection and its condition included: it is the one the server reads for the list. A rule on the collection row is saved, but it does not change what the user sees in the list.

How to check it: sign in as a user of the role and open a record. Delete is no longer in the record's ⋮ menu. Through the API, deleting answers 403.

As administrator: «Delete» and the «Send price list» process are there As a user of the role: neither «Delete» nor the process

docs.title: Conditions: a permission only for some records
docs.text:
What for: a permission that is not «yes or no» but «yes, when this holds». The typical cases:

  • A sales rep only sees their own customers (condition on View collection).
  • They can only edit draft orders (condition on Edit).
  • They can only delete what they created (condition on Delete).

Conditions exist in Objects (on View, View collection, Insert, Edit and Delete) and in Modules.

How:

  1. The row must have a rule. If it is grey, click any cell twice (you deny it and grant it again): it now has a rule and nothing has changed.
  2. Hover over the row and click Condition. The wizard opens under the row.
  3. Choose the permission (for instance, View collection) and, in Assisted mode:
    • the field (SalesRep);
    • the comparison (is equal to, is not, is more than, contains, is empty…);
    • the value: a text, a number or from the context, which is a detail of the user who is looking: their login, their full name, their email, their role, their reference, their language…
  4. + Add condition adds another line, joined with «and» or «or».
  5. Test as: choose a user and click Test. The wizard says how many rows it lets through («It lets 4 of 8 rows through») and shows them.
  6. Save condition. The cell gets a dot.
«View collection» only when SalesRep is the user's login: tested as the sales rep, it lets 4 of the 8 rows through

If you would rather write it, SQL mode takes the condition as it is, with the same variables in braces: {{currentUserLogin}}, {{currentUserId}}, {{currentUserFullName}}, {{currentUserEmail}}, {{currentRoleId}}, {{currentRole}}, {{currentReference}}, {{currentSubreference}}, {{currentUserCultureId}}, {{currentUserLang}}. The wizard warns you if you write a variable the server does not know. Remove condition leaves the permission unbounded.

How to check it: as a user of the role, the list shows only their records, and the footer gives the total they see. The web API's list (and an AI assistant's) comes filtered too.

A condition on View decides on its own

On View, if you write a condition, it is the condition that decides whether the record is seen. On Insert, Edit and Delete, the condition is added to the permission: with the permission denied, no condition helps.

docs.title: Properties: fields that are not seen or not touched
docs.text:
What for: a role that does not see a field (a cost, a margin, a salary) or sees it without being able to change it.

Permission What it controls Visible Whether the field appears on the record and in the record the API returns. Editable Whether it can be changed (it appears locked).

How: Properties family, find the field (rows are grouped by object) and click Visible or Editable.

«Cost» is no longer visible for the role

How to check it: as a user of the role, open a record: the field is not on it.

The record as a user of the role: «Cost» is not there

docs.title: Processes: an object's buttons
docs.text:
What for: a role that cannot run one of an object's processes (Send price list, Invoice, Cancel…).

How: Processes family. Each row is an object + process pair, tagged with the button's text. Click Run the process.

The «Send price list» process of the Customer object, denied

How to check it: as a user of the role, the process disappears from the ⋮ › Processes menu of the record and of the list (see the two pictures in the Objects section). If it is requested through the API, the answer is «Unauthorized process …».

docs.title: Processes (global): by name, with or without an object, and with an SQL condition
docs.text:
What for: deciding on a process wherever it appears: in one or several objects, on a toolbar button, on a menu entry or called by the API with no object. And, if you want, letting it run only while something holds: during working hours, if the user has a reference, if a period is not closed…

It is checked before the object's rule: a process denied here runs nowhere. If it is allowed here, each object's Processes rule still decides.

How:

  1. Processes (global) family, find the process and click Run the process to create the rule.
  2. To give it a condition, the row must be granted (green): click SQL.
  3. The rule opens: Process, Role, Can Run, Connection String (where the query runs) and SQL Enabled.

  4. Write a query that returns 1 when it may run. For instance, only from 8:00 to 19:59:

    SQL
    SELECT CASE WHEN DATEPART(hour, GETDATE()) BETWEEN 8 AND 19 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

  5. Save. The row's SQL button gets a dot.

Anything other than 1 or true (0, empty, no rows) stops it from running. You can use the user's variables: {{currentUserLogin}}, {{currentUserId}}, {{currentRoleId}}, {{currentReference}}, the date ones and the application's context variables. You cannot use the record's fields or the process's parameters.

The process granted and with an SQL condition (the dot) The rule: the process, the role, the connection and the query

How to check it: as a user of the role, outside the condition the process does not appear in menus or toolbars, and if it is called through the API the answer is 403 («Process … is not enabled»). If the query has an error, the process does not appear either and the error goes to the error log.

docs.title: Menu entries
docs.text:
What for: an entry of the side menu that does not appear for the role.

How: Menu entries family. Each row's tag says where it is (Work Area 2026 › Sales). Click Show in the menu.

Each entry with its path in the menu

Hiding is not protecting

Taking an entry off the menu only hides it. If the user reaches the list another way (a link, the search, the API), what decides is the object's rule. So that they do not see the data, deny View collection or View in Objects too.

How to check it: as a user of the role, the entry is not in the side menu.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
What for: a module (a list, a chart, a panel) that does not appear for the role on the pages it is on. It accepts a Condition: the module is only shown when it holds.

How: Modules family, click Show the module. Each row's tag gives the module's type and its object. You can also get here from the module itself, in develop mode: ⋮ › Module security.

A module's condition is checked against the object of the page it is on: the screen runs it before saving it, and if it cannot run it does not save it («The condition does not run, so it has not been saved»). It applies from each person's next sign-in.

Each module with its type and its object

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
What for: a role that cannot open a page.

How: Pages family, click Open the page. The tag gives the page's type and its object.

Each page with its type and its object

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
What for: a role that does not use one of an object's templates (one way of drawing the list or the record).

How: Templates family, click Use the template.

The templates, with their type

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
What for: a role that cannot print one specific report.

How: Reports family, click Print the report. The tag gives the report's type (HTML, Crystal Reports…). To take away all of an object's reports, deny Print in Objects.

The reports, with their type

docs.title: Users and faculties
docs.text:
Everything above works the same with the User or Faculty subject at the top:

  • A user rule is one person's exception: it wins over their role. Remember it replaces the role's whole row for that thing (see how rules combine).
  • A faculty rule applies to every user who has it, whatever their role. If a user has several faculties with a rule on the same thing, one allowing it is enough; with conditions, they are joined with «or».

To give or take faculties from a user, and to change their role, use their record (Control panel › Security › Users).

docs.title: The web API and AI assistants 10.0+
The web API and AI assistants 10.0+
docs.text:
An integration (an ERP, n8n, a script) comes in through the web API, and an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…) comes in through MCP. Both act as a user of the application, and that user's and their role's security applies to them just as on screen. What a role cannot do in the application, it cannot do through the API or through an assistant either.

This page covers what has to do with roles and users. All the detail is in:

  • WebAPI security: answers, processes, OpenAPI, IP lockout.
  • AI assistants (MCP): what an assistant can do, how it connects, settings and log. To try it, Try it: an AI assistant working with your application.

docs.title: 1. Where it is set up
docs.text:
In Control panel › Security › WebAPI. It is not on the Security screen: it is a screen of its own.

The switches at the top; what is published on the left; who gets in on the right Where What it decides Enable WebAPI The whole API, on or off. It comes off. Enable MCP Whether AI assistants can connect. It comes off and needs the API on. Authorized Data Which objects, views and processes are published, and what can be done with each object through the API (view, list, create, edit, delete, print). What is not published does not exist for the API or for assistants. Authorized People Which roles (Authorized Roles tab) and which users (Authorized Users) get in. Two columns: the eye is the permission to use the API; the robot is the permission to connect an AI assistant. They are independent.

docs.title: 2. Three keys that add up
docs.text:
For a user to read or change something through the API or with an assistant, all three must be open:

  1. The object published in Authorized Data, with that action ticked.
  2. The user authorised, through their role or themself, in Authorized People: the eye for the API and the robot for an assistant. If the user has their own row, it wins over their role's.
  3. Their usual security, the one on the Security screen: object permissions, conditions, properties, processes.

Publishing an object in the API skips none of the role's rules. For instance, with the role of the Try it:

Request by the role's user Answer The list of customers Only their customers: the View collection condition applies. Deleting a customer 403: the role cannot delete. Running the denied process «Unauthorized process …».

docs.title: 3. Who can connect an AI assistant
docs.text:
A user can connect an assistant when:

  • Enable MCP is on;
  • their role has the robot column ticked, or they have it themself in Authorized Users (theirs wins over the role's).

Then Connect an assistant and Connected assistants appear in their profile menu. Unticking the robot cuts at once any connection they already have open.

The assistant works as the user who connected it: it sees what that user sees and can do what that user can do, nothing more. What the assistant adds is its own read and write rule.

docs.title: 4. Read or change
docs.text:
When connecting the assistant, the person sees a consent page with two permissions:

  • Read data: lists, records, totals and reports. Always granted.
  • Change data: running processes and creating or updating records. It comes ticked and the person can untick it so the assistant only reads.

With read only, any attempt to change something is refused with a sentence that explains why. And even if the person grants Change data, the assistant can only change what their role allows and what the API publishes for editing or creating.

docs.title: 5. How to check it
docs.text:
• The API: ask for a token with the role's user (POST /token) and try a list, a record and a delete. The answers must match the table in section 2. The detail of each answer is in WebAPI security.
  • An assistant: connect it with the role's user and ask it for the object's list: it only brings the records the View collection condition lets through. If you ask it to delete a record or run the denied process, it must say it cannot. Every call goes to the web API log.

docs.title: Try it: a «Sales rep» role in 15 minutes 10.0+
Try it: a «Sales rep» role in 15 minutes 10.0+
docs.text:
In this walk-through you create a test role, give it three rules on the Security screen and check the result by signing in as a user of that role. At the end you delete it all. It works on your own application, with no special data.

The pictures come from a sample application with a customers object (Customer), its cost field (Cost) and a Send price list process. In yours the names will be different.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
A Flexygo 10 application with the 2026 skin And an administrator user. An object with a «sensitive» field A discount, a cost, a margin… For instance, Customers with its Cost. A process of that object Any that appears in the ⋮ › Processes menu of its record. A private browser window To sign in as the test user without closing your session.

Licence

The test user takes one of the licence's seats while it exists. If the licence takes no more users, use one you already have by changing their role, and give it back at the end.

docs.title: 1. Create the role
docs.text:
1. Control panel › Security › Roles, and New.
  2. Type an identifier (salesrep) and a name (Sales rep). Do not mark it as administrator.
  3. Save.

docs.title: 2. Create a user with that role
docs.text:
1. Control panel › Security › Users, and New.
  2. Fill in the name, user name and email.
  3. In Role, choose Sales rep.
  4. Turn on the manual password, type a test password and turn off that they must change it when signing in; otherwise the first thing you will see with that user is the password change.
  5. Save.

docs.title: 3. Open the role's security
docs.text:
Open the Sales rep role's record (from the list of roles). The Permissions card is already that role's security screen; Open in Security takes it full screen.

The role's record: members on the left and the Permissions card on the right

Every cell is grey: there are no rules and so the role can do everything.

docs.title: 4. First rule: sees the list, but does not delete
docs.text:
1. Objects family.
  2. Type your object's name in the search box.
  3. On the object's row (the one without the collection tag), click the Delete cell.

The row turns green with Delete in red: the role can view, list, create, edit and print, but not delete.

A written rule: green grants, red denies

docs.title: 5. Second rule: does not see the sensitive field
docs.text:
1. Properties family.
  2. Find the field (Cost).
  3. Click Visible.
The field is no longer visible for the role

docs.title: 6. Third rule: does not run a process
docs.text:
1. Processes family.
  2. Find the process.
  3. Click Run the process.
Each row is an object + process pair

The family buttons now say 1 on Objects, Properties and Processes.

docs.title: 7. Check it as the role's user
docs.text:
Open a private window and sign in with the test user.

  1. The list shows: open the object's list from the menu. The records are there.
  2. The field is gone: open a record. The sensitive field is not on it.
  3. Cannot delete or run the process: open the record's ⋮ menu. Delete is not there, and your process is not under Processes.
The record, without the cost field The ⋮ menu: neither Delete nor «Send price list»

Compare it with what you see as administrator on the same record: Delete and the process are there.

docs.title: 8. Ask Diagnosis
docs.text:
Go back to your administrator window. On the security screen, Diagnosis tab: choose the test user, type the object and click Explain. You will see that the Sales rep role decides and that Delete is denied. (In the picture, the role also has the «each sales rep only sees their own customers» condition from Conditions.)

The whole chain and the layer that decides

docs.title: 9. Bonus: an AI assistant sees the same
docs.text:
If your application has the API and MCP turned on (see The web API and AI assistants):

  1. In Control panel › Security › WebAPI, tick the robot of the Sales rep role and publish your object in Authorized Data with view and list.
  2. Connect an assistant with the test user, following Try it: an AI assistant working with your application.
  3. Ask it to delete a record or run the process: it answers that it cannot, because the role cannot.
  4. If you also added the «each sales rep only sees their own customers» condition (Conditions), ask it for the list: it only brings theirs.

docs.title: 10. Clean up
docs.text:
1. Delete the test user: their record, ⋮ › Delete. If you used a user you already had, give them back their role.
  2. On the security screen, with the Sales rep role chosen, use ⋮ › Remove all rules of Sales rep in … in Objects, Properties and Processes.
  3. Delete the role: its record, ⋮ › Delete.
  4. If you ticked the robot or published the object in step 9, untick it.

Next: Rules, one by one, with conditions («each sales rep only sees their own customers») and global processes with SQL.

docs.title: Common mistakes and how to check 10.0+
Common mistakes and how to check 10.0+
How to check a rule
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a user of the role in a private window of the browser. That way you do not close your administrator session and you see exactly what that person sees.
  2. Look at the screen affected: the list, the record, the ⋮ menu, the side menu.
  3. If you do not get what you expected, ask Diagnosis: user, object, Explain. It tells you which layer decides and what each one says.
  4. For the API or an assistant, try with a token of that same user (see The web API and AI assistants).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: What happens Why What to do «I took a permission away and I still see it» You are looking as an administrator: security does not apply to them. Check it with a user of the role, in a private window. The user rule «opens» things the role had closed The deciding layer replaces the whole row. A user rule for an object with everything granted except print also grants delete, even if the role did not. When writing a user exception, go over the row's six permissions, not just the one you wanted to change. Diagnosis shows it. The list's condition filters nothing It is on the row tagged collection. The server reads the list from the object's row. Remove the rule from the collection row and put the condition on View collection of the object's row. I hid a menu entry and they still reach the list The menu only hides: it can be reached by a link, the search or the API. Deny View collection (or View) in Objects. The process disappears from every object It is denied in Processes (global), which decides everywhere. If you only wanted to take it off one object, use the Processes family. The global process with SQL never shows The query does not return 1 (it returns 0, nothing, or fails). An error leaves the process hidden and goes to the error log. Run the query by hand, replacing the variables, and check it returns 1. Check the rule's Connection String. A module's condition is not saved The screen runs it against the page's object before saving it, and it could not run. Fix the condition: the fields must exist in that object. A module's condition makes no difference It applies from each person's next sign-in. Sign the test user out and in again. A user who is not signed in sees nothing For Not Registered, what is not written is denied. Grant explicitly what a public page needs to show. «Start from another role» did not change a rule it already had It only brings what the destination role has not written: it never overwrites. Remove the destination's rule first, or change it by hand. «Set to read-only» took my conditions away It deletes every object rule of the role before writing the new ones. Use it when starting a role, not on one already set up. An AI assistant cannot connect Enable MCP is off, or the role's or user's robot is not ticked in Authorized People. See Who can connect an assistant. The assistant reads but changes nothing Change data was unticked on the consent page, or the role cannot, or the object is not published for editing. Check the three; to change the consent, disconnect the assistant and connect it again.

docs.title: How to hire ABH Sign services?
docs.text:
AHB Sign is not included in the Flexygo license, therefore it is a service that must be contracted separately.

To hire the service you can do it in any of the following ways:

  • By E-Mail: Sending an E-Mail to abh@ahora.es with the subject "Hire ABH Sign" and, into the message, your contact details such as your name, the name of the company and a contact phone number. A sales agent will contact you to carry out the process.

  • Remote: Send an email with the document to sign.
  • In-person: Send the document to be signed to a compatible device to perform the signature. It is necessary to download the following application to view pending documents, available on Android, iOS and Windows.

docs.title: Configure Reports
docs.text:
Once configured, a module is enabled to configure the reports that we want to be able to send.

Type: Enable configuration by report or document management.

Report: Report that we want to enable, the reports associated with the configured object appear.

Document Category: Category (Id) that we want to enable, the documents associated with the configured object that have that category appear (If the category is empty, the configuration applies to all).

After Process: Process that we want to execute once we recover the signed document. (You can add the DocGuid parameter to receive the inserted document or any property of the object)

To choose where we want to sign in the document, there is an assistant that is enabled with a button on the toolbar in which we can upload an example document and draw where we want to sign.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
In the configured object, a process called "Send signed report" or "Send signed document" is enabled, in which you select a report or document from those configured and an email is sent for a person to sign it.

A cron job is enabled in the system that every 30 minutes checks if any of the documents sent has been signed and, if so, collects it and inserts it into document management. Execute after process if configured.

docs.title: Azure AD Integration
docs.text:
Azure is a cloud computing service operated by Microsoft for application management via Microsoft-managed data centers. flexygo provides the integration with Azure Active Directory. This way all users could have the access to your flexygo application entering via personal Microsoft Azure account.

Obtain an SSL certificate from a certificate authority for a successful flexygo integration with Azure AD.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
You need to have certain keys such as Tenant Id, Client Id and Client Secret Id to be able to run the integration process.

  1. Login your Microsoft Azure account where you'll be able to create all required keys.
  2. Open Azure Active Directory, in the left navigation panel go to App Registration -> Add new app.
  3. Finally, generate new Client Secret Id: left navigation panel -> Certificates and Secrets -> Add new Client Secret.

Make sure you have neccesary permitions to create and manage applications.

docs.title: Platform configurations
docs.text: For the correct functionality of Azure AD Integration additional configuration is required: redirect URL, logout URL. Also you can decide if you want to restrict use of your application to accounts in your organizational directory only (single tenant) or accounts in any organizational directorty (multitenant). More info

docs.text: In the case you want to restrict user's access to your flexygo application, you can switch the assignment required option to yes: then users must first be assigned this application before being able to access it. To assign users, enter to Enterprise applications -> choose your flexygo app -> Users and groups

docs.title: Cl@ve Authentication
docs.text: We are pleased to share an exciting update to our flexygo web application: the introduction of Cl@ve as an authentication method. This addition aims to streamline user access, bolster security, and significantly enhance the overall user experience

docs.title: What is Cl@ve?
docs.text: Cl@ve stands for "Identificación Electrónica para las Administraciones Públicas" (Electronic Identification for Public Administrations) and serves as a single gateway for citizens to authenticate themselves across various governmental platforms. It supports multiple authentication methods, including Cl@ve PIN, Cl@ve Permanente, electronic certificates, and DNIe (Electronic National Identity Document).

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
To begin using this new authentication method, the first step is to register as a Service Provider (SP) with Cl@ve. This registration is essential because it involves requesting sensitive citizen information, and Cl@ve must validate that you meet the necessary requirements to access and use this data. You can find the required documentation in the Cl@ve Directory.

Following the successful registration as an SP with Cl@ve and the definition of the electronic certificate to validate SAML requests (information available in the provided documentation), we can proceed with the activation of Cl@ve authentication:

Generate Cl@ve Integration

docs.title: Face Recognition
docs.text: Facial recognition is a way of identifying or confirming an individual's identity using their face. This systems can be used to identify people in photos. flexygo has the feature to indentify known faces in a picture and return related object.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
To enable this function, you need to download trained models and extract them in your flexygo directory, for example: ~/custom/models/

You have to take into account that face recognition requires a 64 bits server.

  1. Open recognition settings and configure new object relation.

  2. After that, you are able to see a new related collection to your desired object with an image manager.

  3. Upload one or more pictures with clear face related to each object.

  4. Then you can test it using Find Faces sample process or code your own function:

JavaScript
function showFaces(file, objectname, tolerance, e): {

    let p = new flexygo.Process('FindFaces');
    let params = [];
    params.push({
        Key: 'File',
        Value: file
    });
    params.push({
        Key: 'ObjectName',
        Value: objectname
    });
    params.push({
        Key: 'Tolerance',
        Value: tolerance
    });
    p.run(params, (r) => {
        let histObj = new flexygo.nav.FlexygoHistory();
        histObj.targetid = 'popup';
        let modal = flexygo.targets.createContainer(histObj, true, e);
        modal.empty();
        modal.closest('.ui-dialog').find('.ui-dialog-title').html(r.Data.Faces.length + ' faces found.');


        let canvas = $('<canvas></canvas>')[0];

        let context = canvas.getContext('2d');

        var img = new Image;
        img.onload = function() {
            canvas.width = img.width;
            canvas.height = img.height;
            context.drawImage(img, 0, 0);

            let colorIndex = 0;
            r.Data.Faces.forEach(function(face) {

                if (colorIndex >= flexygo.utils.colors.length) {
                    colorIndex = 0
                }

                context.strokeStyle = flexygo.utils.hexToRgbA(flexygo.utils.colors[colorIndex], '1');
                context.lineWidth = 3;
                context.strokeRect(face.Left, face.Top, face.Right - face.Left, face.Bottom - face.Top)
                context.fillStyle = flexygo.utils.hexToRgbA(flexygo.utils.colors[colorIndex], '0.6');
                context.fillRect(face.Left, face.Top, face.Right - face.Left, face.Bottom - face.Top);

                let faceItm = $('<div style="float:left;margin-right:10px;"/>');
                faceItm.css('border', 'solid 2px ' + flexygo.utils.hexToRgbA(flexygo.utils.colors[colorIndex], '1'));
                faceItm.css('background-color', flexygo.utils.hexToRgbA(flexygo.utils.colors[colorIndex], '0.6'));
                faceItm.data(face);
                if (face.MostPosibleObject) {
                    faceItm.html(face.MostPosibleObject.ObjectName + ' ' + face.MostPosibleObject.ObjectId + '<br/> Dist: ' + face.MostPosibleObject.Distance)
                } else {
                    faceItm.html('Unknown');
                }
                modal.append(faceItm);

                colorIndex += 1

            });

            let imgH = $('<img style="width:100%;margin-top:10px"/>');
            imgH.attr('src', canvas.toDataURL())
            modal.append(imgH);

        };
        img.src = flexygo.utils.resolveUrl(file);

    });

}

        Try

            Dim readFields As String = "metadata,addresses,biographies,birthdays,emailAddresses,genders,names,nicknames,occupations,organizations,phoneNumbers"

            Dim contactCreate As GoogleContactCreateRequest
            Dim contactsGoogle = New List(Of ContactPerson)
            Dim contactGoogle As GoogleContact

            Dim contactUpdate As GoogleContactUpdateRequest
            Dim contactGoogleupdate As GoogleContact

            Dim response As IRestResponse = Nothing
            Dim infoJson As Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JArray

            '1) Creamos el objeto contact con los datos necesarios.
            contactGoogle = New GoogleContact With {
                .names = New List(Of ContactName) From {

                    }
                },
                .addresses = New List(Of Addresses) From {

            }

            '2) Lo añadimos a la lista de contactos, máximo 4 por envio.

            contactCreate = New GoogleContactCreateRequest With {
                .contacts = contactsGoogle,
                .readMask = readFields 'Propiedades que se recibiran como respuesta.
            }

            '3) Envio de contactos a cuentA de google del usuario, antes debe haber sido identificado en google mediante el proceso: FLEXYGO.Google.GetConsent(Entity, Ret, "contacts")
            If CreateContactsToGoogleApi(contactCreate, Ret, Ret.ConfToken.UserSecurity.UserId, response) Then
                '4) Recogemos la respuesta.
                infoJson = JsonConvert.DeserializeObject(Of Dictionary(Of String, Object))(response.Content)("createdPeople")

                For Each info In infoJson
                    If info("httpStatusCode").ToString = "201" OrElse info("httpStatusCode").ToString = "200" Then
                        '5) Codigo del contacto en google para poder borrarlo. Guardarlo en la ficha del contacto para actualizar o borrar.
                        Dim googleResourceName = info("person")("resourceName").ToString()
                        '6) Propiedad necesaria para realizar la actualización de contactos.

                            Throw Ret.LastException

                            }

                        '9) Borrado de contactos de google del usuario.
                        If Not DeleteContactsToGoogleApi(ContactsToDelete, Ret, Ret.ConfToken.UserSecurity.UserId, response) Then
                            Throw Ret.LastException
                        End If

                    End If

                Next

            Else
                Throw Ret.LastException
            End If

            Ret.Success = True
            Return True

        Catch ex As Exception
            Ret.Success = False
            Ret.LastException = ex
            Return False
        End Try
    End Function

            Dim eventGoogleDelete As GoogleEvent
            Dim response As Object = New Object

            '1) Creamos el objeto event con los datos necesarios.
            eventGoogle = New GoogleEvent With {
                .summary = "Flexygo : Evento de prueba",
                .description = "<h1 style=""color: #1a73e8;"">Evento de prueba</h1><p style='margin-top:10px'>Descripción de prueba</p>",
                .location = "Cami del Mar"
            }

            Dim dateEvent = Date.Now
            eventGoogle.start = New StartEvent With {.dateTime = DateTime.Parse(dateEvent.ToString("dd/MM/yyyy")).Add(TimeSpan.Parse("14:00")).ToString("s")}
            eventGoogle.end = New EndEvent With {.dateTime = DateTime.Parse(eventGoogle.start.dateTime).AddMinutes(45).ToString("s")}

            '2) Obtenedor el Id del calendario donde vamos a crear el evento
            GetCalendarId(userId, Ret, calendarId)

                .email = "micorreo@gmail.com",
                .displayName = "Flexygo"
            }

            eventsGoogle.Add(eventGoogle)

            '4) Envio de eventos a la cuentga de google del usuario, antes debe haber sido identificado en google mediante el proceso: FLEXYGO.Google.GetConsent(Entity, Ret, "calendar")
            If FLEXYGO.Google.SendEventsToGoogleApi(eventsGoogle, Ret, userId, response) Then
                '5) Recogemos la respuesta
                Dim infoSplit = response.ToString().Split("<response-item").ToList
                '6) Quitamos el primer elemento que no contiene información de los elementos
                infoSplit.RemoveAt(0)
                For Each info In infoSplit
                    If info.ToString.Contains("HTTP/1.1 200 OK") Then
                        Dim infoJson = GetJsonResponseEvent(info)
                        '7) Codigo del evento en google para poder borrarlo. Guardarlo en la ficha del evento para actualizar o borrar.
                        Dim googleId = infoJson("id").ToString

                        eventGoogle = Nothing
                        eventsGoogle.Clear()

                        Dim startDate = infoJson("start")("dateTime").ToString
                        Dim endDate = infoJson("end")("dateTime").ToString
                        eventGoogle = New GoogleEvent With {
                            .id = googleId,
                            .summary = "Flexygo : Evento de prueba actualizado",
                            .description = "<h1 style=""color: #1a73e8;"">Evento de prueba actualizado</h1><p style='margin-top:10px'>Descripción de prueba actualizado</p>",

                            .end = New EndEvent With {.dateTime = endDate}

                        eventsGoogle.Add(eventGoogle)

                        '8) Actualizamos el evento.
                        If FLEXYGO.Google.SendEventsToGoogleApi(eventsGoogle, Ret, userId, response) Then
                            eventsGoogle.Clear()
                        Else
                            Throw Ret.LastException
                        End If

                        '9) Cargamos el evento en la lista de eventos a borrar.
                        eventGoogleDelete = New GoogleEvent With {
                            .id = googleId
                        }
                        eventsGoogleDelete.Add(eventGoogleDelete)

                        '10) Borrado de eventos de google del usuario.
                        If FLEXYGO.Google.SendEventsToGoogleApi(eventsGoogleDelete, Ret, userId, response, True) Then ''Si el parametro IsDeleted = True -> Elimina los contactos de Google
                            eventsGoogleDelete.Clear()
                        Else
                            Throw Ret.LastException
                        End If

                    End If
                Next
            Else
                Throw Ret.LastException
            End If

            Ret.Success = True
            Return True

        Catch ex As Exception
            Ret.Success = False
            Ret.LastException = ex
            Return False
        End Try

    End Function

End Class

docs.title: Google API Key
docs.text: Google APIs are application programming interfaces (APIs) developed by Google which allow communication with Google Services and their integration to other services. Examples of these include Search, Gmail, Translate or Google Maps. flexygo invites you to use in your products the integration with Google. To enjoy the advantages of integration with Google, such as Google Maps and Google Places, you need to follow a series of steps.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
1. First of all, you need to get an Google API Key from the Google Cloud Platform Console

  2. Pick product(s) below. You can choose some of them.

  3. Select or create a new project.

  4. Set up your billing and get your API key.Once get the API key, copy this in application settings.

docs.title: Google Places
docs.text: Google Places integration provides a convenient UI for connecting to and querying Google Maps Platform APIs. It can be used to provide autocomplete functionality for text-based geographic searches by returning places such as businesses, addresses and points of interest. To make it possible you need to realize some steps.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
1. Once you've obtained Google API Key by following some steps in flexygo help, you can start configurating Google Places.
  2. With this connector you can transform a simple textbox into a autocomplete address dropdown and get sliced each part on distinct fields.
  1. To add this function, you need to invoke the following function from AfterLoadJS module event.

You can find more information about some specifics of Google Autocomplete visiting Google Maps Platform

docs.title: MailChimp Integration
docs.text:
MailChimp is a marketing automation platform that helps you share email and advertising campaigns with customers and other stakeholders.

MailChimp integration area opens with this link: MailChimp. It is also in the Connectors area of the control panel: MailChimp > MailChimp Work Area (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Connectors > MailChimp > MailChimp Work Area).

API Key is required in order to connect with MailChimp API, so the first step is to inform it. If further info is needed you can get more help about API Keys visiting Mailchimp documentation.

After executing the process, main MailChimp data as lists, templates or campaigns will be available in flexygo. This process may take several minutes depending on the amount of info stored in MailChimp application.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
Once the process is completed, MailChimp lists can be inserted, modified or deleted from flexygo. Launch the process Get lists if lists have been modified directly from MailChimp application to synchronize the info again.

When viewing a list you can see the list of contacts synced in flexygo, from where you can add new contacts to the list or delete them, these actions are immediately synced with the MailChimp list.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
Main information about MaiChimp campaigns is also displayed in this section. As with the lists, campaigns can be synchronized with he process Get campaigns. Click on to see additional details for each campaign.

In this view page, there are two processes: Get campaign info and Launch action campaign. With the first one the detailed information is refreshed. The second one allows you to effect actions as send, test or replicate a campaign for expample. When the campaign is not launched, the contact information that appears is the contacts imported into flexygo associated with the campaign list , from where we can add new contacts which will be immediately synchronized with the Mailchimp list.

When the campaign has been launched, the information of the contacts refers to the sending of the campaign, where it is shown if it has been sent to said contact, if they have opened it or clicked on it. A module with data referring to the campaign report is also enabled.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Custom and predefined MailChimp templates can also be managed from this section and synchronized with Get templates.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text:
One of the most interesting things of the integration is the option of creating contacts from an object of a flexygo application in order to upload them to MailChimp. In the MailChimp Object Configuration create a new register selecting and object and their properties to create new contacts. An object view can optionally be used to get more properties. Next step would be execute the process Generate contacts. Then, contacts will appear in module below. They can be selected and uploaded to MailChimp through Upload contacts.

It has some pre-established filters that will allow you to locate the contacts that have been modified or are pending upload to MailChimp.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: API Key can be changed from configuration area. There's also a process named Change MailChimp account to delete all MailChimp data in flexygo if you want to change to another MailChimp account.

docs.title: MailChimp Demo Processes
docs.text: Some examples of how to perform certain actions in your custom processes are the following :

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
You can create contact, upload it to Mailchimp and remove it from list using the functions provided by flexygo, for example :

Create/Upload/Remove

docs.title: Campaign
docs.text:
You can create campaign, upload it to Mailchimp, launch it and remove it using the functions provided by flexygo, for example :

Create/Upload/Launch/Remove
