docs.title: Actions on save 10.0+
docs.text:
When a record is created, updated or deleted, Flexygo can do things for you without programming: send an e-mail, notify someone in the bell, create or change another record, ask for a decision, call another system or, when what you need is not in the list, run a process of your own.

Everything is configured with rules. A rule says when (on create, on update or on delete, with a trigger and an optional condition) and what it does, as steps that run in order.

flowchart LR
  A[A record is saved] --> B{Does the rule listen<br>to that event, and do its<br>trigger and condition hold?}
  B -- no --> Z[Nothing]
  B -- yes --> P1[Step 1<br>e-mail]
  P1 --> P2[Step 2<br>create a record]
  P2 --> P3[Step 3<br>notification that uses<br>what step 2 created]

Want to try it in ten minutes? Try it: a rule with three steps.

Where it is configured: in skin2026, in the object workbench, section Rules and actions (at the end of the rail, in the group When a record is saved). Decisions and outgoing webhooks also keep their own screens, in both skins: see Approvals, human tasks and outgoing webhooks.

Steps are configured in skin2026

Rules run the same in both skins, but steps are configured from skin2026. In flexy2022 only decisions and webhooks are configured, with their own screens; for the other steps (e-mail, notification, create or change a record, process), switch the profile to 2026.

The list shows each rule in a row: when it runs, its trigger, its condition, the steps it does in order and whether it is enabled. The On / Off switch turns it on or off without opening it.

They never undo the save

Steps run after the record is saved. If a step fails, the record is saved and stays saved; the failure is kept in the rule's last runs.

docs.title: 1. Creating a rule
docs.text:
The New ▾ button of the section opens the list of step types. Choose the first one and the form of a new rule opens with that step already in it, so a one-step rule is a single screen.

The types are grouped:

  • The ones you only configure: e-mail, notification, create a record and change a record.
  • The ones that wait or go outside: decision (waits for a person to decide) and webhook (calls another system).
  • The custom one: run a process. It is the only door to the project's own code.

The form of the rule has three parts: When, Then, in this order (its steps) and Last runs.

docs.title: 2. When it runs
docs.text:
Field What it is Name The name of the rule, as whoever maintains it will read it. Enabled A disabled rule does not run, but it can still be tested (§5). On create / On update / On delete The events it listens to. At least one. Trigger Always: every time. When a field changes: only if the chosen field has a new value. When a field changes to a value: only if the field goes to a value, optionally from another one (From; empty means any value). Only if (optional) One more condition over the record, in SQL, like the where of a list: Offers.Amount > 1000.

The trigger covers the most common case without SQL, «when the offer becomes Accepted»: Trigger = When a field changes to a value, Field = Status, To = Accepted. The To box suggests the values the field holds today.

docs.title: 3. The steps
docs.text:
Steps run one after the other, in the order of the list. Reorder them by dragging the row or with its arrows, edit one with the pencil (the step's form opens under its row) and remove it with the bin. Add step ▾ adds another.

Step What you configure When it happens Where you follow it E-mail Template (optional), subject, to (addresses or {{Field}}), also to a role and a user, and the HTML body Queued at once; sent within a minute, with retries The mail outbox Notification Title, message and who (role or user) At once The bell, with the record linked Create a record The object and its fields: field ← value At once, as the user who saved The new record and its audit Change a record The object, which record (a where over its table) and the fields to set At once, as the user who saved The changed record and its audit Decision Title, for whom, priority, due time, options Opens the task at once and waits for a person The decisions inbox Webhook URL, method, what it sends (the record, its keys or a template) and the secret Queued at once; goes outside within a minute, with retries The webhook's deliveries Run a process The process and its parameters At once, on the record, as the user who saved Whatever the process does; its error, in Last runs

Any text of a step can use {{Field}} of the record that was saved, and also {{currentUserId}} or {{now}}. In the body of an e-mail, the record's values go in as text: a < or a link shows as it is; HTML fields go in as they are.

Required fields when creating a record

The Create a record form warns when the target object has a required field, with no default, that the step gives no value. That record could not be created, and the step would fail every time.

Records are saved as the user who saved

Creating, changing and running a process happen with the permissions of the user who saved the record: their security, their defaults, their audit and the other object's rules apply as if they had done it.

docs.title: 4. Data between steps, and failures
docs.text:
A step that creates or changes a record or runs a process leaves its values to the steps after it: {{Step2.Title}} is the Title field of the record step 2 created. The step's row says so (gives {{Step2.Title}}), and so does the row of the step that uses it (uses step 2).

  • A step cannot use one that comes after it, nor one that leaves nothing (an e-mail, a notification). The form does not save the rule and says why.
  • If a step fails, the others go on, except those that use what it produced: those are skipped, because running them with an empty value would be worse.
  • No loops: a step that saves a record may fire the rules of that other object, but a chain stops at three steps inside one another, and a step never runs inside itself.

docs.title: 5. Testing with a record
docs.text:
Test with a record (at the foot of the form) shows what each step would do with a real record without doing anything: it saves nothing, sends nothing and creates nothing. If the rule has unsaved changes, it is saved before the test. It also works with the rule disabled, which is exactly when you need it.

Choose the event (On create, On update, On delete) and a record from the list, which you can search; or write the where of one.

Each step comes with all its values resolved: the subject with the record's title, users and roles by their name, and what it uses from an earlier step already filled in (Follow-up created: Follow-up of Quarterly audit). A value an earlier step only knows once it runs (the number of a new record) is shown as such. A step that would fail says so, with the reason, and the ones that depend on it show as skipped.

The trigger is not checked in a test

A test has no «value before», so if the rule is When a field changes, the test reminds you: in a real save it runs only if Status changes to Accepted.

docs.title: 6. Last runs
docs.text:
Each time a rule runs it leaves one row per step: done, failed or skipped, with its message. The form shows the latest in Last runs: when, on which record, one mark per step (✓ done, ✕ failed, – skipped) and the result.

What has its own queue does not count as a failure of the rule: an e-mail that was queued and then does not go out (it is retried), or a webhook that was queued and then fails (see its deliveries).

docs.title: 7. For developers
docs.text:
What Where Rules Table Objects_Rules: events (OnInsert, OnUpdate, OnDelete), TriggerType (always, changed, changedto), TriggerField/From/To, Condition, Enabled Steps Table Objects_Actions, one row per step with StepOrder and ActionType; their field = value pairs, in Objects_Actions_Fields Step types Table Objects_Actions_Types, with the class that runs it (Handler). A new type is a row and a class that implements IObjectAction Runs Table Objects_Rules_Log (done, failed, skipped)

Rules, like the rest of the configuration, travel with their origin: a rule created with origin 0 is part of the product.

docs.title: Try it: a rule with three steps 10.0+
Try it: a rule with three steps 10.0+
docs.text:
In ten minutes you will have a rule working, without a line of code: every time someone creates a role,

  1. the administrators get a notification in the bell;
  2. a task is opened to give that role its permissions;
  3. and you get another notification with the number of that task, which step 2 has just created.

We use Roles because every application has them; any other object works the same. No mail server or other system is needed.

This page is the short way to try it. What each step type does, the triggers and the failures are in the reference: Actions on save.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: A Flexygo application, version 10 A local development install will do. Log in as an administrator. The skin2026 skin Steps are configured in skin2026. If your profile is flexy2022, switch it to 2026 to configure; the rule runs the same in both skins.

docs.title: 1. Open the rules of the Role object
docs.text: In the control panel, Objects, find sysRole and open it: that is the object workbench. At the end of the rail, Rules and actions.

docs.title: 2. Create the rule with its first step
docs.text:
New ▾ › Notification. The form of a new rule opens with a notification already in it. Fill in:

Field Value Name Welcome a new role On create on (it is by default) Trigger Always Step 1, Step name Tell the admins Step 1, Title New role {{Name}} (the braces read the record's field) Step 1, To the role Admins

docs.title: 3. Add the step that creates the task
docs.text:
Add step ▾ › Create a record:

Field Value Step name Open a task to give it permissions In object sysTask (the tasks of the decisions inbox) Add field: Title ← Give permissions to the role {{Name}} Add field: Assigned role ← admins

docs.title: 4. Add the notification that uses step 2
docs.text:
Add step ▾ › Notification:

Field Value Step name Tell me the task Title Task {{Step2.TaskId}}: {{Step2.Title}} To the user you

{{Step2.TaskId}} is the number of the task step 2 will create. The row of step 2 now says gives {{Step2.TaskId}}, and the row of step 3, uses step 2. Save.

docs.title: 5. Test it without doing anything
docs.text:
Test with a record, event On create, and pick the role Admins from the list.

Each step shows its values resolved: New role Admins for the role Admins, the task it would open and your notification with its title. The task number is marked TaskId of step 2, once created: it is only known once the task exists. Nothing has been saved, sent or created.

docs.title: 6. Create a role
docs.text:
Open the list of roles and create one: Id salestest, name Sales test. Save.

Check:

  • In the bell (or the list of notices), New role Sales test and Task 6cf7…: Give permissions to the role Sales test.
  • In the decisions inbox, the task Give permissions to the role Sales test, for Admins.
  • In the rule's form, Last runs: ✓ ✓ ✓ and All done.

docs.title: What next
docs.text:
• Switch the trigger to When a field changes to a value, so the rule acts only when a field goes to a given value.
  • Add an E-mail step if mail is configured.
  • To remove the test: delete the rule from its form (Delete) and, if you like, the role salestest and its task.

docs.title: Approvals, human tasks and outbound webhooks 10.0+
Approvals, human tasks and outbound webhooks 10.0+
docs.text:
Decisions and webhooks are two step types of actions on save

A decision rule or an outgoing webhook is a rule with one step. If you want a single save to do several things in order (an e-mail, a notification, create a record, a decision, a webhook…), see Actions on save. This page still covers everything specific to decisions (inbox, card, escalation, web API) and to webhooks (signature, retries, deliveries).

Flexygo does not orchestrate automations: that is what n8n, Make, Zapier or any other orchestrator is for. What it does do is what an orchestrator cannot do on its own: open a decision to a person or a role inside the application, with its inbox, its deadline and its escalation, and notify the outside world when a record changes (outbound webhooks). The two pieces combine into a circuit:

flowchart LR
  A[A record is saved] --> B{Subscription\nmatches}
  B -- yes --> C[Outbound webhook\nsigned POST]
  C --> D[Orchestrator\nn8n, Make…]
  D -- sysTaskCreate --> E[Task in Flexygo]
  A --> F{Decision rule\nmatches}
  F -- yes --> E
  E --> G[A person decides\ninbox, record view or API]
  G -- CallbackUrl --> D
  G -- OnResolveProcess --> H[Flexygo process]

The orchestrator and the callback are optional: a decision rule opens tasks on save without leaving Flexygo, and an outbound webhook serves any HTTP receiver even if there is no task behind it.

Want to try it in fifteen minutes? Try it: a decision and an outbound webhook.

Everything looks and is configured the same way in both skins (skin2026 and flexy2022):

What skin2026 flexy2022 The inbox Decisions menu node, with a counter Decisiones menu node, with a counter Decision rules Control panel › Logic and rules › Decision rules Admin › Lógica y reglas › Reglas de decisión Outbound webhooks and their deliveries Control panel › Logic and rules › Outgoing webhooks Admin › Lógica y reglas › Webhooks de salida From the object The object's workbench, Rules and actions section (see Actions on save) —

docs.title: 1. Human tasks (decisions)
docs.text:
A task is a question with options —Approve / Reject by default— addressed to a role, to a person, or to a person within a role, about a record or without one. It lives in the Tasks table (sysTask object), with its history in Tasks_Log.

Where it is decided What is there Decisions (menu node, with a counter) The inbox: Mine · My roles · All open · Resolved, with the options on the row and the link to the record. The task record view (sysTask) The Resolve, Reassign and Cancel processes in the process menu (only while it is pending). The record's record view The Pending decision card (sysmod-task-decision-2026 module) shows the pending tasks of that record with their buttons, the comment and the history. It comes out of the box at the top of the default record views (view and edit) of every object that has no record view of its own, and takes no space if the record has nothing pending. On an object with its own record view (users, roles…) it is placed by hand like any module. The bell Each pending task leaves a notice (Notices) for the user or the role members; it expires when the task is decided, cancelled, reassigned or expires. The web API The same processes, see §3.

What the card costs

Opening a default record view runs one more query, the record's pending tasks, backed by the IX_Tasks_Status_Object index on Tasks. Measured with 50,000 tasks in the table: between 44 and 57 ms per opening. Lists do not carry it.

docs.title: Statuses and priorities
docs.text:
Status When pending Open, waiting for someone. applying Someone chose an option and the decision waits a minute (ApplyAt) before it applies; meanwhile it can be undone. resolved Someone chose an option (Outcome), with or without a Comment, and it applied. cancelled It was cancelled without a decision. expired The deadline passed and there was no one to escalate to.

Priority: 0 normal, 1 high, 2 urgent.

docs.title: Deadline and escalation
docs.text:
The flxTaskEscalation job (every 5 minutes, sysTaskEscalation process) looks at overdue pending tasks:

  • At DueDate + EscalateAfter minutes, if the task names a target (EscalateToRoleId or EscalateToUserId), it escalates only once: the target becomes the assignee, escalated is recorded in the log and the new assignee is notified.
  • If it names no target, it expires (expired, expired action in the log).
  • Without EscalateAfter, the task only shows as overdue: nobody moves it.

docs.title: What happens on decision
docs.text:
1. It checks that the person deciding is allowed —the assigned user, anyone with the assigned role, an administrator, or anyone if the task is not assigned; role membership is read from the database at that moment— and that there is a comment if the task or the option requires one (RequireComment, or requireComment on the option).
  2. The decision stays applying for 60 seconds (ApplyAt), with Outcome, Comment and who decided. Nothing else happens yet and nobody else can decide it. Within that minute, whoever decided (or an administrator) can undo it with Undo on the card or the sysTaskUndo process: it goes back to pending without a trace. It is the same minute you get when deciding from the chat (Approving decisions from the chat).
  3. Once the minute is over, the flxTaskApply job (every 15 seconds) applies it: it writes resolved with ResolvedBy and ResolvedDate, along with the log. From then on it cannot be undone.
  4. If the task has an OnResolveProcess, that Flexygo process is run with TaskId, Outcome, Comment, ObjectName, ObjectWhere and CorrelationId, bound to the task's record if it has one. The decision stands even if the process fails: the failure comes back as a warning (WarningMessage) and in Data (OnResolveProcessSuccess: false).
  5. If the task has a CallbackUrl, a webhook with the result is queued (§5). The same happens on cancel and on expiry.

docs.title: 2. Decision rules
docs.text:
A rule (a rule of Objects_Rules with a decision step in Objects_Actions; sysTaskRule object, Decision rules / Reglas de decisión node under Logic and rules, and the Rules and actions section of the object's workbench) opens a task when a record of the object is saved, with no code. It is evaluated after the save is committed, whether it comes from a screen or from the web API; whoever saves does not need permission on the task processes.

Field What for Object The object being watched. After insert / After update On which saves it is evaluated. Only if (Condition) A WHERE on the object's table; the rule fires if the saved record meets it. Empty: always. Title / Description Templates with {{Field}} from the record (and {{currentUserLogin}} and the rest of Flexygo's placeholders). Options JSON [{"id":"approve","label":"Approve"},{"id":"reject","label":"Reject","requireComment":true}]. Empty: Approve / Reject. Require a comment Makes a comment mandatory for any option. Assigned role / user Who it is opened to. Role and user together: the person within the role. Priority and Urgent if A fixed priority, and a WHERE that raises it to urgent when the record meets it. Due in (minutes) Deadline from the moment it is opened. Escalate after / to role / to user The escalation from §1. On resolve process Process that receives the result (§1). Callback URL / Callback secret To notify an orchestrator on decision (§5). The secret is stored in the rule, is shown masked and is passed on to every task the rule opens. Enabled A disabled rule does not fire.

External objects: no condition

On an external object (its records live behind an API, see External entities) there is no table to evaluate a WHERE on. That is why, when an external object is chosen, Only if and Urgent if are disabled, and the server rejects a condition that arrives by another route (the web API, or a value that was already written) with «An external object takes no condition». A rule without a condition works just as on any other object.

Test with a record

In the rule's record view, the Test with a record process asks for a WHERE that names a record (Id = 'admins') and shows, without creating it, the task it would open: rendered title, assignee, priority, due date, escalation and events. The answer comes up in a dialog titled with the rule's name, closed with OK. If the record does not meet the condition, or the rule is disabled, it says so. Through the web API, the same text arrives in Data.Message.

An object's rules are read once along with its configuration and are reloaded when a rule is saved or deleted from its record view: no restart is needed. An object without rules pays nothing on save.

docs.title: 3. Tasks API
docs.text:
Everything goes through the Flexygo web API: POST /token (grant_type=password, username, password) and Authorization: Bearer …. The user needs API access (WebAPI_Users), and the processes and the sysTask object must be published in it (WebAPI_Processes, WebAPI_Objects), like any other.

Call What it does POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskCreate Opens a task. Parameters in the body (JSON), below. POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskResolve/sysTask/{TaskId} Decides: Outcome (mandatory, the id of an option) and Comment. The decision applies a minute later. POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskUndo/sysTask/{TaskId} Undoes the decision taken while it has not applied. POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskCancel/sysTask/{TaskId} Cancels: Comment. POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskReassign/sysTask/{TaskId} Reassigns: AssignedRoleId, AssignedUserId, Comment. GET /webapi/object/sysTask · GET /webapi/object/sysTask/{TaskId} Reads tasks like any object. POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskRuleTest/sysTaskRule/{RuleId} A rule's Test with a record: Record (a WHERE that names a record, Id = 'admins'). Creates nothing; the text of the task it would open comes back in Data.Message. POST /webapi/exec/sysWebhookTest/sysWebhookSubscription/{SubscriptionId} A subscription's Send a test: Record, as above. Queues a real delivery with event: test. POST /webapi/exec/sysWebhookRetry/sysWebhookDelivery/{DeliveryId} Retry: queues a failed or dead delivery again.

A process of an object is called with its object and its record

Every process that hangs from an object is called as /webapi/exec/<process>/<object>/<id>: the web API requires it and, without the object and the record in the route, answers «send the object and the record (id or filter) to run it on». An id that does not exist gives 404 «record not found», and a process that the record does not allow (a Retry of a delivery already sent) gives «not available for this record». Only sysTaskCreate, which hangs from no object, goes without a record. Rules, subscriptions and deliveries are administrators only: the API user that tests or retries them has to be one.

docs.title: sysTaskCreate parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes Title text Mandatory. Accepts {{Field}} from the record if ObjectName/ObjectWhere is given. Descrip long text Context for whoever decides; also with {{Field}}. ObjectName, ObjectWhere text The record being decided on. ObjectWhere can be plain (Id = 'x', or a webhook's objectWhere as is) or encrypted as a Flexygo screen delivers it; it is always stored in plain form, as the record's key ([AspNetRoles].[Id] = N'x'), so that the task keeps finding its record even if the application moves to another server. No record is also fine. AssignedRoleId, AssignedUserId text To whom. Both: the person within the role. Neither: the task stays open to anyone. Priority 0 · 1 · 2 normal · high · urgent. DueDate date-time Deadline. EscalateAfter, EscalateToRoleId, EscalateToUserId The escalation from §1. Options JSON The options; empty: Approve / Reject. RequireComment boolean OnResolveProcess text Flexygo process that receives TaskId, Outcome, Comment, ObjectName, ObjectWhere and CorrelationId. CallbackUrl URL POST with the result on decision, cancellation or expiry (§5). CallbackSecret text The secret shared with whoever receives the callback, to sign it (§4, Headers and signature). It is stored in the task and shown masked in its record view. Empty: the callback goes unsigned. CorrelationId text Whatever the caller wants to get back (its execution id, for example).

The response is that of any process: Success, SuccessMessage, WarningMessage, LastException and Data (TaskId and Status; on resolve, also Outcome and the result of the OnResolveProcess).

JSON
POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskCreate
{
  "Title": "Approve the new role {{Name}}",
  "ObjectName": "sysRole",
  "ObjectWhere": "Id = 'sales'",
  "AssignedRoleId": "admins",
  "Priority": 1,
  "DueDate": "2026-09-17T18:00:00",
  "EscalateAfter": 1440,
  "EscalateToRoleId": "admins",
  "CallbackUrl": "https://n8n.example.com/webhook-waiting/1234",
  "CallbackSecret": "a-long-random-string-shared-with-n8n",
  "CorrelationId": "1234"
}

When resolving through the API, Outcome goes in the body with the option's id:

JSON
POST /webapi/exec/sysTaskResolve/sysTask/0F12D8AC-…
{ "Outcome": "reject", "Comment": "Not this quarter" }

docs.title: 4. Outbound webhooks
docs.text:
A subscription (a rule of Objects_Rules with a webhook step in Objects_Actions; sysWebhookSubscription object) sends a POST to a URL when a record of the object is saved or deleted. The save never waits for the receiver: the delivery is queued (WebHooks_Deliveries) and the flxWebhookDispatcher job (every minute, SendPendingWebhooks process) sends it.

Subscriptions and their deliveries live on a single screen, Outgoing webhooks / Webhooks de salida, with two tabs: Subscriptions (Suscripciones) and Deliveries (Envíos), the log of everything that has been sent. It is the same in both skins. It can also be reached from the Webhooks section of the object's workbench.

Outbound and inbound webhooks

This screen is the outbound one: Flexygo notifies another system. Inbound webhooks (another system calls Flexygo, /webhook/{id}, sysWebHook object) belong to the web API and have no menu node.

Field What for Object The object being watched. After insert / update / delete The events it listens to. Only if (Condition) A WHERE on the table; on delete it is evaluated before deleting. Not allowed on an external object (as with rules, §2). Url, Method Where and how (POST by default). Headers Fixed headers, in JSON: {"X-Api-Key": "…"}. Secret The secret shared with the receiver, which signs every delivery (below). It is stored in the subscription and shown masked. Empty: the delivery goes unsigned. Payload record (The whole record: all fields of the record), keys (only the keys) or template (Template rendered with {{Field}}, as is). Timeout (seconds), Attempts 10 s and 6 attempts by default. Enabled A disabled subscription does not queue.

An object's subscriptions are read once along with its configuration and are reloaded when a subscription is saved from its record view. An object without subscriptions pays nothing on save.

docs.title: The body
docs.text:
With record and keys, the body is a fixed envelope with the record in data (binary fields are omitted):

JSON
{
  "event": "insert",
  "object": "sysRole",
  "objectWhere": "[AspNetRoles].[Id] = N'sales'",
  "subscriptionId": "2eebc76e-…",
  "firedAt": "2026-09-15T20:03:11.4+02:00",
  "firedBy": "admin",
  "data": { "Id": "sales", "Name": "Sales", "…": "…" }
}

event is insert, update, delete, test (a test delivery) or task (a task callback, §5). objectWhere is the record's key in plain form: it can be used as is for sysTaskCreate or to read the record through the web API. With template, the body is exactly the rendered template.

docs.title: Headers and signature
Retries and statuses
docs.text:
A 2xx response marks the delivery sent. Any other —or no response within the timeout— leaves it failed and schedules the next attempt: 1 · 5 · 15 · 60 · 240 · 720 minutes after the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and subsequent failures. Once the attempts (MaxAttempts) are used up, it becomes dead. The last code, the response (up to 4,000 characters) and the error are stored.

Status What it is pending Queued, waiting for the dispatcher. sent Delivered (2xx). failed It failed and will be retried at NextAttempt. dead It used up its attempts.

All deliveries, including task callbacks (§5), are on the Deliveries tab (Envíos). In the record view of a failed or dead delivery, the Retry process queues it again right away (a failure leaves it dead again).

Send a test

In the subscription's record view, Send a test asks for a WHERE that names a record and queues a real delivery with event: test, even if the subscription is disabled or the record does not meet the condition —the message says whether a save would have fired it—. It goes out within a minute and stays on the Deliveries tab.

docs.title: 5. A task's callback
docs.text:
When a task with a CallbackUrl is decided, cancelled or expires, a task delivery to that URL is queued, through the same queue and with the same headers and retries (POST method, 10 s, 6 attempts); signed if the task has a CallbackSecret (if a rule opened it, the rule's Callback secret). The task log records callback_sent or callback_failed.

JSON
{
  "event": "task",
  "object": "sysTask",
  "objectWhere": "(TaskId='0F12D8AC-…')",
  "taskId": "0F12D8AC-…",
  "firedAt": "2026-09-15T20:05:40.1+02:00",
  "firedBy": "admin",
  "data": {
    "taskId": "0F12D8AC-…",
    "title": "Approve the new role Sales",
    "status": "resolved",
    "outcome": "approve",
    "comment": null,
    "correlationId": "1234",
    "objectName": "sysRole",
    "objectWhere": "…",
    "resolvedBy": "admin",
    "resolvedDate": "2026-09-15T20:05:38",
    "sourceProcess": "rule New role needs a look"
  }
}

An expired task arrives with "status": "expired" and "outcome": null; a cancelled one, with "status": "cancelled".

docs.title: Public addresses only
docs.text:
The CallbackUrl is set by whoever opens the task through the API, not by an administrator, so Flexygo only calls it when its server is at a public address. It does not call it if the name resolves to an internal address: loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1), private networks (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), link-local (169.254.x, including the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254, and fe80::), CGNAT (100.64.x), multicast, broadcast, and IPv6 unique-local addresses (fc00::/7) or ones that carry a private IPv4 inside. Every address of the name is checked when connecting, the connection goes to the address that was checked, and a redirect to an internal address is refused too.

If the orchestrator is on the internal network (an n8n on the intranet, for example), its host is added to the DecisionCallbackAllowedHosts setting (security group): a comma-separated list of host names, or of host:port to allow that port only. For example, n8n.intranet, 10.0.0.5:5678. Empty by default.

The server's certificate is validated: a self-signed or invalid one is only accepted from a host listed in DecisionCallbackAllowedHosts. Callbacks do not go through a proxy: a server that can only reach the Internet through one cannot deliver them.

A refused call does not lose the decision: the task stays resolved and the delivery fails with the error Internal address not allowed: … on the Deliveries tab, which names the host and the setting. It is retried like any other delivery, so once the host is added to the setting the next attempt goes out; Retry sends it right away. If the address is written in the URL (http://127.0.0.1:5678/..., http://localhost/...), sysTaskCreate says so when the task is created. Only the first 500 characters of the callback's answer are kept.

docs.title: 6. Example: n8n orchestrates, Flexygo decides
docs.text:
1. A subscription on sysRole (After insert) points to the n8n Webhook node.
  2. n8n requests a token (POST /token), calls sysTaskCreate with the payload's objectWhere, CallbackUrl = {{ $execution.resumeUrl }}, CorrelationId = {{ $execution.id }} and, if it wants to check who calls it, a CallbackSecret, and waits in a Wait node (resume on webhook). If n8n is on the internal network, its host goes in DecisionCallbackAllowedHosts (§5).
  3. A person decides in the Flexygo inbox.
  4. The callback reaches the resume URL; n8n continues along the approve or reject branch by reading body.data.outcome.

Without n8n, the same circuit is built with a decision rule on sysRole and, if a reaction is needed, an OnResolveProcess.

docs.title: Try it: a decision and an outbound webhook 10.0+
Try it: a decision and an outbound webhook 10.0+
docs.text:
In about fifteen minutes you will have two things working, without a line of code:

  • a decision: every time someone creates a role, an administrator has to approve it, from their inbox;
  • an outbound webhook: every time a role is saved, another system receives the whole record, signed.

We use Roles because every application has it; with any other object it works the same way.

This page is the short path to try it. What each piece does, the web API, the signature, the retries and the n8n example are in the reference: Approvals, human tasks and outbound webhooks.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
A version 10 Flexygo application A local development installation will do. Log in with an administrator user (Admins role). An HTTP receiver for the webhook The quickest is a webhook.site address, which shows every request it receives. An n8n Webhook node also works. Only for steps 4 and 5.

Both skins (skin2026 and flexy2022) have the same screens. Where the path differs, both are given.

docs.title: 1. Creating a decision rule
docs.text:
skin2026 flexy2022 Control panel › Logic and rules › Decision rules Admin › Lógica y reglas › Reglas de decisión

New, and fill in:

Field Value Name New role, approve it Object Role Enabled, After insert on Title Approve the new role {{Name}} (the braces read the record's field) Description {{currentUserLogin}} created the role {{Name}} Assigned role Admins Due in (minutes) 60

Leave Options empty (they will be Approve / Reject) and Only if empty (every new role). Save.

Check: in the record view's menu, Test with a record, with Id = 'admins'. A dialog shows the task it would open (rendered title, to whom, priority, due date), without creating it.

docs.title: 2. Creating a role
docs.text:
Open the roles list (in skin2026, the Roles shortcut in the control panel; in flexy2022, under Admin › Seguridad) and press New: Id salestest, name Sales test. Save.

Check: the Decisions menu node (Decisiones) raises its counter by one, and there is a notice in the bell. If you do not see it straight away, reload the page.

docs.title: 3. Deciding
docs.text:
Open Decisions. The task Approve the new role Sales test is among yours, assigned to Admins («anyone in the role»), with its deadline and the link to the role. The segments at the top separate what is yours, what belongs to your roles, everything open and what is resolved.

Press Approve on the row. Check: the row moves to Resolved, with who decided and when.

The card on the record's record view

On objects that use the default record view, the same decision shows at the top of the record's record view, with its comment and its history. It is the most direct way to decide while looking at the record. Roles has its own record view, so it does not show there: the sysmod-task-decision-2026 module is placed by hand, like any other.

docs.title: 4. Creating an outbound webhook
docs.text:
skin2026 flexy2022 Control panel › Logic and rules › Outgoing webhooks Admin › Lógica y reglas › Webhooks de salida

It is one screen with two tabs: Subscriptions (Suscripciones), what is being watched, and Deliveries (Envíos), everything that has been sent.

On Subscriptions, New:

Field Value Name Roles to my receiver Object Role Enabled, After insert, After update on Url your receiver's address (the webhook.site one, for example) Secret any long string; write it down, the receiver needs it to check the signature Payload The whole record

Save. The secret is masked in the record view.

Check: in the record view's menu, Send a test, with Id = 'admins'. It queues a real delivery with event: test. In less than a minute it shows on the Deliveries tab as sent with status 200, and your receiver shows the POST.

docs.title: 5. Watching it arrive for real
docs.text:
Edit the Sales test role (change the name) and save. The save does not wait for the receiver: the delivery is queued and goes out within the next minute.

Check:

  • on Deliveries there is a new row, event update, sent, 200;
  • the receiver gets the envelope with the whole role in data, and the headers X-Flexygo-Event: update and X-Flexygo-Signature: sha256=….

To check the signature with the secret from step 4, the code is in the reference: Headers and signature.

docs.title: 6. Going further: an orchestrator waiting for the decision
docs.text:
The two pieces come together when an orchestrator (n8n, Make…) opens the task through the web API and waits for someone to decide:

  1. it calls sysTaskCreate with a CallbackUrl and a CallbackSecret;
  2. the person decides in the inbox;
  3. Flexygo sends the result, signed, to that URL.

The complete n8n example is in the reference: n8n orchestrates, Flexygo decides.

docs.title: 7. Cleaning up
docs.text: Turn off Enabled in the rule and in the subscription (or delete them) and delete the Sales test role.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text:
What you see Why What to do No task opens when the role is created The rule is disabled, has no After insert, or its Only if is not met Step 1: Test with a record says which of the three The Decisions counter does not go up The task is assigned to a role that is not yours Look at All open in the inbox; change Assigned role Reject asks for a comment The option or the rule requires a comment That is expected: write the reason Only if is disabled The chosen object is external: its records live behind an API and there is no table to evaluate a WHERE on It works without a condition; see External objects The delivery stays pending The flxWebhookDispatcher job is not running In Logic and rules › Cron Jobs, make sure it is active The delivery comes out failed with a code The receiver did not answer 2xx within the timeout It retries on its own (1, 5, 15, 60, 240 and 720 minutes); Retry on the delivery's record view sends it now The signature does not match at the receiver The receiver computes over the already parsed body, or with another secret Compute the HMAC over the raw body, with the same Secret The rule's record view does not accept the Callback URL The field validates a public address: localhost or 192.168.… do not pass Use a public address, or open the task through the web API

For everything else (statuses, escalation, the web API, the shape of the body and of the callback) there is the reference: Approvals, human tasks and outbound webhooks.

docs.title: Open page
docs.text:
We can open any object default page using the flexygo.nav.openPage method and indicating the taget type and the entity or collection.

TypeScript
/**
* Opens the default object page
 * @method openPage
 * @param {string} pagetypeid - Type of the page (list, view, edit)
 * @param {string} objectname - Name of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} objectwhere - Where of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} defaults - Defaults to be added to the page
 * @param {string} targetid - Target to open the window
 * @param {boolean} excludeHist - True to not store in history
 * @param {JQuery} triggerElement - Relative element to open the page
 * @param {boolean} isClone - Only for opening page with clone options
 * @param {flexygo.nav.FlexygoHistory} previousHist - Previous page history
 * @param {string} presets - Used for opening page with a default preset, can be a preset ID or a JSON string 
 */
openPage(pagetypeid: string, objectname: string, objectwhere: string, defaults: string | flexygo.nav.PageDefaults, targetid: string, excludeHist?: boolean, triggerElement?: JQuery, isClone?: boolean, previousHist?: flexygo.nav.FlexygoHistory, presets?: string ): void

docs.title: Open page by name
docs.text:
We can open an specific page using the flexygo.nav.openPageName method and indicating the paget name and the entity or collection

TypeScript
 /**
 * Opens a page by its name
 * @method openPageName
 * @param {string} pagename - Identifier of the page
 * @param {string} objectname - Name of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} objectwhere - Where of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} defaults - Defaults to be added to the page
 * @param {string} targetid - Target to open the window
 * @param {boolean} excludeHist - True to not store in history
 * @param {JQuery} triggerElement - Relative element to open the page
 * @param {boolean} isClone -Only for opening page with clone options
 * @param {flexygo.nav.FlexygoHistory} previousHist - Previous page history
 * @param {string} presets - Used for opening page with a default preset, can be a preset ID or a JSON string 
 */

openPageName(pagename: string, objectname: string, objectwhere: string, defaults: string, targetid: string, excludeHist: boolean, triggerElement?: JQuery, isClone?: boolean, previousHist?: flexygo.nav.FlexygoHistory, presets?: string): void

docs.title: Execute process
docs.text:
We can execute any process in the flexygo repository by using the flexygo.nav.execProcess method and indicating the process and the entity or collection.

TypeScript
/**
 * Executes a process, opening its param page if required
 * @method execProcess
 * @param {string} processname - Identifier of the process
 * @param {string} objectname - Name of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} objectwhere - Where of the collection or entity
 * @param {string} defaults - Defaults to be added to the process
 * @param {any} processparams - Array of process parameters
 * @param {string} targetid - Target to open the window
 * @param {boolean} excludeHist - True to not store in history
 * @param {JQuery} triggerElement - Relative element to open the page
 * @param {function} callBack - callback to be called after execute
* @param {boolean} showprogress - false to hide progress indicator
 */

execProcess(processname: string, objectname: string, objectwhere: string, defaults: string | flexygo.nav.PageDefaults, processparams: any, targetid: string, excludeHist: boolean, triggerElement: JQuery, callBack?: any, showProgress?: boolean):void

docs.title: Sample of executing a process with parameters
docs.text:
In this sample we shall translate the content of the MyTextbox property on the current edit form using the The TranslateTextTo process

JavaScript
let module = $(triggerElement).closest('flx-module')[0];
let TextBox =$(module).find("[Property='MyTextbox']")[0];
let qs= TextBox.getValue();
if(qs!=null){
    flexygo.nav.execProcess('TranslateTextTo','sysProcess','',null,[{"key":'Text',"value":qs},{"key":'Lang',"value":'es'}],'current',false,$(this),function (ret){TextBox.setValue(ret.JSCode)})
}

docs.title: Object actions
docs.text:
We can create any entity or collection and execute object actions such as read, insert, update, delete using flexygo.obj.Entity method

JavaScript
/**
* Library to access entity objects and collections from JS.
*
* @class flexygo.Entity
* @constructor
* @param {string} objectName - The object name.
* @param {string} [objectWhere] - Where condition (only if object isn't new).
* @return {object} - Entity object.
*/
var e = flexygo.obj.Entity (objectName, objectWhere);


/* read object info */
e.read();
/* insert */
e.data.PropertyName=newValue;
e.insert();
/* update */
e['PropertyName']=newValue;
e.update();
/* delete */
e.delete();

docs.title: Context Variables
docs.text:
Context variables are the variables which can have different values in different environments. These variables are used to make the code production ready and can be used in solutions as tokens in any Template or SQL Sentence.

Whatch the following video about context variables.

docs.title: Default Tokens
docs.text:
All tokens must be referenced with curly brackets {{ / }}. flexygo includes the following variables by default:

  • {{currentReference}}: Wildcard used for linking other system elements to the current user
  • {{currentSubreference}}: 2º Wildcard used for linking other system elements to the current user
  • {{currentRole}}: Current users role name
  • {{currentRoleId}}: Current users role Id
  • {{currentUserLogin}}: Current users login
  • {{currentUserId}}: Current users Id
  • {{currentUserFullName}}: Current users full name
  • {{currentUserCultureId}}: Current users culture Id
  • {{currentUserLang}}: Current users Language. First two digits of culture Id
  • {{currentUserEmail}}: Current users Email.
  • {{currentDate}}: Current Date.
  • {{currentTime}}: Current Time with minutes precision.
  • {{currentTimeSec}}: Current Time with seconds precision.
  • {{currentDateTime}}: Current Date and Time with minutes precision.
  • {{currentDateTimeSec}}: Current Date and Time with seconds precision.

docs.title: Generate Tokens
docs.text:
Flexygo allows you to generate your own Tokens by using SQL sentences. We shall indicate the Connection string we want to use and wich SQL Sentence using any of the previously generated tokens.

If I have an Employee Table in my data model with an Email and I want to obtain EmployeeID from employee table. We can create a new token called {{EmployeeId}}

SQL
SELECT EmployeeId FROM Employees WHERE Email = '{{currentUserEmail}}'

Now our new {{EmployeeId}} token can be used as a standard variable anywhere in our solution.

Custom control dependencies
docs.text:
Using dependencies for changing type of control of dependent property. You can use dependencies between properties to change the control type of the dependent property. Before creating the dependency you must create one or more custom controls that are the ones that you will assign to the dependent property.

  • Set custom control based on parent property values: You will first choose the values for which the dependent property will change and in the combo choose the corresponding custom control.

  • Set the custom control via sql statement: In this case, it will be the sql statement that will establish the custom control of the dependent property. The sql statement must return the name of the custom control.

docs.title: Custom DLL
docs.text:
In some cases it's necessary to program functionalities which flexygo doesn't have. For this, it's possible to customize our own DLLs. It's necessary:

  1. Create a new C# class library for .NET 9 (net9.0, the same version as the flexygo libraries), for example with dotnet new classlib -f net9.0.

  2. Add a reference to the Flexygo.Library NuGet package, which brings the flexygo libraries (Table 1). Use the same flexygo version as the application:

    XML
    <ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Flexygo.Library" Version="x.x.x" />
</ItemGroup>
Table 1. Some flexygo libraries included in the package flxDataManager flxEntity flxGlobals flxLocalization flxMail flxObjectConfig flxSession flxSettings flxUtilities

  1. See the C# sample code:

    Insert, Update And Delete object function

    Object Process with parameters

    Object Process without parameters

    Collection Process with parameters *

    Collection Process without parameters *

    Load Object or Change Property

    Methods must be public static. flexygo passes each process parameter by name, as well as Entity and Ret.

    Don't forget to configure Unique Identifier in object configuration

  2. Compile the custom DLL and copy it to the custom/bin folder of the Backend (in the process, the file is set as ~/custom/bin/MyLibrary.dll; ~ is the Backend folder).

  3. Configure your process inside flexygo, visualize image (Image 1.)

docs.title: Custom C#
docs.text:
Embedded C# processes serve the same purpose as custom DLL processes.

References to libraries and the code of the process are directly inserted into the flexygo form (Image 2.)

When you save your C# process in flexygo, it is compiled to check for any errors.

To start debugging a C# process:

  1. Turn on the DebugProcesses setting: control panel → Environment area → Settings, System group (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Environment > Settings).
  2. To set a breakpoint at a specific location in your C# code, you can insert: C#
    System.Diagnostics.Debugger.Break();

This will open the generated C# code in Visual Studio, enabling you to debug the process.

docs.title: Custom Stored Procedure
docs.text:
Stored procedure is a collection SQL statements and sql command logic, which is compiled and stored on the database. Stored procedues in SQL allows us to create SQL queries to be stored and executed on the server. The main purpose of stored procedures to hide direct SQL queries from the code and improve performance of database operations such as select, update, and delete data. You can create your own stored procedure. In this article we'll see the difference between object stored procedure and collection stored procedure.

Whatch video about creating stored procedure in flexygo environment:

docs.title: Add stored procedure process into object menu
docs.text:
1. Code stored procedure in database. Example

  2. Add it to flexygo stored procedure repository at the control panel → Logic and rules area → DB Stored Procedures (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Logic and Rules > DB Stored Procedures).

  3. If stored has parameters insert it automatically using Generate parameters menu.

  4. Add relation to object in the control panel → Objects area → Logic (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Object Management > Logic).

docs.title: Add stored procedure process into list menu
docs.text:
1. Set Unique Identifier Field in object configuration to allow collection process.

  2. Code stored procedure in database. Append a param with name @sysCollectionSentence and type nvarchar(max) to recive an SQL with selected items. Example

  3. Add it to flexygo stored procedure repository at the control panel → Logic and rules area → DB Stored Procedures (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Logic and Rules > DB Stored Procedures).

  4. If stored has parameters insert it automatically using Generate parameters menu.

  5. Add relation to collection in the control panel → Objects area → Logic (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Object Management > Logic). If process only can be executed with selected items, please set switch to true, otherwise process will be executed with all items filtered in current screen.

docs.title: Custom Stored on Object Load Or Property Change
docs.text:
To every object or property a Custom Stored can be assigned to get executed when this one is created or changed, for that the Stored will receive an XML with every propertie value, here you have an example on how to use it:

Example

SQL SQL
CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[pPers_LockClient]

        @IdClient int,
        @IdState int, 
        @BlockReason varchar(250),
        @BlockDate smalldatetime

        AS

            BEGIN TRY

            if exists (select * from Client where IdClient = @IdClient and IdState = @IdState ) begin
                RAISERROR( 'Selected client is already blocked.',12,1)
            end

            begin tran  

                    -- Update Client
                    UPDATE Client SET IdState = @IdState, blockReason = @BlockReason, blockDate = @BlockDate                
                    WHERE IdClient = @IdClient

            COMMIT TRAN         
            RETURN -1
        END TRY
        BEGIN CATCH

            IF @@TRANCOUNT >0 BEGIN
                ROLLBACK TRAN 
            END

            print 'The selected client could not be updated. ' + ERROR_MESSAGE()
            RETURN 0

        END CATCH
SQL
CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[pPers_LockClientBatch]
          @IdState int,
          @BlockReason varchar(250),
          @BlockDate smalldatetime,
          @sysCollectionSentence nvarchar(max) --This param has sql sentence with selected items unique identifiers.
          AS

              BEGIN TRY

              begin tran    

                      Declare @Clients Table (IdClient int)
                      INSERT INTO @Clients EXEC sp_executesql @sysCollectionSentence;

                      update C 
                      set IdState=@IdState, BlockReason=@BlockReason, BlockDate=@BlockDate
                      from Client C inner join @Clients Sel on C.IdClient=Sel.IdClient          


              COMMIT TRAN   

              RETURN -1
          END TRY
          BEGIN CATCH

              IF @@TRANCOUNT >0 BEGIN
                  ROLLBACK TRAN 
              END

              declare @Error nvarchar(max) = 'The selected client could not be updated. ' + ERROR_MESSAGE()
              RAISERROR(@Error,12,1)
              RETURN 0

          END CATCH
SQL
--#NAME

CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[SampleLoadProcess]
    @Values AS XML,
        @ContextVars as XML
AS
    DECLARE 
      @PropertyName AS NVARCHAR(50),
      @changeValue AS BIT,
      @newValue AS NVARCHAR(MAX),
      @changeClass AS BIT,
      @newClass AS NVARCHAR(MAX),
      @changeRequired AS BIT,
          @newRequired AS BIT,
          @changeEnabled AS BIT,
          @newEnabled AS BIT,
          @changeVisibility AS BIT,
          @newVisibility AS BIT,
          @changeSQL AS BIT,
          @newSQL AS NVARCHAR(MAX),
          @docu AS NVARCHAR(50) 

    SET @docu = @Values.value('(/Row/Property[@Name=''Docu'']/@Value)[1]', 'nvarchar(50)' )

        SET @PropertyName = 'OriginId'
    SET @changeValue = 1
    SET @newValue = '1'
    SET @changeClass = 1
    SET @newClass = 'box-danger'
    SET @changeRequired = 1
        SET @newRequired = 1
        SET @changeEnabled = 1
        SET @newEnabled = 0
        SET @changeVisibility = 1
        SET @newVisibility = 1
        SET @changeSQL = 1
    SET @newSQL = 'select ObjectName from objects where objectname like ''' + @docu + ''''
