        </div>
        <div class="col-10">
          <h4 class="txt-outstanding">Cristina Aguilera></h4>
          More text here
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
</div>

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
To call a property from the object, collection or view, you need to use curly brackets {{...}}.

Example:

HTML
<span> {{UserName}} </span>

To use the format, we need three parameters. The first we will indicate the property that you want to use, the second we will indicate the type of data and the last parameter that we need is the value that we are going give to format.

HTML
<span> {{ Property | format : values }} </span>

docs.title: Boolean
docs.text:
To add a style, we will first indicate your property, followed by the data type and finally need two parameters to complete the type Boolean (true value, false value).

JavaScript
{{ Property | bool: value true, value false }}

In the next example, we can see as the property CanView applied to the class of the label we can give a style or another. If the value that contains corresponds to true will apply the class text-muted, on the contrary if the value of the property is false, will apply the class txt-danger.

Also we can observe in the proper example, the same functioning for the title of the tag.

Example:

HTML
<i class = "flx-icon icon-eye {{CanView|bool:text-muted,txt-danger}}" title = "{{CanView|bool:Visible,Not Visible}}"></i>

It may be the case that one of the two values is empty, it will take the value by default and will not make changes.

Example:

HTML
<i class = "flx-icon icon-eye {{CanView|bool:,txt-danger}}"></i>
If the value is false then... If the value is true then... If the value is not defined If the value is defined If no value If value If value = false If value = true If value = ' ' If value = 'true' If value = 0 If value = 1 If value = null - If value = 'null' -

docs.title: Decimal
docs.text:
To format the type of data decimal, use the same syntax as in previous examples, to difference of the parameters of value. In this case, we need only one, this value will indicate the number of decimal places that you want to display.

HTML
<span> {{ Property | format : value }} </span>

The code that we see in the example, formats the value returned by the property Number to three decimals.

Example:

HTML
<span> {{Number|decimal:3}} </span>

docs.title: Url
docs.text:
We got with the format type url, parse the paths to the images, icons or addresses with relative paths. Thus, we will not lose the display of the element and avoid taking into account the route at the time of parsing manually. Only it is needed the call to the property and the word url.

HTML
<span> {{ Property | url }} </span>

Bellow, there is an example of call to an image of the property "Avatar" having associated to this address ~/profiles/miFoto.png.

Example:

HTML
<img class = "img-responsive img-circle" src = "{{Avatar| url}}" alt = "profile">

docs.title: String
docs.text: String type format keeps the same syntax we've used so far, it also offers three possibilities of configuration. If you want to display the text returned by the property to lowercase, we will use the following:

docs.title: Lowercase
docs.text:
HTML
<span> {{ Address|string: lower }} </span>

docs.title: Uppercase
docs.text:
HTML
<span> {{ Address|string: upper }} </span>

docs.title: Capitalized / Title case
docs.text:
HTML
<span> {{ Address|string: capitalized }} </span>

docs.title: String length
docs.text:
Finally, offers us to tell you that number of characters we want to show by adding back three points. We have to take into account that the spaces are counts.

HTML
<span> {{ Address|string: 20 }} </span>

If we look at the example, we have set the property Address to show us the first 20 characters: We show an address e...

docs.title: IsNull
docs.text:
IsNull type format sets new value when returned value is empty or null. If the value is not null, it will display the original value.

HTML
<span> {{ Address|isnull: No address }} </span>

It also accepts an optional parameter if we need to change original value.

Example:

HTML
<span> {{ Address|isnull: No address, Address found }} </span>

docs.title: Switch
docs.text:
This type of format, allows us to insert a list of values, must meet one of them with the associated property. But when the property doesn't meet any of the values, the value from Else will be applied directly.

JavaScript
{{ Property | switch: [value1:result1, value2:result2, value3:result3, else:result4] }}

Example:

HTML
<span> {{State|switch:[1:'Receive',2:'Accept',3:'Complete',null:'Outstanding',else:'Closed']}}" ></span>

docs.title: Date Formats
docs.text:
Type format date maintains the same syntax we've used so far, it also offers three possibilities of configuration.

JavaScript
{{UpgradeDate|date:LL}}
JavaScript
moment().format(MMMM Do YYYY, h:mm:ss a); // October 17th 2025, 10:08:03 am
moment().format(dddd);                    // Friday
moment().format(MMM Do YY);               // Oct 17th 25
moment().format(YYYY [escaped] YYYY);     // 2025 escaped 2025
moment().format();                        // 2025-10-17T10:08:03+02:00
JavaScript
moment().format(W);             // 2025-10-17T10:08:03+02:00
moment().format(LT);            // 10:08 AM
moment().format(LTS);           // 10:08:03 AM
moment().format(L);             // 10/17/2025
moment().format(l);             // 10/17/2025
moment().format(LL);            // October 17, 2025
moment().format(ll);            // Oct 17, 2025
moment().format(LLL);           // October 17, 2025 10:08 AM
moment().format(lll);           // Oct 17, 2025 10:08 AM
moment().format(LLLL);          // Friday, October 17, 2025 10:08 AM
moment().format(llll);          // Fri, Oct 17, 2025 10:08 AM

docs.title: From now
From the moment in which it made until now
Translate
docs.text:
We can translate template text using the following syntax:

JavaScript
{{translate|Any text to translate}}

Example:

HTML
<i class = "flx-icon icon-object" title= "{{translate|More info}}"></i>

The translation is taken from the translation table in the template area, if it is not found in the template area, it will try to be localized in the property area.

docs.title: Nested formats
docs.text:
Format strings can be nested inside each other:

Example:

JavaScript
{{State|switch:[1:'{{Receive|bool:{{Cad|string:lower}},No}}',2:'Accept',3:'Complete',null:'Outstanding',else:'Closed']}}

The previous format string with the following values var obj={State: 1, Receive: 1, Cad: 'this is my result'} would produce the following output: "this is my result"

docs.title: File Linking
docs.text:
flexygo has a system to return files in an encrypted link, for this, the field of the view that returns the address of the document must have an alias that begins with one of the following formats:

flxpathimage: Flexygo image management.

flxpathdocument: Flexygo document management.

flxpath|ObjectName|PropertyName: The property configuration of that object is read.

flxpath: Management of images or ERP documents, as long as the document path is complete.

flxpathzoom: Thumbnail image management, can include thumbnail size separated by _, if you do not specify a default size it will be 75x75 [width]x[height].

View:

SQL
SELECT Foto as flxpathzoomEmployee\_120x120 FROM Employees

Template:

HTML
<img src = "{{flxpathzoomEmployee|url}}"/>

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
This tags allows you to render a toolbar in a list or a wiew module, using the object configuration of the module to render the buttons:

JavaScript

docs.title: Navigation button
docs.text: Navigation button, developed such as web component, used to avoid pasting JavaScript in to your HTML markup and keeping the markup clean.

docs.title: Go Home
docs.text:
To go home use:

HTML
<flx-navbutton type="home">
    <button class="btn btn-outstanding">View sample here</button>
</flx-navbutton>

Instead of onclick event with:

JavaScript
flexygo.nav.goHome();

docs.title: Open Page
docs.text:
Edit sample here View sample here List sample here List with preset id sample here List with preset object sample here

To edit an object use:

HTML
<flx-navbutton type="openpage" pagetypeid="edit" objectname="sysHelpItem" objectwhere="(HelpId='{{syshelp-navbutton}}')" defaults="{'Field':'{{value}}','DateField':'{{value|date:YYYY-MM-DD}}'}" targetid="current" excludehist="false"></flx-navbutton>

Instead of onclick event with:

JavaScript
flexygo.nav.openPage('edit','sysHelpItem','(HelpId=\\'syshelp-navbutton\\')','{"Field":"{{value}}","DateField":"{{value|date:YYYY-MM-DD}}"}','current',false,$(this));

To view an object use:

HTML
<flx-navbutton type="openpage" pagetypeid="view" objectname="sysHelpItem" objectwhere="(HelpId='syshelp-navbutton')" defaults="" targetid="popup" excludehist="false">
    <button class="btn btn-outstanding">View sample here</button>
</flx-navbutton>

Instead of onclick event with:

JavaScript
flexygo.nav.openPage('view','sysHelpItem','(HelpId=\\'syshelp-navbutton\\')','null','popup',false,$(this));

</flx-navbutton>

flexygo.nav.openPage('list','sysHelpItems','','null','popup',false,$(this),null,null,'Help\_Offline\_App');

To list a collection with a default preset for a module use:

docs.title: Object Templates
docs.text: Flexygo modules like lists or views normally include a change template button . This button allows us to switch different forms of displaying the module allowing each user to establish which view is best for him setting this one such as default template. Each view for each module is memorized just by selecting it.

docs.title: List Templates
docs.text:
The List module template button displays elements in the following way:

  1. Defined List Type Templates
  2. Defined Object Data Views with the Display as Grid check enabled

When a List module is loaded the displayed template will follow this sequence:

  1. Last template displayed by current user
  2. List template marked as default
  3. Data view marked as default
  4. Data view marked as show as grid

docs.title: View Templates
docs.text:
The List module template button displays elements in the following way:

  1. Defined View Type Templates
  2. Defined Edit Form in a view mode

When a View module is loaded, the displayed template will follow this sequence:

  1. Last template displayed by current user
  2. View template marked as default
  3. View form based on Edit design

docs.title: Edit Templates
docs.text:
The List module template button displays elements in the following way:

  1. Defined Edit Type Templates
  2. Default Edit Form

When an Edit module is loaded the displayed template will follow this sequence:

  1. Last template displayed by current user
  2. Edit template marked as default
  3. Edit form based on Edit design

docs.title: Special Template Tokens
docs.text:
Templates can also include specific strings for displaying diferent types of buttons:

  • {{objectmenu}}: To display the complete object menu
  • {{processmenu}}: To display only the object process menu
  • {{reportmenu}}: To display only the object report menu
  • {{deletebutton}}: To the object delete button
  • {{viewbutton}}: To the object view button
  • {{editbutton}}: To the object edit button
  • {{newbutton}}: To the object new button
  • {{bagbutton}}: To display the bag button on the elements of a collection (list)

docs.text:
Sometimes you need to nest templates for a more complex display:

docs.title: Skeletons
docs.text:
When loading a module is always good to show the user that something is happening, so that's where skeletons take place.

Skeletons are basic html structures that will show while the module is loading, instead of leaving blank modules. They can be added to every module, where an standard one can be used or a new one can be created.

The most common module types (flx-list, flx-edit, flx-view, flx-moduletab and flx-buttontab) have got an standard skeleton set, but it can be overwritten by setting to your desired module the skeleton you want to show.

docs.title: How to create your own skeleton
docs.text:
Adding a custom skeleton is as easy as opening Skeletons in the Environment area of the control panel (in the flexy2022 skin: Admin Work Area > Environment > Skeletons) and adding a new one to the list.

Skeleton may divide in three parts (skeletonHeader, skeletonBody, skeletonFooter) this is do to the necesity of showing or not certain elements depending if it's the module first load or if it's a refresh. For flexygo to know which part it is, it will be needed to encapsulate skeleton with divs containing the classes (skeletonHeader, skeletonBody, skeletonFooter), as in the following example.

Example:

HTML
<div class="skeletonHeader">
    <div> My Skeleton Header </div>
</div>

<div class="skeletonBody">
    <div> My Skeleton Body </div>
</div>

<div class="skeletonFooter">
    <div> My Skeleton Footer </div>
</div>

Once stablished the skeleton html you could add an image to the skeleton so when searching through the skeletons list is easier to find, but is not compulsory.

docs.title: Using Flexygo skeleton effect
docs.text:
Flexygo skeletons use an animation to show the user that the app is still running properly. Using this animation is as easy as using the classes skeletonElementContainer and skeletonElement as shown in this example.

Example:

HTML
<div class="skeletonElementContainer">
    <div class="skeletonElement"></div>
</div>

docs.title: Data handling in Flexygo AI
docs.text: In Flexygo, AHORA's tool, advanced artificial intelligence systems have been implemented to optimize the management and retrieval of information. Among these, the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and SQL Live Data systems stand out, both designed to enable smart interaction with the data stored in the tool. Both systems guarantee privacy and confidentiality, keeping the data under strict control within Flexygo's private environment.

docs.title: How the RAG system works
docs.text:
The RAG system in Flexygo lets you manage and query information from documents previously uploaded to the system through the following steps:

  • Document upload: users upload documents directly into the Flexygo tool. Only PDF, TXT and DOCX (Word) documents are supported for processing through the RAG system.
  • Document vectorization: documents are automatically split into manageable chunks (generally paragraphs). These specific chunks are sent individually to the OpenAI API, which converts the text into numeric vectors capable of capturing the semantic meaning of the text, making later similarity searches possible. It's worth noting that OpenAI does not have full or public access to the document, only to specific chunks.
  • Storage in SQL Server: the vectorized chunks are stored exclusively in a SQL Server database owned by Flexygo, ensuring efficient and secure access.
  • Interaction through chat: when queries are made in the chat, they are also vectorized through the OpenAI API. The system compares the vectorized query against the stored chunks, sending only the relevant chunks as specific context to generate the responses.

docs.title: How the SQL Live Data system works
docs.text:
The SQL Live Data system lets the chat generate responses from direct database queries using T-SQL statements generated by OpenAI. This works as follows:

  • Secure query generation: the OpenAI API does not have real or direct access to the database. Instead, it creates specific T-SQL queries that are then executed in Flexygo.
  • Privacy in queries: the queries generated by OpenAI are strictly read-only, making it impossible to modify the database. Only the specific, limited results of those queries are sent to the chat, guaranteeing privacy. These isolated results lack full context, which further increases data protection — for example, providing only an isolated value like "32" with no additional context. Users can also view the queries executed by the chat, ensuring transparency and trust in the process.

docs.title: AI assistants connected through MCP 10.0+
docs.text:
Starting with version 10, Flexygo includes an MCP server so each user can connect their own AI assistant, for example Claude or ChatGPT. In this case the data doesn't go through OpenAI: query results are sent to the assistant the user connects, and are handled under its provider's privacy policy.

  • Disabled by default: the administrator enables MCP in Administration > Security > WebAPI and grants the permission to the authorized users or roles.
  • With the user's permissions: the assistant only sees and does what the user who connects it can do. When connecting it, the user decides whether it will have read-only access or can also modify data.
  • Under the user's control: from Connected assistants, in the profile menu, they can review the connections and disconnect them.

See AI assistants connected to the application (MCP).

docs.title: OpenAI's privacy policy
docs.text: All communication and data sent to the OpenAI API from Flexygo is carried out in accordance with OpenAI's privacy policy.

docs.title: Error connecting to the WebApi from the Offline App on Android 12/13 devices
Error connecting to the WebApi from the Offline App on Android 12/13 devices
docs.text: After renewing/updating the Sectigo certificate, it becomes impossible to access the Offline App from these devices because the certificate is not recognized on them.

docs.title: Steps to follow on the IIS server where the certificate is installed
docs.text:
The solution is to add the R46 certificate to the "Untrusted Certificates" store and install a "cross-signed certificate":

  1. Export "Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46" from the Trusted Root Certification Authorities store and save the certificate file

  2. Remove it from the Trusted Root Certification Authorities store

  3. Import it into "Untrusted Certificates"

In addition, the "cross-signed certificate" must be added to the Third-Party Root Certification Authorities store

Once this is done, verify that access to the Offline App from the older devices works correctly.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text: Download the Sectigo-RSA-Domain-Validation-CA-Bundle.pem file containing the cross-signed certificate mentioned in step 3.

docs.title: Before opening a ticket
docs.text:
Before opening a support ticket, keep the following recommendations in mind:

  1. Make sure your software is up to date. Test on the latest beta version of Flexygo to avoid delays on issues that are already fixed.

  2. Check the help's frequently asked questions. Your problem may already be solved in the More information → FAQ section of this help.

  3. Gather all the information needed to reproduce the problem. Document the steps precisely and state whether the error happens every time or only occasionally.

    • Bad example: "I can't save invoices"
    • Good example: "Saving the Invoices object shows the error 'binary string would be truncated'. Reproducible by opening the Invoices edit screen with IdFactura = 25 from the left-hand panel in the Clients menu"

  4. Provide visual evidence. Screenshots or videos speed up reproducing and resolving the error.

  5. Include environment details. Browser type, operating system version, mobile device, configured language, connection speed and any other relevant context.

  6. Summarize your project's context. Explain what you're building, since Flexygo supports countless different solutions and the guidance you get may depend on a different screen approach.

  7. One issue per ticket. Including several questions in the same ticket affects response times and service quality, since each issue is assigned to a specific professional.

  8. Account for system limitations. Virtual machines with insufficient resources, database limitations (SQL Express: 1 GB of memory per instance, a single processor), or server overload.

docs.title: Example of a return callback for a combo with the allow-new button
Example of a return callback for a combo with the allow-new button
docs.text:
When configuring a combo where we want to let the user add new elements, by default we'll set the object to create and the return field that will be assigned to the combo after the new element is created.

In some cases we'll need, for example, to assign default values to the object so that when the new object's window opens it already has those values set. In these cases we can program a function that performs those assignments and, on its return, also adds the value to the combo.

It's best to save this function in a .js file inside the custom folder and upload it as a plugin, so it will load as one more function of the application and be available at any time.

Once the function is written and added, we need to specify it in the Allow New Return Function section.

docs.title: Practical example
docs.text:
We attach an example where, from a customer's record, we give the option to create and assign a direct debit; so when the direct debit opens, it will already inherit the customer's id.

The call to the function would look like this (*):

Text Only
newCustomerDirectDebit({{CustomerId}});

* If the value is text, it must be wrapped in quotes:

Text Only
newCustomerDirectDebit('{{CustomerId}}');

docs.title: Example code
Using DataManager in library processes
docs.text: The DataManager object lets you query and execute SQL statements against Flexygo's databases. It's recommended to instantiate it with the session's security context using information from the ProcessHelper object.

docs.title: Instantiation
GetValue
docs.text:
Gets a single value from a SQL query:

C#
int ne = Convert.ToInt32(dm.GetValue("SELECT Max(IdEjercicio)+1 As NewEjercicio FROM Conta_Ejercicios", "NewEjercicio"));

docs.title: DataTable
docs.text:
Queries and iterates over record sets:

C#
DataTable dt = dmData.DataTable("Select script as field1, field2 from table");
foreach (DataRow row in dt.Rows)
{
    // Process each row
}

Includes transactional control:

  • dmData.BeginTrans() — starts a transaction
  • dmData.CommitTrans() — commits changes
  • dmData.RollbackTrans() — rolls back changes

docs.title: ExecuteSql
docs.text:
Executes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE SQL statements:

C#
string sql = "Insert into table (f1, f2, f3, f4) Values ('1','2',3,'4')";
Entity.DataManager.ExecuteSql(sql);

docs.title: ExecuteStored
docs.text:
Executes stored procedures with parameters:

C#
BaseCollection parameters = new BaseCollection();
parameters.Add("IdEjercicio1", idEjercicio);
parameters.Add("IdEjercicio2", ne);

if (dm.ExecuteStored("Ejercicios_Trasvase", parameters))
{
    // Success: OUTPUT parameters updated in the collection
}

docs.title: ExecuteStoredResult
docs.text:
Executes stored procedures that return result sets:

C#
DataSet ds = null;
if (!dm.ExecuteStoredResult("_testdata", parameters, ref ds, "Cli,Emp"))
{
    throw new InvalidOperationException("Error", dm.LastException);
}

docs.title: How do I decrypt and re-encrypt the configuration?
How do I decrypt and re-encrypt the configuration?
docs.text:
For security, Flexygo keeps the connection strings, the mail password and other keys of its configuration encrypted. They live in the appsettings files of the conf folder of the Backend and the Frontend, and they are encrypted value by value: the rest of the file stays readable.

  • Which files: only appsettings.json and appsettings.Production.json. The others (appsettings.Development.json…) always stay in plain text.
  • Where: in IIS and in production Docker containers. Anywhere else (development, Kestrel, the installer's test Docker) the application decrypts them when it starts.
  • The key: on Windows there is one per server (%ProgramData%\Flexygo\keys\config.key), shared by every application on the server. To move an application to another server, config export-key on the source and config import-key on the destination.
  • Docker: in production the key is given as the secret flexygo_config_key, the same one for every container. If the secret's file is missing, the application does not start and says why.

docs.title: Changing a connection string, the mail account or another key
docs.text:
1. In the application's folder, from an administrator console, decrypt the configuration:

    Text Only
    Flexygo.Backend.exe config decrypt

    (or Flexygo.Frontend.exe config decrypt for the Frontend).

  2. Edit the value in appsettings.json: the connection string under ConnectionStrings, the mail account under MailSettings.

  3. Encrypt the configuration again:

    Text Only
    Flexygo.Backend.exe config encrypt

    (or Flexygo.Frontend.exe config encrypt for the Frontend).

  4. Restart the application (in IIS, recycle the pool) so it reads the new value. If you skip step 3, the application encrypts whatever is left in plain text when it starts.

config status says where the key is and what each file holds encrypted.

All the detail (the console, losing the key, updating, moving servers and Docker) is in Encrypted appsettings.

docs.title: I've generated a DLL and Flexygo doesn't recognize it
I've generated a DLL and Flexygo doesn't recognize it
docs.text: When setting up the parameters for the function whose process we want to add to the Flexygo environment, we get an error saying the DLL can't be loaded because its format isn't recognized.

docs.title: Check the framework and the location
docs.text:
Starting with version 10, processes run in the Backend, which runs on .NET 9. The DLL must be built for .NET 9 (<TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework> in the .csproj). A DLL built for .NET Framework doesn't load, whether it's built as AnyCPU or x86.

Copy the DLL to the Backend folder. In the process's file path, ~ is the Backend folder (for example, ~/bin/MyLibrary.dll); if the DLL isn't in bin, Flexygo looks for it in the root of that folder.

docs.title: Check the platform
docs.text:
Another possible reason is that it wasn't compiled for all CPUs: it was built as x86 (32-bit), while Flexygo's application pool is configured as incompatible with 32-bit.

There is a tool, sigcheck.exe, that gives us that information.

docs.text: The solution is to recompile the DLL in the right format, i.e. AnyCPU instead of x86:

docs.title: What should I take into account for document management?
What should I take into account for document management?
docs.text: For document management to work correctly, there are several aspects to keep in mind.

docs.title: 1. Custom storage paths
docs.text:
If we want images or files to be saved in a PATH different from the project's own, we need to configure DocumentPath, ImagePath and the Impersonate parameters:

To modify these values, go to Design area → Environment → Parameters → Edit.

docs.title: 2. IIS user permissions
docs.text: The IIS user needs read and write permissions on the folders that document management needs to access.

docs.title: 3. Available configuration types
docs.text:
In the document management configuration we can choose between two types of setup:

  • If we choose Ahora Freeware ERP, our document management will link to the ERP's document management; to do this we'll need to specify the ERP object it links to and that object's key.
  • If we choose Flexygo standard, our document management will be stored at the project's default path in Flexygo (e.g. ~\Custom\Documentos).

docs.title: 4. Filtering limitations
docs.text: If two levels of filtering are needed to display it, keep in mind that document management can't filter by the same field twice. To achieve this, you need to create a new field that concatenates both values — this becomes the field that document and image management relate on — or add an identity field to the main table.

docs.title: I'm updating the version and I get a Foreign Key conflict error
I'm updating the version and I get a Foreign Key conflict error
docs.text:
If an update shows an error similar to this one:

The problem is that records have been added to new Flexygo objects (objects, views, modules, pages...) with the wrong OriginId — meaning certain customizations were marked as system or product by mistake (usually from copy-pasting). As a result, the system won't add them during merges, and it will throw errors in other related tables.

The CambiarOriginId.sql script, available from Developing: script to change the OriginId of all our modifications, reports every record whose origin is marked as system or product but should be marked as customer.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: The solution is to modify those records and change their OriginId, usually changing 0 or 1 to 2.

docs.title: Data update algorithm in mobile applications
Data update algorithm in mobile applications
docs.text: This article details the data synchronization process in Flexygo mobile applications, through a specific algorithm for receiving and updating information.

docs.title: Algorithm steps
docs.text:
1. Initial download: configuration of objects, views, menus, properties and templates.
  2. Creating temporary tables: generated with the temp_ prefix and including control fields: _isInserted, _isUpdated, _isDeleted, _syncDate, _insertDate, _updatedDate, _deletedDate.
  3. Data download: processed across multiple execution threads.
  4. Unified transaction: compares the previous structures and runs the following operations:
    • Removes obsolete tables
    • Renames the new tables (removing the temp_ prefix)
    • Processes matching tables according to the mode

docs.title: A) Refresh data
docs.text:
• Validates changes in the primary key
  • Marks records as deleted
  • Inserts new records
  • Updates matching fields
  • Finishes by renaming the tables

docs.title: B) Overwrite data
docs.text:
• Removes the old tables
  • Renames the new ones (without the temp_ prefix)

docs.title: Developing: script to change the OriginId of all our modifications
Developing: script to change the OriginId of all our modifications
Scope
docs.text: Development environment of a project/solution/product.

docs.title: Situation
docs.text:
We've made changes to our development without marking the origin of the modifications.

Note

To change our origin, we go to the object collection, where there is a process from which we can change the origin. This setting means every record will be marked with the new origin (system, product, project or user).

This means that when we want to script our changes, we'll have trouble locating and saving them.

The solution is to locate and update the records that have an OriginId other than the one we want.

To do this, we'll run the attached script, which gives us the updates needed to leave the records correctly set.

The code is set up to go from origin "Project" (id 2) to origin "Product" (1), but it can be changed by assigning different origins to the following variables:

SQL
set @OldOriginId=2
set @NewOriginId=1

After that, we can run zscript, which will generate the SQL change files for our application/product.

Example:

Text Only
zscript 1, 'C:\Codigo GIT\Flexygo\flexygo\BBDD\FLEXIGOBD\FLEXIGOBD\scripts\staticdata '

docs.title: Attachment
docs.text: Download CambiarOriginId.sql.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• How the OriginId works in 4 steps
  • I'm updating the version and I get a Foreign Key conflict error

docs.title: How the OriginId works in 4 steps
How the OriginId works in 4 steps
Step 1: Identifying the record's owner
docs.text:
The OriginId indicates who owns a record during updates:

  • OriginId 0: new records from Flexygo's own developers
  • OriginId 1: new records from product developers
  • OriginId 2: new records created during customization or deployment

docs.title: Step 2: OriginId is immutable
docs.text: The OriginId of an existing record in the tool or product is never modified. Other fields can be changed regardless of the owner, but the OriginId never is.

docs.title: Step 3: Comparative update logic
docs.text:
During updates, the system compares fields between versions:

New version? Customization? Action No No The previous value is kept Yes No It's updated No Yes The customization is kept Yes Yes It's updated, but a conflict is generated*

* There are configured exceptions where the customization takes priority: property labels, standard languages, logos, variable colors, template bodies, node order, and scheduled job states.

docs.title: Step 4: Managing deletions
docs.text: If a record with OriginId 0 or 1 is deleted in a deployment but isn't also deleted from the tool or product, that record will be reinserted. It's recommended to disable records instead of deleting them.

docs.title: How to do a partial synchronization in Flexygo Offline
How to do a partial synchronization in Flexygo Offline
docs.text:
By default, the Flexygo Offline app sends all the records of tables that have any of the change bits active, as indicated by the _isInserted, _isDeleted, _isUpdated fields. And when a data refresh is done, it's performed for the entire model.

Sometimes it may be necessary to do a custom data send or receive, i.e. specifying exactly which tables you want to synchronize at a given moment. To do this, you need to create a JS function like any of the functions and examples described below.

docs.title: Get data from server without overwriting modified rows
docs.text:
• {boolean} reloadPage
  • {string} jscode
  • {SyncOptions} options
    • {boolean} partialSync?: if true, only gets the tables and views in the syncTables/syncViews array
    • {Array<string>} syncTables?: list of tables to get
    • {Array<string>} syncViews: list of views to get
    • {boolean} partialSend?: if true, only sends the tables and views in the syncTables/syncViews array
    • {Array<string>} sendTables?: list of tables to send
    • {Array<string>} sendViews?: list of views to send
JavaScript
flexygo.sync.syncData(reloadPage, jscode, options);

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A partial synchronization is performed on only the Partes, Conf_Partes, Clientes_Datos and Contactos tables:

JavaScript
Recibir = async function(){

    let opts = {
      partialSync: true,
      syncTables: [],
      syncViews: []
    };

    opts.syncTables.push('Partes');

    opts.syncTables.push('Conf_Partes');

    opts.syncTables.push('Clientes_Datos');

    opts.syncTables.push('Contactos');

    flexygo.sync.syncData(true, "", opts);

  }

docs.title: Get data from server overwriting modified rows
docs.text:
• {boolean} reloadPage

docs.title: Security recommendations
docs.text: Security in Flexygo is based on three fundamental steps.

docs.title: Step 1: HTTPS and SSL certificates
docs.text:
The key to most of this is having a secure address for the application (https://), by installing a paid certificate for the domain. This allows you to:

  • Disable HTTP and use only HTTPS
  • Encrypt communications between client and server
  • Protect passwords and shared documents

docs.title: Step 2: password management
docs.text: Flexygo implements automatic protection mechanisms, including locking after five failed attempts and configuring complexity parameters.

docs.title: Step 3: security audit
docs.text: For customers with special requirements, a full audit is recommended covering: firewalls, communications, operating system versions and antivirus.

docs.title: Security measures built into Flexygo
docs.text:
• Static code analysis
  • Security testing (ethical hacking)
  • Heuristic blocking using white/grey lists
  • Sentinel Agent for forensic auditing
  • Continuous deployment
  • Audit log of user actions

Important

You should never guarantee to your customer that your system is 100% secure, since it isn't — not with Flexygo, nor with anything else.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Secure Configuration Guide
  • Minimum requirements

docs.title: Sending a standard VCalendar from a library process
Sending a standard VCalendar from a library process
docs.text:
Flexygo has a function you can call from library processes that sends an email with a vCalendar attachment.

You need to fill in the corresponding parameters and pass them to the FLEXYGO.Vcalendar function.

C#
public Vcalendar(DateTime aStartDate, DateTime aEnddate, string aLocation, string aOrganizerName, string aOrganizerEmail, string aSummary, string aSubject, string aAttendeeEmail, string aguid, string aBody = "", bool aReminder = false, bool aDefaultBodyText = true, dynamic aReminderDate = null)

Example showing the instance and call to then send the email:

C#
var vcal = new FLEXYGO.Vcalendar(pStartDate, pEndDate, pLocation, pCreatedByName, pEmail, pObservations, pSubject, pEmail, pCalendarIdentificator, pBodyTextMail);

vcal.Send();

If the user sending it has an associated mail account, that account will be used. Otherwise, the default sending account defined in the system will be used.

The system account is the one entered in the Outgoing mail step of the configuration wizard, and it's stored in the MailSettings section of the Backend's appsettings.json.

docs.title: Where do I start?
docs.text:
If you've already installed Flexygo, take a look at this playlist, which shows you step by step how to get started with your first Flexygo projects.

You can find this short online course on YouTube.

If you'd rather, you can also take the course on Udemy.

And don't hesitate to contact us if you have any questions or issues.

docs.title: Version 10.0
docs.text: Flexygo 10.0 moves to .NET 9, introduces the Flexygo 2026 skin and puts artificial intelligence to work with you. Installing, updating and exporting your projects is also simpler.

docs.title: Flexygo on .NET 9
docs.text:
Flexygo runs on .NET 9. The interface, the backend and the database can run on the same server or on different ones, on IIS, as a service or in Docker, on both Windows and Linux.

More information: Flexygo architecture

docs.title: Setup wizard
docs.text:
The first time you open a new installation, a wizard on the login page takes you through the connection, the databases, the project and the mail. It checks every value before saving it and, if you leave, you continue where you left off.

More information: configuration wizard

docs.title: The Flexygo 2026 skin
docs.text:
A complete redesign of the application, with a side bar that groups the menus and can be collapsed, new typography and controls, and light, dark or system themes. The previous skin is still available.

More information: Flexygo 2026 skin

docs.title: Icon browser
docs.text:
Search more than 5,000 icons, preview them and copy them. Administrators can add their own SVGs and generate the font of the project's icon libraries.

More information: icons

docs.title: AI assistants through MCP
docs.text:
Connect Claude or ChatGPT to Flexygo to query your data and, if you allow it, change records and run processes. Always with the user's permissions, and the user decides whether the access is read-only.

More information: AI assistants

docs.title: A renewed updater
docs.text:
A wizard installs, reverts or switches versions: it checks the requirements and the locks, shows the progress and the result of each step, and rolls back if something fails.

More information: update flow

docs.title: Export your project as a product
docs.text:
Turn the installed application into a product project: choose what it includes and its template, follow the progress and download a ZIP ready to open in Visual Studio.

More information: export a project

docs.title: Build products by talking
docs.text:
Tell an AI assistant connected to the Flexygo MCP what application you need: it gathers the requirements, proposes the design and builds it with you. A board brings together the tasks, the decisions and the quality checks.

More information: MCP workflow

  • Deployment: The container recognizes the configuration database even if the capitalization changes.

docs.title: Fixes

See the fixes in this version

  • Login: signing in works without an alias and after resetting the password, and the after-login process runs only once.
  • Lists and filters: deleting the last row shows the last page; filters work with empty values and with their dependencies.
  • Forms: decimal and boolean values, the barcode control and closing dialogs on delete are fixed.
  • Documents and images: downloads and file names are right through the proxy and with external folders.
  • Processes: C# code processes, the Excel import, Redsys and restarting failed jobs are fixed.
  • Artificial intelligence: vector searches, ChatGPT requests and the layout on different screen sizes are fixed.
  • Interface: layout details in the kanban board, the calendars, dark mode and the module grid are fixed.
  • Notifications and conversations: mentions notify again and the sound no longer repeats when many notifications arrive at once.
  • Security: New product installations assign the 2026admin profile to the administrator.

docs.title: Did you know you can enable RAG functionality on an AI agent?
Did you know you can enable RAG functionality on an AI agent?
docs.text:
To enable RAG functionality on your agent, go to its configuration and enable the Can Use RAG option. Then, in the assistant step called Knowledge Base, you can attach one or more RAG configurations containing the documents the agent will interpret.

Once configured correctly, you will be able to query the agent about the information contained in those documents.

docs.title: Did you know you can use AI in the Flexygo app?
Did you know you can use AI in the Flexygo app?
docs.text: If your Flexygo instance has an AI assistant configured, you can access it directly from the mobile application, as long as you have an internet connection.

docs.title: Technical implementation
docs.text: To enable this feature, use the JavaScript function flexygo.nav.goAI, passing the assistant's identifier as a parameter. This instruction will automatically navigate to a dedicated screen where you can interact with the AI assistant.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• An AI assistant configured in your Flexygo instance
  • An active internet connection on the mobile device

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can autocomplete any text?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can autocomplete any text?
docs.text:
Flexygo offers an AI-powered autocomplete capability. To use it, you need to select the desired agent in the property's configuration.

With this feature enabled, the AI can assist with various tasks such as:

  • Writing news content
  • Drafting emails
  • Reviewing code
  • Other custom functionality

The system uses the form's fields that trigger the autocomplete capability as its basis, generating contextualized text based on the data available in the form.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can create objects for you?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can create objects for you?
docs.text: Flexygo's AI assistant can create new objects based on a specific table. For example, you can ask the assistant: "Create the object for the Customers table".

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Functionality based on natural-language commands
  • Automatic generation of objects from existing tables

docs.title: Did you know you can set default prompts on an AI agent?
Did you know you can set default prompts on an AI agent?
docs.text:
From your agent's configuration, in the section called Prompts, you can set default instructions. This feature makes it easier for users to provide information to the agent.

The goal is to simplify the initial interaction, letting you define in advance what kind of data or context the agent should request or consider by default.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can explain a SQL query to you?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can explain a SQL query to you?
docs.text: If your agent is able to run queries against the database, you can ask it to explain any query to make it easier to understand.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can generate your data model?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can generate your data model?
docs.text: From the wizard for creating a new object, you can select the Create data model button. Using this option, the AI assistant called Aitor "Lowdy" can help you generate the scripts needed for your data model according to your specific requirements.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Automatic generation of table structures (for example, a Customers table and its related Contacts)
  • Creation of scripts with sample data
  • Option to create objects from the tables after running the scripts

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can search for information on Google?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can search for information on Google?
docs.text: From the agent's configuration, you can enable the Can access Web option to allow real-time automatic Google searches.

docs.title: Key feature
docs.text: Once this setting is enabled, users can ask the agent to run web queries. An example: "Search Google for information about Flexygo".

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can insert records for an object?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can insert records for an object?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you automate record creation through its AI functionality. To enable this feature, two configurations are required:

  1. In the agent's configuration: enable the Can call processes option
  2. In the assistant's "Flow Processing" step: select which object and properties your agent can insert

For example, with these settings enabled you can ask your assistant to register a location.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI lets you query data without knowing SQL?
Did you know Flexygo's AI lets you query data without knowing SQL?
docs.text: You can use Flexygo's AI functionality to access data without needing to know SQL.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
To implement this feature, you must:

  1. Go to the agent's configuration
  2. Enable the Can Access DB option
  3. Define which tables and fields the user will have access to

Once configured, the agent will be able to answer questions by automatically querying those tables in real time.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's AI can run processes from a conversation?
Did you know Flexygo's AI can run processes from a conversation?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you automate process execution through conversations with AI.

docs.title: Configuration instructions
docs.text:
Go to your agent's settings and enable Can Call Processes to link the Flexygo processes you want to run from conversations.

This feature enables interactions such as asking the agent "Create a customer named Ahora with phone 666 666 666", and the system will register it automatically.

docs.title: Did you know you can set usage limits for Flexygo's AI assistants?
Did you know you can set usage limits for Flexygo's AI assistants?
docs.text:
From the agent list you can limit users' token usage for AI assistants by role. This feature lets administrators manage and control users' token spend according to their role within the system.

Flexygo lets you set consumption restrictions for AI assistants' tokens. These limits are configured at the user role level, providing granular control over resource and budget usage.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Restricting token usage limits helps organizations to:

  • Control the spend associated with AI assistants
  • Manage resource consumption per user
  • Implement usage policies based on organizational role

docs.title: Did you know you can see the monthly token usage for Flexygo's AI assistants?
Did you know you can see the monthly token usage for Flexygo's AI assistants?
docs.text:
From the agent list you can review the monthly token usage for AI assistants, broken down by user. This feature lets administrators monitor and control the resource spend associated with using AI assistants.

The Flexygo platform lets you view token consumption metrics on a monthly basis, making it easier to manage and oversee the use of AI tools at the individual user level.

docs.title: Did you know you can attach an AI agent to a Flexygo toolbar?
Did you know you can attach an AI agent to a Flexygo toolbar?
docs.text:
To integrate an AI agent into a Flexygo toolbar, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the toolbar where you want to add the agent
  2. Create a new button of the corresponding type
  3. Select the agent you want to launch
  4. Confirm the configuration

Once this process is complete, you will be able to access, from that module, an agent capable of:

  • Running processes
  • Querying the database
  • Searching the internet
  • Accessing your document management (if configured to do so)

docs.title: Did you know you can talk directly to the app's AI?
Did you know you can talk directly to the app's AI?
docs.text:
In addition to the flexygo.nav.goAI function available in the Flexygo application, there is an additional function called flexygo.ai.startVoiceRecognition.

This function only requires you to specify the assistant's identifier. Once enabled, it shows a modal that starts listening to what the user says. Once the audio capture is finished, the message is automatically sent to the AI assistant so it can provide its response.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo's API can accept collections?
Did you know Flexygo's API can accept collections?
docs.text:
Flexygo's API has a notable capability: it can process multiple records at once. When an array of objects is sent instead of a single object, the system tries to insert each item independently.

An important safety feature is that if a problem arises during the process, the API will have tried to insert each of them independently. If any problem occurs, it will roll back all the changes made, guaranteeing data integrity.

This transactional behavior protects the database against partial inserts, ensuring that either every operation completes successfully, or none of them are applied.

docs.title: Did you know you can make Flexygo's searches accent-insensitive?
Did you know you can make Flexygo's searches accent-insensitive?
docs.text: Flexygo has a setting called SearchDbCollation that lets you customize how searches are performed on the platform.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: Without any additional configuration, the system uses its default behavior. However, administrators can set specific values such as Modern_Spanish_CI_AI to change the search behavior.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
By enabling this setting with a case- and accent-insensitive collation, users can:

  • Search without worrying about capitalization
  • Skip accented characters during searches
  • Find results regardless of how the information was originally recorded

This feature applies to search screens and combo fields throughout the application.

docs.title: Did you know pressing ALT lets you view property names?
Did you know pressing ALT lets you view property names?
docs.text: You can quickly view the actual names of properties while configuring them for an object in the wizard.

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: To view property names, hover the cursor over any property's label and hold down the ALT key. This action will automatically reveal the properties' actual identifiers instead of their descriptions or visible labels.

docs.title: Did you know you can link Flexygo to a BI tool or any other system very easily?
Did you know you can link Flexygo to a BI tool or any other system very easily?
docs.text: Linking Flexygo with Business Intelligence tools or external systems is a straightforward process.

docs.title: Main steps
docs.text:
1. Enable Friendly URLs on the objects you want to link, using the corresponding checkbox
  2. Generate links with the format: Text Only
    https://crm.myflexygo.com/view/crm_cliente/25
  3. Simple integration: generate these links from any software and open them in the browser

docs.title: Additional information
docs.text: For more information, with every access possibility, check the built-in help at Help → Information → Friendly Urls.

docs.title: Did you know there's a parameter to set the browser window's title pattern?
Did you know there's a parameter to set the browser window's title pattern?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.x, Flexygo offers a new setting called WindowsNameStructure that lets you customize the browser window's title using specific patterns. The title updates by itself as you move around the application.

docs.title: Available placeholders
docs.text:
The setting accepts the following variables:

  • {{ObjectDescrip}}: shows the object's description, if it exists
  • {{PageDescrip}}: shows the object's description or, failing that, the page's description
  • {{ProjectName}}: shows the project's name

docs.title: Benefit
docs.text: This feature lets you change browser window titles to provide more relevant and contextual information about their content, improving the user experience and navigation within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Did you know you can change how many records at a time the app fetches for an object?
Did you know you can change how many records at a time the app fetches for an object?
docs.text: From an object's configuration, you can adjust the number of records retrieved during synchronization. This parameter, called the buffer size, has a direct impact on the process's performance.

docs.title: Changing the buffer size
docs.text:
To make the adjustment, you just need to modify the property called buffer size. The benefits vary depending on the configuration:

  • Larger buffers: allow faster synchronization by processing multiple records per iteration
  • Smaller buffers: recommended for tables with large or complex records

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text: Best practice suggests using a smaller buffer size when working with tables that contain heavy or complex records, avoiding errors or performance issues. In contrast, for lighter tables, a larger size can be used to optimize synchronization speed without risking overload.

docs.title: Did you know you can mention other users in the chatter?
Did you know you can mention other users in the chatter?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.11.0.x, users can mention other application participants in the chatter using the @ symbol.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: This lets you insert references to other users by typing "@" followed by the user's name in the chatter. When someone is mentioned this way, the system automatically sends a notification alert to the referenced user.

docs.title: Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the Cl@ve system as an authentication method?
Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the Cl@ve system as an authentication method?
docs.text:
Starting with Flexygo version 6.5, administrators can implement the Cl@ve system as an authentication method. This feature pursues two main goals:

  • Speeding up user access
  • Strengthening security measures

docs.title: Implementation instructions
docs.text:
For the technical details on how to implement this feature, check Flexygo's built-in documentation at:

Help → Connectors → Cl@ve Authentication

docs.title: Did you know you can clone an object's dependencies into the collection's?
Did you know you can clone an object's dependencies into the collection's?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.12.0.X, a feature has been implemented that lets you clone an object's dependencies into the collection.

docs.title: Accessing the feature
docs.text: The feature is accessed through a button added to the edit grid's configuration. Enabling it shows an option to decide the cloning behavior.

docs.title: Available options
docs.text:
• Overwrite the existing dependencies in the edit grid
  • Keep the existing dependencies unchanged, only adding the ones that don't already exist

This feature optimizes the workflow by letting you reuse dependency configurations flexibly, giving you full control over whether previous configurations are replaced or kept intact.

docs.title: Did you know you can clone an object based on another object?
Did you know you can clone an object based on another object?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.x, you can duplicate objects along with their main configurations: properties, dependencies, relations, presets, views and templates.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Go to the object you want to duplicate
  2. Run the object cloning process
  3. Specify the new object's name
  4. Select which options you want to include in the copy

docs.title: Did you know you can apply an object's security to a combo?
Did you know you can apply an object's security to a combo?
docs.text:
When configuring a combo or dbcombo, there is an option called "Security object". Selecting it applies the security configured on the object itself, avoiding the need to add where clauses in the query.

This feature simplifies configuring access controls by using the security rules already established on the object, without needing to add extra conditions directly in the SQL query.

docs.title: Did you know you can configure combos to allow new values?
Did you know you can configure combos to allow new values?
docs.text: The flx-dbcombo and flx-multicombo components can be configured to allow new values to be added directly through them. When the record is saved, these new values are automatically added to the designated object.

docs.title: Configuration instructions
docs.text:
To enable this feature:

  1. Go to the Allow new values option
  2. Set up the required fields in the corresponding section

docs.title: Did you know you can compare two databases, both in structure and data, using Visual Studio?
Did you know you can compare two databases, both in structure and data, using Visual Studio?
docs.text: Flexygo relies on tools built into Visual Studio that let you perform powerful database comparisons.

docs.title: Schema comparison
docs.text: Going to Tools → SQL Server → New Schema Comparison, you can compare and update two databases, or a database and a Visual Studio project.

docs.title: Data comparison
docs.text: Through Tools → SQL Server → New Data Comparison, users can compare two databases and generate scripts or perform direct updates.

docs.title: Did you know you can get configuration table changes directly from Flexygo?
Did you know you can get configuration table changes directly from Flexygo?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you access the changes made to configuration tables directly from the application.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Access: the option to get configuration table changes can be found in the object list
  2. Setup:
    • Specify the date from which you want to view changes
    • Select the specific tables to review
    • Generate a script with all the changes made

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: The generated script lets you easily view, review and copy the changes to use them later.

docs.title: Did you know you can build views with information from different databases?
Did you know you can build views with information from different databases?
docs.text: Flexygo can work with multiple databases at the same time through different connection strings. The system uses ConfConnectionString to access tables and functions in the configuration database, while DataConnectionString serves as the main data model.

docs.title: Setting up multiple connections
docs.text:
To add additional connection strings, you need to:

  • Add them to the ConnectionStrings section of the Backend's appsettings.json
  • Create an entry in the DbConnectionStrings system table

Encrypted strings

In IIS and in a production container, connection strings are stored encrypted (enc:v1:...). You can write the new one in plain text: the application encrypts it on the next start. To change an existing one, see Changing an encrypted value by hand.

docs.title: Cross-database queries
docs.text:
In Flexygo's data views, you can write your SQL query mixing several data models, simply by naming the connection string, followed by a dot, the schema and the table name.

Syntax:

SQL
LEFT JOIN {~ConfConnectionString~}.dbo.AspNetUsers

Practical example:

SQL
SELECT EMPLOYEE.employee_id, EMPLOYEE.firstname,
       EMPLOYEE.lastname, u.Id as UserId
FROM EMPLOYEE
LEFT JOIN {~ConfConnectionString~}.dbo.AspNetUsers U
  on U.Reference=EMPLOYEE.employee_id

This approach lets you combine employee information with the application's user data in a single view.

docs.title: Did you know you can view, create, edit or delete objects through JS?
Did you know you can view, create, edit or delete objects through JS?
docs.text: You can perform CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) on objects directly through JavaScript in Flexygo, instead of using SQL processes or DLLs.

docs.title: Key points
docs.text:
• It is essential to call .read() after declaring an object to get its information before performing any action
  • JavaScript functions respect the system's security; if the user lacks permissions, an error message will be shown and the action will not run

docs.title: Code examples
docs.text:
Insert:

JavaScript
function sampleInsert(){
  let obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest');
  obj.read();
  obj.data['TestId'].Value = 1;
  obj.data['Descrip'].Value = 'Sample description';
  if(obj.insert()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Inserted");
  }
}

Update:

JavaScript
function sampleUpdate(){
  let obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest','_Test.TestId=1');
  obj.read();
  obj.data['Descrip'].Value = 'Sample description updated';
  if(obj.update()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Updated");
  }
}

Delete:

JavaScript
function sampleDelete(){
  var obj=new flexygo.obj.Entity('sysTmpTest','_Test.TestId=1');
  if(obj.delete()) {
      flexygo.msg.success("Deleted");
  }
}

docs.title: Did you know you can turn a property into a custom property?
Did you know you can turn a property into a custom property?
docs.text:
Recent versions of Flexygo let you create a custom property based on an existing one through a specific process.

Once this process is complete, the resulting custom property can be used anywhere in the application.

docs.title: Did you know you can set a default filter on a listing that clears itself after the first search?
Did you know you can set a default filter on a listing that clears itself after the first search?
docs.text: This feature helps optimize performance on screens that are frequently used to filter information.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Set a default filter (such as "mine, today's, etc.")
  2. Enable the Remove on first search option

As a result, once the initial filter has been applied, the custom criteria the user sets in later searches will take precedence.

This optimizes the speed of screens that are always used to filter data, since they come with preset parameters that automatically adjust to the user's needs.

docs.title: Did you know we can create users with a preset password?
Did you know we can create users with a preset password?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.0.0.1, Flexygo lets you create users with passwords set administratively.

docs.title: Creation process
docs.text: In the user creation form, select the Set manual password option. You can additionally enable Must change password to require the user to choose a new password after their first login.

docs.title: Main benefit
docs.text:
By setting a password manually from this form, the user will not need to confirm their password by email, since they will be validated automatically with the assigned password.

This feature speeds up user onboarding by avoiding the need for email confirmation, letting the user sign in immediately with the assigned credentials.

docs.title: Did you know you can set a text to confirm the deletion of a record?
Did you know you can set a text to confirm the deletion of a record?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you configure a security mechanism on objects that requires the user to type a confirmation text before deleting a record.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Customization: the confirmation message can be tailored using specific properties of the object
  • Improved security: adds an extra layer of protection against accidental deletions
  • Flexible configuration: managed directly from the object's configuration

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This feature significantly reduces unintended deletions by requiring users to explicitly confirm their record deletion actions, providing greater control over critical data.

docs.title: Did you know you can open any Flexygo screen directly from a link?
Did you know you can open any Flexygo screen directly from a link?
docs.text:
You can access any Flexygo screen directly through a link.

When a user clicks that link, if they are already signed in, the selected screen will open automatically. If they are not authenticated, the system will ask for the access credentials and then redirect the user to the corresponding location.

docs.title: Additional feature
docs.text: You can also perform an automatic sign-in. To do this, the URL must include the access_token parameter along with a valid access code. These codes can be generated through Flexygo's web API.

docs.title: Did you know we can disable module events?
Did you know we can disable module events?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 4.1.0.6, event management became more flexible. In the event creation/edit form you can choose whether it is active or not, letting you prevent that event from running without having to delete it.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Disable events without deleting them: users can disable events on modules without needing to remove them from the system
  • Visibility in the listing: the event list makes it easy to see at a glance which events are active and which are not

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: This feature provides greater flexibility in event administration, letting you temporarily pause execution without losing the existing configuration.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has an emergency stop mode?
Did you know Flexygo has an emergency stop mode?
docs.text: Flexygo offers two modes for managing the application's availability.

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text: Administrators can keep the application operational while update tasks are performed. See Did you know there is a mode for performing maintenance work on the application?.

docs.title: Emergency stop mode
docs.text:
To completely stop an application published in IIS, create an app_offline.htm file in the Frontend's site folder (and in the Backend's, if it's in a separate site or application). Its content is the page users will see. This will:

  • Block connections: every connection to the system will be stopped
  • Show a browser message: a page indicating the offline status will be shown

docs.title: Restoring the service
docs.text:
Once maintenance is finished, delete or rename the app_offline.htm file and the service resumes automatically.

Note

The app_offline.htm file is a feature of the ASP.NET Core Module for IIS. It doesn't work in Docker or when the application runs directly on Kestrel: in those cases, stop the container or the service.

Important warning

This action will leave the application completely inaccessible.

docs.title: Did you know you can choose which columns to export to Excel?
Did you know you can choose which columns to export to Excel?
docs.text: Just click the Excel export option on any list and it will automatically ask which fields you want to use in the report.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Select the Excel export option from any listing
  2. The system will automatically ask which fields you want to include in the report
  3. Choose the desired fields to customize the exported document

docs.title: Did you know you can easily import/export Excel?
Did you know you can easily import/export Excel?
Importing Excel
docs.text:
To import Excel files, do a basic setup from the imports menu. You need to select:

  • The object to import
  • The process generated for the import
  • The template to use

Once configured, the process will be available in the tools menu to import Excel directly.

docs.title: Exporting Excel
docs.text:
Although listings have a standard export option, it is not ideal for large volumes of data. For that reason, you can create an Excel-type report instead.

The process is simple: specify the desired object and view, and the export will be configured. It will then be available in the object's process menu just like any other report.

docs.title: Did you know you can format a field without memorizing every type?
Did you know you can format a field without memorizing every type?
docs.text: Flexygo includes a wizard tool that makes it easy to add fields to templates, letting you apply the desired format intuitively.

docs.title: Step-by-step process
docs.text:
1. Click the button available next to the template's code
  2. Follow the instructions provided by the wizard

The platform also offers access to the application's icons right below the wizard, providing complementary visual tools for customizing fields without requiring deep technical knowledge of data types.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has a generic search for every object?
Did you know Flexygo has a generic search for every object?
docs.text: Flexygo lets you configure a generic search for any object in the application, a feature that is often overlooked during development.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
In the Flexygo 2026 skin:

  1. Enable developer mode
  2. Open the search with Ctrl + K or from the search box in the sidebar
  3. Click the Search settings gear at the bottom of the search (it's only visible in developer mode)
  4. Set every search field you want for any object in the application
The search (Ctrl + K) groups the results by object; the gear at the bottom right opens its settings

In the flexy2022 skin, the settings are in the magnifying-glass icon in the top bar:

docs.title: Did you know we can generate HTML reports?
Did you know we can generate HTML reports?
docs.text:
You can create reports in Flexygo using an HTML template associated with a specific object. The process involves two main steps:

  1. Create an HTML template for the desired object
  2. Generate a new report selecting the HTML type, the corresponding object and the created template

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text: This feature lets you generate reports quickly and easily without needing tools like Crystal Reports.

docs.title: Did you know you can restrict access to Flexygo by IP?
Did you know you can restrict access to Flexygo by IP?
docs.text: This feature lets you implement IP-address-based access restrictions within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Authorized IP groups: you can define sets of allowed IP addresses
  • Assignment to users: the created groups can be linked to specific user accounts
  • Use cases: useful for restricting access to specific locations only, such as the corporate office

docs.title: How to configure it
docs.text:
1. Go to Security > IP Groups to create the IP address groups
  2. Assign the created groups while managing or editing users in the system

This feature provides an extra layer of security by controlling where authenticated users can access the platform from.

docs.title: Did you know we can import role and user security?
Did you know we can import role and user security?
docs.text:
You can import a security configuration already defined at the role level into another role, without needing to set it up from scratch. The process is simple: go to the new role, run the import security process and select the role you want to get the configuration from.

This same option is also available at the user level.

docs.title: Did you know you can handle Flexygo events with JavaScript?
Did you know you can handle Flexygo events with JavaScript?
docs.text: You can use the flexygo.events.on and flexygo.events.off functions to manage events in Flexygo through JavaScript.

docs.title: Practical example
docs.text:
A common use case is refreshing a module only when the customer has an active status:

  1. Define a callback function that checks specific conditions:
    • Checks whether the sender is an instance of flexygo.obj.Entity
    • Validates that the object's name is "Cliente"
    • Confirms the Activo field has a value of 1
  2. Get the module's HTML element using a query selector
  3. Subscribe the module to the event using flexygo.events.on() with the parameters: the module, the event type ("entity"), the action ("updated") and the callback function

docs.title: Available data
docs.text: When the event runs, the callback's parameter provides data whose sender corresponds to the event's class (for example, flexygo.Process for process events).

docs.title: Did you know you can add JavaScript to the offline application directly from a file?
Did you know you can add JavaScript to the offline application directly from a file?
docs.text: You can include JavaScript code in an offline application by loading it from a physical file.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text: This approach makes the code easier to maintain and allows logic to be reused across different parts of the application.

docs.title: Did you know you can call JavaScript functions from Flexygo's own templates?
Did you know you can call JavaScript functions from Flexygo's own templates?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you invoke JavaScript functions directly from templates using a specific syntax. To use this feature, write your marker following this pattern: {{myJSFunction(param1, param2, ...)}} and Flexygo will call the function.

The system will automatically process the call and display the result in the template. A useful feature is that if the parameter names match existing fields in the template, the system will automatically convert those parameters to their corresponding values.

docs.title: Did you know you can manage object insert, update and delete actions with JSON procedures?
Did you know you can manage object insert, update and delete actions with JSON procedures?
docs.text:
In recent versions of Flexygo, you can manage object insert, update and delete actions through stored procedures using JSON.

This feature complements the pre-existing option that uses XML to perform these data manipulation operations.

docs.title: Documentation location
docs.text: For detailed information and practical examples about this feature, check Flexygo's built-in help under: Help → Programming → Update types.

docs.title: Did you know every Flexygo instance has a kanban for managing custom boards?
Did you know every Flexygo instance has a kanban for managing custom boards?
docs.text: There is an object called Boards that makes it easy to create multiple custom boards with adjustable columns. Every instance ships with a first board containing the basic development cycle states.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
The Boards tool lets users:

  • Create as many boards as needed
  • Customize the columns according to their specific requirements
  • Access a default board that includes standard development-cycle states

docs.title: Did you know you can set a fixed order for a Kanban's cards?
Did you know you can set a fixed order for a Kanban's cards?
docs.text:
From the kanban's configuration you can define the fields by which cards will be automatically sorted, instead of using the free-form order that comes by default.

For example, cards can always appear organized by priority once this parameter is configured in the system.

This feature lets you customize the kanban's behavior to keep an ordered structure based on specific criteria of the project or workflow being used.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has keyboard shortcuts?
Did you know Flexygo has keyboard shortcuts?
docs.text:
Flexygo includes several useful keyboard shortcuts:

  • F1: opens the tool's help
  • F2: opens the configuration parameters
  • Ctrl + S: saves changes when the focus is on an edit form

In the Flexygo 2026 skin, also:

  • Ctrl + K: opens the search
  • Ctrl + Shift + M: opens Place modules, to arrange the page's modules
  • Ctrl + Space: opens developer mode's Quick access. See Did you know you can access any object's configuration from the sidebar?

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl for the last three.

docs.title: Did you know there is a mode for performing maintenance work on the application?
Did you know there is a mode for performing maintenance work on the application?
docs.text: Maintenance mode blocks access to the application while you work on it. Starting with version 10 it's managed from the Version Management screen, which only administrators can open. In the Flexygo 2026 skin, open it by clicking the Version row at the bottom of the sidebar.

docs.title: Enabling or scheduling maintenance
docs.text:
1. In Version Management, open More actions (the three dots next to Update) and choose Maintenance mode.

    More actions: Maintenance mode and Refresh screens

  2. In When should it start?, choose Start now or Schedule and set the Start date and time.

  3. Optionally, write a Message for users (optional). This is what users will see shows how the maintenance page will look.
  4. Click Activate and confirm.
The panel with Schedule chosen: start date and time, message and preview of the maintenance page (Spanish interface)

While it's on or scheduled, Version Management shows a notice with a Manage button to change it. For a scheduled maintenance you can use Reschedule or Cancel schedule; otherwise it turns on by itself on the scheduled date.

docs.title: Who can still get in
docs.text:
• The administrator who enabled it keeps using the application normally.
  • Other administrators can open Version Management to turn it off, even if whoever enabled it isn't available.
  • Every other user is redirected to the maintenance page, with the message you entered. Open pages update when the state changes and, when maintenance ends, users can go back to their page.

To finish, click Maintenance mode and then Deactivate. Maintenance stays on until an administrator turns it off: it has no scheduled end.

Note

During an application update, maintenance is controlled by the update process itself, with no exemptions for anyone, and it can't be turned off manually until the update finishes.

docs.title: Refreshing users' screens
docs.text:
In Version Management, open More actions and choose Refresh screens. You can reload the screen of All users connected or of Specific users, whom you can search for and select.

Removed processes

The system processes EnableMaintenanceMode and DisableMaintenanceMode were removed in version 10. If you called them from a button or an integration, use the Version Management screen.

docs.title: Did you know you can add security to the App's menus?
Did you know you can add security to the App's menus?
docs.text:
From the shield available in the Menus section of the Offline App panel, you can implement access controls based on roles, users and specific permissions. This feature lets you customize the visibility of the different menus depending on the identity of the user who signs in to the application.

This capability makes it easy to selectively hide or show menu options, improving both security and user experience by restricting access to only the functions relevant to each profile.

docs.title: Did you know you can use multiple databases in Flexygo?
Did you know you can use multiple databases in Flexygo?
docs.text: Flexygo can work with more than one data model, even hosted on different servers. This feature lets users create objects against multiple databases and set relations between them without worrying about their source location.
