docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Automatic real-time query generation
  • Compatible with standard products
  • Transparently linking data from different sources

docs.title: Documentation reference
docs.text: For more information, check: Help → Programming → Linked Servers.

docs.title: Did you know you can have more than one account in Flexygo Mobile?
Did you know you can have more than one account in Flexygo Mobile?
docs.text: Flexygo Mobile lets you manage multiple accounts at the same time, with the ability to switch between them without needing a connection.

docs.title: Supported account types
docs.text:
The system supports accounts that can differ in:

  • Different domains
  • Different users
  • Different applications within the same domain

docs.title: Did you know you can enable and disable nodes through a SQL query?
Did you know you can enable and disable nodes through a SQL query?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.5.0.1, Flexygo lets you enable and disable nodes through SQL queries.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The node's configuration includes a new section called Enable that uses a SQL query to determine whether a node should be enabled or disabled.

docs.title: Did you know you can now configure applications' mail and Web Mail accounts with the OAuth 2.0 protocol?
Did you know you can now configure applications' mail and Web Mail accounts with the OAuth 2.0 protocol?
docs.text: Mail accounts used in the Web Mail section can now be configured using the OAuth 2.0 protocol. This capability extends to both Microsoft and Google accounts.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Built-in help: the platform includes built-in assistance for the setup
  • New authentication option: account configuration now shows a new authentication type section
  • Bearer token support: users can configure the new authentication method through the bearer token option

docs.title: Did you know you can create and restore backups of the offline application?
Did you know you can create and restore backups of the offline application?
docs.text: You can back up the database in Flexygo's offline application.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
To access these functions, go to the application's synchronization menu. Once there, turn on the advanced options switch and you will find two main buttons at the bottom of the screen:

  1. Create backup: generates a file with the data currently stored in the application
  2. Restore backup: lets you load a previously created backup file to recover the saved data

This process lets you preserve the application's information and transfer it between devices or restore it when needed.

docs.title: Did you know you can query the offline application's database?
Did you know you can query the offline application's database?
docs.text: The Flexygo application lets you access the database in offline mode through a feature available in the synchronization menu.

docs.title: Accessing the feature
docs.text: To use this feature, go to the app's synchronization menu and turn on the advanced options switch. At the bottom of that screen you will find the Database button.

docs.title: Available features
docs.text:
Once you access this section, you have two options:

  1. Write custom queries using SQLite
  2. Directly select the table you want to query

This feature lets you flexibly query the local database synchronized on your device, making it easier to access information without an internet connection.

docs.title: Did you know you can resize images coming from offline?
Did you know you can resize images coming from offline?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.6.0.1 you can configure image compression for an object, so the pictures coming from the offline app are not stored at excessive sizes.

docs.title: Steps to configure compression
docs.text:
In skin 2026, with development mode on:

  1. Open the configuration of the object that stores the images. The quickest way is Quick access (Ctrl Space) → Extra settings.
  2. In Extra settings, choose Images in the selector at the top right (next to Documents, Chatter and Mail).
  3. In the Compression section, fill in:
    • Compression: Nothing, Low, Medium or High. The last three reduce the size, but also the quality.
    • Max width and Max height: the maximum size of the image. The proportions are kept without exceeding those values.
  4. Click Save.
Extra settings → Images, with the Compression section at the bottom (Spanish interface)

In the flexy2022 skin you get there from the object wizard: in the last step, Image settings.

This way the application automatically resizes the images captured in offline mode and they take less space in the database.

docs.title: Did you know you can access the offline app's synchronization history list?
Did you know you can access the offline app's synchronization history list?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you review the full log of synchronizations performed by the offline application and run them again if problems were detected during the initial process.

This feature provides significant value to users working with Flexygo's offline version. It lets them verify that every synchronization completed successfully and, if not, re-run them without needing to restart the entire synchronization process.

In addition, accessing the synchronization history gives users greater oversight of the updates applied to the application, letting them confirm that data stays continuously up to date.

docs.title: Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the synchronization timeout in the offline app?
Did you know that in Flexygo you can set the synchronization timeout in the offline app?
docs.text:
Flexygo lets you configure the timeout for synchronization in the offline application, improving the user experience and optimizing data transfer.

This feature lets you customize the synchronization intervals between the offline app and the connected database. This makes it possible to adapt the parameters to each organization's particularities, ensuring data is updated quickly and efficiently.

The timeout adjustment is also especially useful in scenarios where the internet connection is poor or unstable. Users can configure these timeouts to ensure the application works without interruptions, allowing for a smoother experience and reliable synchronization in any circumstance and location.

docs.title: Did you know you can enable/disable presets linked to objects?
Did you know you can enable/disable presets linked to objects?
docs.text:
In the latest versions of Flexygo, you can enable/disable presets linked to objects, making it easier to manage stored presets.

This feature lets users more efficiently manage the predefined settings associated with different objects within the Flexygo platform.

docs.title: Did you know you can enable the profiler in the Offline App from anywhere?
Did you know you can enable the profiler in the Offline App from anywhere?
docs.text: Flexygo's offline application includes a profiling tool that you can use from anywhere in the application.

docs.title: Main functions
docs.text:
To access the profiler, you need to know two fundamental functions:

  • flexygo.sql.initProfiler: starts logging all SQL queries and their results
  • flexygo.sql.stopProfiler: stops logging and displays the captured data in the console

docs.title: Filtering results
docs.text:
When working with complex edits that contain multiple dependencies, you can use:

  • flexygo.sql.filterProfiler: lets you search for specific statements in the logged data

This function is case-insensitive by default, but you can change this behavior by passing true as the third parameter if you need a case-sensitive search.

docs.title: Did you know you can use a profiler for the Offline App's queries?
Did you know you can use a profiler for the Offline App's queries?
docs.text: To access the application's profiler, go to the database menu. There you will find a green button that, when pressed, starts logging every SQL statement executed and its results.

docs.title: Steps to use the profiler
docs.text:
1. Start logging: click the green button in the database menu
  2. Navigate: browse to the screen you want to analyze so its statements and results get logged
  3. Stop logging: go back to the database menu and click the red box
  4. View results: every SQL query executed will be shown along with its results

docs.title: Additional feature
docs.text: The profiler includes a filter at the bottom that lets you show only the statements containing specific text, making it easier to search and analyze particular queries.

docs.title: Did you know you can publish the database with just a double-click?
Did you know you can publish the database with just a double-click?
docs.text: Publishing databases in Flexygo can be simplified into a two-step process.

docs.title: Step 1: configure the publish
docs.text: Open the context menu (right-click) and select "Publish". Complete every step of the publish wizard, setting the required parameters.

docs.title: Step 2: save the profile
docs.text: Before clicking the final publish button, select Save Profile As... to store the configuration.

docs.title: Later use
docs.text: Once the profile is saved, publishing becomes much simpler. You only need to double-click the publish profile file to run the process without reconfiguring the parameters every time.

docs.title: Did you know you can generate QR codes with Flexygo?
Did you know you can generate QR codes with Flexygo?
docs.text:
To create QR codes in Flexygo, you just need to add a specific marker in your configuration. The method is very direct: add the marker with the field's name followed by a pipe and the word QR.

This feature lets you generate QR codes easily, directly from the platform, without needing any additional external tools.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has Radio and Multiple checkbox controls?
Did you know Flexygo has Radio and Multiple checkbox controls?
docs.text:
Flexygo offers UI controls called Radio and Multiple checkbox that work similarly to the combo and multicombo controls.

The main feature that sets these controls apart is their visual presentation: they display every value on screen at once, which can be a good option for letting the user pick an option more quickly when there are only a few values to choose from.

These controls are especially useful when:

  • There is a limited number of available options
  • A faster selection by the user is required
  • A more direct and visual interface is preferred

docs.title: Did you know you can enable and disable an object's relation through a SQL query?
Did you know you can enable and disable an object's relation through a SQL query?
docs.text: Starting with version 4.9.0.1, Flexygo lets you dynamically control relations between objects. The platform introduces a new section called Enable conditions in the relation's configuration.

docs.title: Main feature
docs.text: This feature lets users use SQL queries to determine whether a relation between objects should be active or inactive.

docs.title: Practical application
docs.text: The solution is implemented directly in the configuration parameters of object relations within the Flexygo system, providing greater flexibility in data management and workflows.

docs.title: Did you know you can integrate Flexygo with scales?
Did you know you can integrate Flexygo with scales?
docs.text:
Flexygo supports integration with weighing devices. Users can capture weight data in two ways:

  1. Manual method: pressing a button located in the text field to capture the weight
  2. Automated method: configuring triggers that collect the data automatically

For additional technical details, check the documentation at Help → Connectors → Scales.

docs.title: Did you know you can send events from the server to the browsers?
Did you know you can send events from the server to the browsers?
docs.text: Flexygo lets the server send notices to the connected browsers without the user doing anything: a new message, an error in the background, some data that has changed…

docs.title: Server side (C#)
docs.text:
From a process, create an EventHelper (namespace FLEXYGO.Interfaces.SignalR.Events) with its class and type, fill in masterIdentity to identify the notice and sender with the data, and send it with the FLEXYGO.SignalR.Events class:

C#
using FLEXYGO.Interfaces.SignalR.Events;
using FLEXYGO.SignalR;

EventHelper eventInfo = new EventHelper(eEventClass.Push, eEventType.Notify)
{
    masterIdentity = "orderServed",
    sender = new Dictionary<string, object>
    {
        { "order", orderId },
        { "message", "The order has been served" }
    }
};
Events.FireGenericUserEvent(eventInfo, username);

Depending on who the notice is for:

  • FireGenericUserEvent(eventInfo, userName): one user, by name.
  • FireGenericUsersEvent(eventInfo, userNames): several users.
  • FireGenericUserIDEvent(eventInfo, userId): one user, by Id.
  • FireGenericAllUserEvent(eventInfo): every connected user.

The methods are asynchronous (Task): you can await them or fire them without waiting. The process runs in the backend, which hands the notice to the frontend (api/frontend/Events/...), and the frontend delivers it to the browsers through SignalR. That is why it works the same with the frontend and the backend on different servers.

docs.title: Client side (JavaScript)
docs.text:
Listen to the event class and type with flexygo.events.on and check masterIdentity to keep only your notices:

JavaScript
flexygo.events.on(this, 'push', 'notify', function (e) {
    if (e.masterIdentity === 'orderServed' && e.sender) {
        flexygo.msg.info(e.sender.message);
    }
});

If the component can be drawn again, remove the handler first with flexygo.events.off(this, 'push', 'notify') so it is not registered twice.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text: Real-time notices, refreshing a screen when new data arrives, or reporting errors of background processes. The WhatsApp connector, for example, uses it to refresh the conversation when a message comes in and to warn when one could not be sent.

docs.title: Did you know two Flexygo applications can share a single document management system?
Did you know two Flexygo applications can share a single document management system?
docs.text: It is very common for an enterprise Flexygo and a customer portal to share document management. When both applications are linked to the same ERP, there is no issue. However, when both are Flexygo instances, one can be used as the main repository while the second accesses the shared documents directly.

docs.title: Configuration steps
docs.text:
Step 1 - Application structure

  • A main application with its own database and configuration
  • A second application with its own database and configuration, plus a third connection pointing to the main application's configuration database

Step 2 - Common path

Configure a setting that specifies the common path where shared documents will be stored.

Steps 3-5 - Updating connection strings

Run SQL scripts to change the connections of the following objects and views in the second application:

  • Document
  • Document_Object
  • Document_Version
  • Documents
  • sysDocumentsCategories

These changes point the document objects to the main application's configuration database.

docs.title: Did you know you can access any object's configuration from quick access?
Did you know you can access any object's configuration from quick access?
docs.text: In the Flexygo 2026 skin, with developer mode enabled, the floating Quick access button appears. Open it by clicking it or with Ctrl + Space (Cmd + Space on a Mac) from any page. You can move through its options with the arrow keys and pick one with Enter.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Object: shows the object of the page you are currently viewing.
    • Change (or Choose, if the page has no object) opens a filter to jump to any other object. The choice lasts until you go to another page.
    • The + icon (New object) opens the wizard to create an object.
    • List, Edit and Security open the object's listing, its form for inserting records and its security.
    • Wizard, Settings and View Object open the object's configuration, and Extra settings the documents, images and chatter settings.
  • Page: Place modules (Ctrl + Shift + M) to arrange the page's modules. It doesn't appear on touch screens.
  • Processes: Reload cache, Generate scripts and Change origin, with the origin in use underneath.
  • Administration: Control panel and Dashboard, from any page.

This feature provides an efficient way for developers to navigate and quickly access different sections of the application without having to go through multiple menu levels.

docs.title: flexy2022 skin
docs.text:
The flexy2022 skin keeps the Page Config sidebar. It works by default to configure the object you are currently viewing, but you can change its value to quickly access any other object:

  • Quick access to configuration: change the value in the sidebar to switch between different objects
  • List icon: gives direct access to the object's listing
  • Plus (+) icon: gives direct access to inserting new records

docs.title: Did you know there's an option to see which users are viewing the same module at the same time?
Did you know there's an option to see which users are viewing the same module at the same time?
docs.text: Starting with Flexygo version 4.9.0.x, a new feature in the module configuration lets you enable visibility of simultaneous users on list, edit, view and kanban type modules.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: When this option is enabled in the module's configuration, an indicator icon appears showing the number of people currently viewing the module. Hovering the cursor over this icon shows a list with the names of every connected user.

docs.title: Applicability
docs.text:
This feature is available on modules of the following types:

  • List
  • Edit
  • View
  • Kanban

docs.title: Did you know you can identify the source of a SQL connection by application?
Did you know you can identify the source of a SQL connection by application?
docs.text:
To analyze the source of the connections to your database, you can filter using the application's name.

The configuration wizard doesn't add this attribute: if you don't set it, SQL Server shows the data provider's generic name. To identify your application, add the Application Name attribute to each connection string in the ConnectionStrings section of the Backend's appsettings.json:

JSON
"ConnectionStrings": {
  "ConfConnectionString": "Data Source=MyServer;Initial Catalog=MyApp_IC;User ID=sa;Password=...;TrustServerCertificate=True;Application Name=MyApp",
  "DataConnectionString": "Data Source=MyServer;Initial Catalog=MyApp_Data;User ID=sa;Password=...;TrustServerCertificate=True;Application Name=MyApp"
}

Restart the Backend (in IIS, recycle the application pool) so it uses the new strings.

Encrypted strings

In IIS and in a production container, connection strings are stored encrypted (enc:v1:...). To change them, see Changing an encrypted value by hand.

docs.title: Did you know the offline app's sqllist components can import templates?
Did you know the offline app's sqllist components can import templates?
docs.text: Starting with version 6.4 of the offline application, you can use page templates directly in the flx-sqllist component.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
To use this feature, two attributes must be added to the component:

  • PageName: the page's name
  • ObjectName: the name of the object whose configuration you want to use

The app will get that page's configuration (SQL statement, header, body and footer), but will only use the values that are not explicitly configured in the component.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The system follows a priority hierarchy:

  1. Explicit settings within the component take precedence
  2. The referenced page's settings are applied as default values
  3. This lets you combine custom elements with reusable templates

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: This feature enables more efficient development by reusing existing templates, letting the flx-sqllist component show listings on different pages without duplicating code.

docs.title: Did you know you can pin the toolbar in place?
Did you know you can pin the toolbar in place?
docs.text: Since Flexygo version 4.9.0.2, you can keep the toolbar fixed at the top while scrolling through a module. To enable this feature, add the sticky-toolbar class to the corresponding module's configuration.

docs.title: Additional features
docs.text: Similarly, you can also pin a listing's header using the sticky-header class. This keeps the header visible while scrolling through the data.

docs.title: Did you know you can review the Offline App's synchronizations from Flexygo?
Did you know you can review the Offline App's synchronizations from Flexygo?
docs.text: From the offline application menu you can access the synchronization history. To do so, just press the button located at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Available features
docs.text:
Once you access the history, you will be able to:

  • View the synchronizations performed
  • Identify the types of synchronization that were run
  • Restart or repeat the synchronization of specific data

docs.title: Did you know you can create template groupings that users can select and reorder?
Did you know you can create template groupings that users can select and reorder?
docs.text: When creating template groupings in a list, you can enable an option called "User can configure groups" directly in the template's configuration.

docs.title: Technical implementation
docs.text:
When this option is enabled, a specific line must be added to the template's header. The proposed code uses an interactive button:

HTML
<button class="btn {{groupButtonActive(this,'IsCollection')}}"
onclick="$(this).closest('flx-list')[0].toggleGroup('IsCollection');">
Object/Collection</button>

The IsCollection parameter must exactly match the group field you want the user to be able to toggle.

docs.title: Expected result
docs.text: After adding one line of code per grouping you want to enable, users will be able to choose which groupings stay active at any given time, providing greater flexibility and interface customization.

docs.title: Did you know you can set up a test environment without worrying about the license?
Did you know you can set up a test environment without worrying about the license?
docs.text: The Convert to dev database action (process SetDbDevelopMode; in earlier versions, Set Single User Mode) gets a copy of the configuration database ready for testing.

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text: It is useful when you move the production database to a test environment: the license does not work there, because the server and the environment change, and you do not want every production user to be able to sign in.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Deletes the license from the database. You then have to activate a new one, for example an evaluation license.
  • Blocks every user except admin, guest and the one you choose in Enable user to perform tests.
  • Reloads the cache and the page.

This way you can develop with admin and test with the chosen user, with their profile and roles. The chosen user keeps their own password.

Use it only on a copy

It deletes the license and blocks users in the database the application is connected to. Before running it, make sure you are working in a test environment that is distinct from production: server, database, configuration and project name.

docs.title: Where it is
docs.text:
Only administrators can run it. In skin 2026, open the control panel and, in the actions, click Convert to dev database. It asks for the test user and for a confirmation before doing anything.

Control panel actions, with Convert to dev database (Spanish interface)

In the flexy2022 skin it is the Set Db to Development Mode process of the object collection (Admin Area → Object Collection).

docs.title: Did you know the offline app can read messages out loud?
Did you know the offline app can read messages out loud?
docs.text: The Flexygo platform includes a text-to-speech capability through the flexygo.ai.textToSpeech function. This tool lets you play back text content out loud.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Customizable text input: specify any text content you want to be read out loud
  • Language setting: it defaults to the user's language, but it can be changed manually
  • Speed control: adjust the playback speed to your preference
  • Volume control: adjust the playback's volume level

docs.title: Did you know you can install Flexygo unattended?
Did you know you can install Flexygo unattended?
docs.text:
Starting with version 10, the Backend can apply every step of the configuration wizard on its own when it starts, without anyone opening the wizard. The values are read from configuration, usually from environment variables (for example, in a docker-compose.yml or in the .env file). This lets you automate a deployment from start to finish.

Note

The old FlexygoInstaller.exe /unatended ... no longer exists in version 10.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Required What it's for Setup__Unattended Yes true enables the unattended setup. Setup__ProjectName Yes Project name. It can't be empty or rename. Setup__AdminPassword Yes Password of the administrator user. ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString Yes Full connection string of the configuration database. ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString Yes, if the product uses it Connection string of each data database: one ConnectionStrings__<name> variable for every active connection registered in the configuration database. MailSettings__Host No SMTP server. If it isn't set, the outgoing mail step is skipped. MailSettings__Port No SMTP port (25 by default). MailSettings__Ssl No true to use SSL. MailSettings__From, MailSettings__UserName, MailSettings__Password No Sender and credentials of the SMTP server.

Connection strings must include the server (Data Source), the database and SQL Server authentication (User ID and Password); integrated security isn't supported.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
YAML
services:
  flx-backend:
    environment:
      Setup__Unattended: "true"
      Setup__ProjectName: "CustomerName_CRM"
      Setup__AdminPassword: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"
      ConnectionStrings__ConfConnectionString: "Data Source=sqlserver;Initial Catalog=CRM_IC;User ID=sa;Password=${SQL_PASSWORD};TrustServerCertificate=True"
      ConnectionStrings__DataConnectionString: "Data Source=sqlserver;Initial Catalog=CRM_Data;User ID=sa;Password=${SQL_PASSWORD};TrustServerCertificate=True"
      MailSettings__Host: "mail.mycompany.com"
      MailSettings__Port: "25"
      MailSettings__Ssl: "true"
      MailSettings__From: "admin@mycompany.com"
      MailSettings__UserName: "MymailUser"
      MailSettings__Password: "${MAIL_PASSWORD}"

The passwords go in the .env next to the compose, in single quotes so they are taken as is, and that file is not committed to git:

Text Only
ADMIN_PASSWORD='<admin password>'
SQL_PASSWORD='<SQL Server password>'
MAIL_PASSWORD='<mail password>'

A complete compose, with the database in a container, in Deploying with Docker.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. When it starts, the Backend validates the values. If any is missing, the log says which variable must be defined.
  2. It sets up the configuration database (creating it, updating it or leaving it as it is), applies the project name and the administrator password, and sets up each data database and the outgoing mail. It uses the same steps as the wizard.
  3. When it's done, it saves Setup:UnattendedCompleted = true in the Backend's appsettings.json, so it doesn't run again on the next starts.

There's no screen: progress is written to the log. While it runs, api/backend/setup/ready returns 503, so the Docker container shows as "starting" until it finishes. If it fails, the Backend stops with a non-zero exit code; with a restart policy, the container tries again.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo added a new signature control integrated with Wacom tablets?
Did you know Flexygo added a new signature control integrated with Wacom tablets?
docs.text: Flexygo has developed a new control type, similar to the WhiteBoard, that lets you work with Wacom tablets to capture signatures.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
Configuration:

  • A new control type called Wacom Signature
  • Configured as an object property or process parameter

  • Available in the Options section

Functionality:

The system lets you save both the signature and the biometric data captured through the Wacom tablets, making it easier to integrate digital signatures into Flexygo's processes.

docs.title: Did you know you can reuse the WebAPI's authorization tokens?
Did you know you can reuse the WebAPI's authorization tokens?
docs.text: By default, Flexygo generates a new token on every request to the /token endpoint. However, this behavior can be changed.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
For the system to return the same token while it remains valid, you need to:

  1. Go to the application's parameters
  2. Enable the ReuseTokens option

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Once this setting is enabled, as long as a token stays "alive" it will be returned on every request. This optimizes performance by reusing valid tokens instead of constantly generating new ones.

docs.title: Did you know Flexygo has webhooks?
Did you know Flexygo has webhooks?
docs.text:
Flexygo can receive events from external services regardless of their transmission protocol.

This feature enables secure integration with third-party services. For example, it can be used to securely receive notification of when a user completes a payment and start shipping an order.

Flexygo can also notify outwards when a record changes (outbound webhooks) and open decisions to people or roles: Approvals, human tasks and outbound webhooks.

docs.title: What is Flexygo's SBOM and why do we publish it?
What is Flexygo's SBOM and why do we publish it?
docs.text:
At Flexygo we maintain an ongoing commitment to the transparency, security and trust that our customers place in us. With that goal in mind, we have decided to publish our platform's SBOM (Software Bill of Materials), a document that details all the software components — both our own and third-party — that are part of the solutions built with Flexygo.

An SBOM can be understood as the digital equivalent of a bill of materials in manufacturing. In a software context, this document structurally records every library, module and dependency involved in developing, running and maintaining an application. This provides a complete view of the product's technical composition, which is essential to guarantee its traceability and strengthen the security of the digital supply chain.

Publishing the SBOM follows an increasingly widespread practice in the technology industry, driven by the growing need to control the risks associated with external dependencies and to comply with new international standards on cybersecurity and regulatory compliance. Bodies such as the United States' National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) actively promote the adoption of SBOMs as a key tool to increase the transparency and resilience of computer systems.

With this in mind, the decision to publish Flexygo's SBOM pursues three main objectives. First, guaranteeing transparency, giving our customers, auditors and partners the ability to know precisely which components make up the platform. This information enables compliance analysis, license verification and technological compatibility checks with other environments. Second, strengthening security, by making it easier to detect and manage vulnerabilities associated with external dependencies or outdated versions. Having an up-to-date SBOM makes it possible to act quickly on security alerts and apply preventive measures effectively. And third, meeting regulatory and technology-governance requirements, which are becoming increasingly strict in both the public and private sectors.

Having an audited SBOM demonstrates a genuine commitment to secure development best practices and to the traceability of software throughout its entire lifecycle.

Publishing our SBOM is not a simple transparency gesture, but a strategic measure that strengthens trust in the Flexygo platform. It represents a decisive step towards a more open, verifiable and sustainable development model, where users can have full certainty about the origin, licensing and security of every component. It also lets us improve our own internal quality-control, version-management and dependency-monitoring processes, strengthening the foundation on which our technology solutions evolve.

In short, publishing Flexygo's SBOM reflects our commitment to responsible innovation and technical excellence. We believe that transparency and traceability are not merely regulatory obligations, but fundamental values that help build a more trustworthy, secure and collaborative digital ecosystem.

docs.title: Attachment
docs.text: You can download Flexygo's SBOM in CycloneDX (JSON) format.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: The purpose of this document is to establish recommendations and best practices for a secure Flexygo installation on an IIS environment, minimizing vulnerabilities and ensuring the protection of associated data and services.

docs.title: 2. Recommended architecture
docs.text:
• Web server (IIS): dedicated exclusively to Flexygo and its associated web services.
  • Database server (SQL Server): a separate instance from IIS, not exposed externally. It should only be accessible from the internal network or via VPN.
  • File server (NAS): a repository external to the website where the documents managed by Flexygo will be stored.

docs.title: 3.1. Installation location
docs.text:
• Install Flexygo in a separate folder from IIS's standard structure (C:\inetpub\wwwroot).
    • Recommended example: D:\WebApps\Flexygo
  • Assign the minimum necessary permissions to the Application Pool account (Read, Execute).

docs.title: 3.2. IIS security configuration
docs.text:
• Disable directory listing (Directory Browsing).

  • Remove server headers: in web.config or through the URL Rewrite module:

    XML
    <outboundRules>
  <rule name="Remove Server Header">
    <match serverVariable="RESPONSE_Server" pattern=".+" />
    <action type="Rewrite" value="" />
  </rule>
</outboundRules>

  • Enable Request Filtering to block unnecessary extensions (.cmd, .bat, .exe, .dll).

docs.title: 4. External document management
docs.text:
• Configure Flexygo so that document storage does not reside within the IIS website.
  • Use a dedicated NAS or file server, accessible only from the internal network.
  • Implement secure SMB or NFS authentication.
  • Control access through specific NTFS permissions or ACLs.

docs.title: 5. Database (SQL Server)
docs.text:
• Install on a separate server, preferably on an internal subnet with no direct Internet access.
  • Disable "sa" authentication and enable Windows authentication whenever possible, and create a dedicated user for Flexygo.
  • Restrict access ports through an internal firewall.

docs.title: 6. HTTPS and SSL/TLS certificates
docs.text:
• Install a valid SSL certificate issued by a trusted CA.
  • Force HTTPS across the whole site (301 redirection from HTTP).
  • Configure TLS 1.2 or higher, disabling SSL 2.0, SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0.

docs.title: 7. Additional hardening
docs.text:
• Regularly update IIS, .NET, Windows and Flexygo.
  • Implement a web application firewall (WAF) if available (e.g. ModSecurity or Azure WAF).
  • Enable detailed logging (IIS Logs + Event Viewer + Flexygo logs).
  • Implement automatic backups (web, NAS and database).
  • Enable monitoring and alerts for suspicious access.
  • Enable MFA either in Flexygo itself or in the delegated authentication system.

docs.title: 1. Principle of least privilege (mandatory)
docs.text:
Every object, process or customization MUST be created applying the principle of least privilege.

  • Explicitly define roles with access and their read, write and delete permissions
  • Avoid objects accessible by all users.
  • Do not rely on button visibility as a security control.
  • Block direct execution by URL when it should not be allowed.
  • Do not expose unnecessary objects in the API.

docs.title: 2. Integrating Flexygo into a CI/CD cycle
docs.text:
Flexygo must be integrated into a CI/CD pipeline to guarantee ongoing quality and security.

  • Version control through NuGet packages.
  • Use centralized repositories (Git).
  • Define a Hotfix policy.

docs.title: 3. Including tests in CI/CD
docs.text:
Every development must include automated tests, adapted to Flexygo's low-code nature.

  • Develop interface tests to ensure full functionality and access.
  • Unit tests to test DLLs or stored procedures.
  • Include running Flexygo's native tests to verify the tool's structure.
  • Add load tests if you'll be working in environments with many users.

docs.title: 4. Protecting passwords and secrets
docs.text:
It is mandatory to ensure that no password or secret leaves the system.

Forbidden:

  • Hardcoding passwords in code, SQL or configuration.
  • Sending credentials through logs or error messages.
  • Committing passwords to source control.

Mandatory:

  • Add pipeline checks that:
    • Look for secret patterns in the code.
    • Block the deployment if any are detected.

docs.title: 5.1 Enabling auditing
docs.text:
Enable auditing on every object that:

  • Handles sensitive data
  • Allows critical changes
  • Affects key business processes

docs.title: 6. Secure DLL development
docs.text: When developing custom DLLs, the following rules must be strictly followed.

docs.title: 6.1 Database access
docs.text:
Use exclusively:

  • Parameterized SQL
  • Stored Procedures

Dynamic SQL built by string concatenation is forbidden.

❌ Incorrect:

C#
string sql = "SELECT * FROM Clientes WHERE Id = " + id;

✅ Correct:

C#
SqlCommand cmd = new SqlCommand("GetClienteById", conn);
cmd.CommandType = CommandType.StoredProcedure;
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@Id", id);

docs.title: 7. Pre-production review checklist
docs.text:
Before deploying to production, make sure you meet these points:

  • [ ] Least privilege is applied to all objects
  • [ ] Flexygo is integrated into CI/CD
  • [ ] Tests run successfully in the pipeline
  • [ ] No passwords or secrets are exposed
  • [ ] Auditing is enabled where appropriate
  • [ ] DLLs use parameterized SQL or stored procedures

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The Flexygo project implements a formally structured Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC), integrating security practices, quality control and traceability into every phase of the build, integration and deployment process. The continuous integration (CI/CD) system documents and runs more than 30 automated steps that ensure the integrity, availability and security of the software at every stage of the development cycle.

The automation environment guarantees that every build follows a reproducible flow, with security controls, code analysis, unit tests, secure packaging and periodic artifact backups.

docs.title: 2. General flow of the applied SDLC
docs.text:
Flexygo's development process is structured into sequential stages with dependencies conditioned on the success of the previous steps, guaranteeing a secure, error-free flow before reaching the publishing environment.

Main phases:

  1. Environment preparation and cleanup
  2. Controlled code build
  3. Secure dependency management
  4. Validation and unit tests
  5. Quality and coverage analysis
  6. Artifact generation and publishing
  7. Automated technical documentation
  8. Version backup and retention
  9. Secure configuration closure

Each phase includes verifiable controls and evidence demonstrating the application of security and quality measures.

docs.title: 3.1. Environment preparation (steps 1–2)
docs.text:
• Cleaning connection strings in the appsettings.json files (in installations they are stored encrypted): the automated process runs a PowerShell script that removes or masks sensitive connection strings before starting the build, preventing accidental credential exposure. This control ensures compliance with the principle of minimizing sensitive information in development environments.
  • Source code backup: before building, an automated backup of the source code is made, preserving a restore point in case of later alterations or errors. The backup mechanism is conditioned on the success of the previous steps, ensuring only valid versions are stored.

docs.title: 3.2. Build and dependency management (steps 3–6)
docs.text:
• NuGet package restoration: packages are obtained from controlled sources, with verified and locked versions to ensure the reproducibility and integrity of the build environment.
  • Solution build (.NET): the project is built and published automatically with dotnet build and dotnet publish, ensuring full traceability from source code to the generated binary.
  • Publishing configurations and databases (CONFIG DB and DATA DB): the publishing scripts use SQLPACKAGE and run controlled build processes, only validated if the previous steps succeeded, applying the principle of build-chain integrity.

docs.title: 3.3. Testing, validation and technical auditing (steps 11–14, 23–25, 30)
docs.text:
• Building and running service and interface tests: unit tests are run using Visual Studio Test (VSTest), integrated into the pipeline. These tests verify the functionality of the main modules and the interoperability between services. Test results are automatically collected and analyzed to assess compliance with quality criteria.
  • Code coverage: the system uses JetBrains dotCover to collect coverage metrics, allowing the degree of test validation of the code to be measured. This step only runs if the build succeeds, avoiding reports on inconsistent versions.

  • Static code analysis (SonarQube): although some analyses appear disabled in the screenshots, the SDLC process considers their execution part of the full cycle. The TypeScript, T-SQL and C# modules are audited for vulnerabilities, poor practices or insecure code. This provides evidence of compliance with the static analysis controls of OWASP SAMM and ISO/IEC 27034.

docs.title: 3.4. Artifact and documentation generation (steps 16–22)
docs.text:
• Automated changelog: generated through PowerShell, ensuring traceability between versions and facilitating change audits.
  • Secure packaging (ZIP APP, ZIP DOCU, NuGet package): artifacts are packaged automatically and versioned, including a build number and an internal digital signature. This process guarantees the non-repudiation and integrity of the distributed artifacts.

  • Automatic technical documentation generation: three types of documentation are generated:

    • JS: through Node.js (YUIDoc)
    • C#: through GhostDoc
    • SQL: through TeamCity SQLDoc

    This ensures documentation consistency and technical traceability between code and documentation.

docs.title: 3.5. Backup and configuration control (step 26 and 12–15)
docs.text:
• Post-publication backup copy: automatic copies are generated after publishing each build, ensuring the preservation of final artifacts and deployment evidence.
  • Configuration file management: the system cleans and replaces config files at different points of the pipeline (start and close) to ensure that:
    • No credentials or keys are exposed in test environments.
    • Sensitive configurations stay out of source control.

docs.title: 3.6. Dynamic security scanning and validation (SecDevOps)
docs.text:
The SecDevOps pipeline, integrated within the development cycle, is responsible for validating the software's resilience against vulnerabilities and exploits before it is published. The flow includes the following automated steps:

  1. Download the installer: retrieves the latest compiled version of the software from the internal repositories, ensuring tests run against the final version rather than intermediate environments.
  2. Install Flexygo: automates installing the application in an isolated test environment that replicates the production infrastructure.
  3. Run exploit (automated security testing): a Python script (flexygoscan.py) is run that performs controlled penetration tests against the deployed instance. These tests include validations of authentication, SQL injection, XSS and session manipulation, serving as evidence of an active dynamic application security testing (DAST) process.
  4. Uninstall Flexygo: the test environment is automatically cleaned up once the analysis finishes, ensuring no execution artifacts or sensitive data remain.
  5. Delete the test database: as the final phase, the database used during the tests is securely deleted, preserving confidentiality and preventing information exposure.

This process constitutes key evidence of operational security, demonstrating that Flexygo applies active controls for early vulnerability detection before releasing versions.

docs.title: 3.7. Artifact publishing and distribution control
docs.text:
The final publishing flow includes validating and deploying NuGet packages to authenticated repositories:

  1. Publishing internal and external NuGet artifacts:
    • Ahora's corporate repository (nuget.ahorabh.com)
    • Microsoft's official NuGet repository (nuget.org)
  2. Each publication is conditioned on the successful completion of all previous steps, ensuring that only verified and audited artifacts are distributed.
  3. Marking artifacts as "pinned": the final PowerShell process locks critical versions in the internal repository, preventing their accidental deletion or overwriting. This control ensures the traceability and availability of certified versions.

docs.title: 4. Audits and traceability
docs.text:
Every SDLC stage is logged in the continuous integration system, making it possible to audit:

  • Execution times
  • Test results
  • Build and publishing logs
  • Generated versions
  • Configuration changes

The pipeline prevents moving on to the next phase if a step doesn't run correctly, which constitutes a security flow control and evidence of compliance with DevSecOps best practices.

docs.title: 5. Conclusions
docs.text:
Flexygo's secure development model incorporates security, control and traceability mechanisms across the entire software lifecycle. The evidence shows the systematic application of information protection measures, version control, code auditing and artifact validation.

This process complies with the principles of a secure SDLC, aligned with international standards such as OWASP SAMM, ISO/IEC 27034 and NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF), providing guarantees of integrity, traceability and security for the software produced.

docs.title: Vulnerability management
docs.text: At Flexygo, vulnerability management is a key process within the secure development lifecycle (SecDevOps). This process ensures early detection, assessment, prioritization and remediation of vulnerabilities present in the code or in deployment environments, guaranteeing the integrity, availability and confidentiality of applications.

docs.title: 1. Vulnerability detection with SonarQube
docs.text:
Flexygo uses SonarQube as its main tool for static code analysis. This system is integrated directly into the development pipelines and performs the following functions:

  • Automatic analysis of the source code on every commit or pull request, detecting vulnerabilities, code smells and poor security practices.
  • Quality assessment based on OWASP security rules and international standards (CWE, SANS).
  • Risk report generation, reviewed by the development and security team before approving integration into the main environment.
  • Alerts and metrics: SonarQube automatically notifies the people responsible when critical or blocking vulnerabilities are detected.

docs.title: 2. Integration with the SecDevOps cycle
docs.text:
The SecDevOps strategy implemented at Flexygo ensures that security is present from the earliest stages of development. Its key principles include:

  • Shift-Left Security: detection and remediation happen in early development phases, reducing cost and time.
  • Test automation: CI/CD pipelines automatically run security analyses and pre-deployment validations, launching attack scripts against every final version.
  • Multidisciplinary collaboration: development, operations and security teams work together to ensure vulnerabilities are managed efficiently and transparently.

docs.title: 3. Remediation and deployment with GitFlow and Hotfix
docs.text:
If a critical vulnerability is detected in production, a structured remediation flow based on GitFlow is followed:

  1. Creating a Hotfix branch: a specific branch is created from main or release to address the issue without interfering with ongoing development.
  2. Fix and validation: the development team implements the fix and re-runs the SonarQube analyses to verify the patch's effectiveness.
  3. Immediate deployment (Hotfix): once the fix is validated, it is deployed immediately to the production environment through the automated pipeline.
  4. Controlled merge: the Hotfix branch is then merged into develop and main, ensuring the fixed code is synchronized across all active branches.

docs.title: 4. Mitigation and preventive measures
docs.text:
In addition to detection and remediation processes, Flexygo implements active mitigation mechanisms that protect the environment in real time against exploitation attempts. The system monitors every incoming request, analyzing its parameters and behavior. If a suspicious pattern or signs of an attack are identified — such as code injection, header manipulation or unauthorized access attempts — the request is blocked immediately. Likewise, if five suspicious requests from the same IP are detected within a minute, the system automatically blocks that IP address as a preventive measure.

Additionally, to prevent brute-force attacks, Flexygo applies a temporary user lockout after five failed authentication attempts, preventing repeated access attempts and significantly reducing the risk of credential compromise. These measures, combined with early detection and automated response, strengthen the overall security posture of the Flexygo ecosystem.

docs.title: Requirements for certifying a new Flexygo product
Requirements for certifying a new Flexygo product
Overview
docs.text:
To certify a product at the factory and publish it on the marketplace, several requirements must be met and commercial and technical demonstrations must be presented (these can be done online).

Every certified product must be built starting from Flexygo as a NuGet package; development built on top of another Flexygo product will not be certified.

docs.title: Marketing
docs.text:
• Product name
  • Pricing structure
  • Logo
  • Promotional text
  • Promotional video

docs.title: Technical requirements
docs.text:
• Installer* (depends on the factory)
  • Publish a NuGet package to a public repository
  • Continuous deployment (automatic updates)
  • Implemented security (roles/profiles)
  • Functional demonstration of the application
  • Testing with demonstrable minimums
  • Include the licensing chain* (depends on the factory)

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Friendly interface (UI/UX)
  • Continuous database deployment
  • Functional and technical documentation
  • Functional videos
  • Product roadmap

* Items marked with an asterisk are the factory's responsibility and are provided once certification is complete.

docs.title: How do I generate a HOTFIX?
How do I generate a HOTFIX?
Full procedure
docs.text:
Before starting the hotfix, we pull develop and master and make sure we're up to date:

We click GitFlow > Start new hotfix

We name the branch starting with HOTFIX_ (uppercase) followed by a short description that identifies it. We click OK.

We publish the project's databases, set the correct origin, make the fix and download the changes, the same way we would for a new feature.

We review the pending changes and mark the ones that belong to the fix.

We make a commit starting the message with the FIX: tag, followed by the description of the fix (the symptom users saw). The release notes only pick up FT:, FIX:, HL: and DEP: commits; see How do I develop in GIT?.

We fetch and check that we have no pending pulls; if we do, we switch to the corresponding branch, pull, and go back to the hotfix branch.

We click Git Flow > Finish Hotfix

We push develop, switch to master and push master as well.

docs.title: How do I generate a RELEASE?
How do I generate a RELEASE?
1. Create the release in SourceTree
docs.text:
Start from the develop branch, clean and with no pending changes.

  • Click the Git-Flow button

  • Confirm the popup screen with OK

  • Click Git-Flow again

  • Select Start New Release and enter a name such as RELEASE_4_11_0_1

A new branch is created from develop. Run tests and fix any issues on it through normal commits until it's validated.

  • Click Git-Flow again and select Finish Release

  • Confirm the merge into master and develop, including the corresponding tag

Before pushing

Before pushing, the next step on TeamCity must be completed.

docs.title: 2. Update the version number in TeamCity
docs.text:
• Go to the develop branch project → Edit settings
  • Change the first two numbers of the Build Number format (e.g. from 4.10 to 4.11) and reset the Build Counter to 1
  • Repeat the same process on the master branch project → Edit settings
  • Change the format (e.g. from 4.10.0 to 4.11.0) and reset the counter

docs.title: 3. Back in SourceTree
docs.text:
• Push the pending merges
  • Verify that TeamCity builds and publishes correctly

docs.title: How do I develop in GIT?
How do I develop in GIT?
Commit prefixes for the release notes
docs.text:
The subject of every commit starts with a prefix. With it, the commit's text is automatically included in the release notes of the version (in the application, the help and the NuGet package):

  • FT: marks a new feature or an improvement users can see
  • FIX: marks the fix of an identified issue; describe the symptom users saw
  • HL: marks one of the highlights of the version (only a few per version). Besides the note, it opens the summary and the news article of the version and generates a help page
  • DEP: marks features that become deprecated or discontinued, and what to use instead
  • INT: internal work (refactors, build, tests, tooling, internal documentation). It never appears in the release notes

The notes are written only from the subject and body of the commit, never from the code: describe what changes for the user, not which classes were touched.

docs.title: Rules the repository checks
docs.text:
The commit-msg hook of the Flexygo repository (.githooks/commit-msg) rejects the commit if it breaks them:

  • The subject starts with one of the prefixes above (merges and reverts are exempt).
  • The subject is longer than 50 characters (better keep it at most about 72).
  • No line contains ... as filler.
  • An HL: commit adds at least one image (.png, .jpg, .jpeg or .gif) under release-notes/images/.

docs.title: HL: commits
docs.text:
The body of an HL: follows a fixed structure, because the highlighted note, the news article and the help page are written from it (and from its screenshot):

Text Only
HL: Update Flexygo from a guided wizard with automatic rollback

What: A wizard updates the frontend, the backend and the database in one go, checks the
requirements and the locks first, and rolls the update back when it does not finish.
Where: Admin > Maintenance > Versions, button "Update".
How:
1. Open the Versions page and choose the version to install.
2. Review the requirements and the locks the wizard detects.
3. Start the update and follow its progress; the log can be filtered.
Settings: Repository and credentials of the packages in the updater settings.
Permissions: Administrators only.
Help: Maintenance and updates
  • What, Where and How are mandatory; Settings, Permissions and Help only when they apply.
  • The screenshot is mandatory and goes in the same commit, under release-notes/images/, with a descriptive kebab-case name (update-wizard.png).

docs.title: 🔄 Evolución de la arquitectura
docs.text:
Flexygo ha evolucionado desde el modelo clásico basado en .NET Framework hacia una arquitectura completamente nueva basada en .NET 9.

Hasta ahora, el modelo de Flexygo consistía en una única aplicación web que contenía tanto el frontend como el backend y todas sus librerías dentro del mismo sitio.

Con la nueva arquitectura, Flexygo se divide en:

  • 🖥️ Frontend: la interfaz web que el usuario ve
  • ⚙️ Backend: la lógica del servidor y las APIs
  • 🛢️ Base de datos

Este enfoque modular responde a varios objetivos clave:

  • Seguridad: al separar los componentes, puedes alojar el frontend en un servidor distinto del backend y la base de datos. Si se comprometiera el servidor frontend, no habría acceso directo a los datos ni a la lógica interna.
  • Escalabilidad: puedes distribuir las partes del sistema en diferentes entornos físicos o virtuales.
  • Flexibilidad: permite desplegar soluciones personalizadas y adaptadas a cada cliente o entorno.
  • Rendimiento y mantenimiento: usar .NET 9 permite trabajar con las últimas mejoras del ecosistema .NET en rendimiento, soporte multiplataforma y facilidad de despliegue.

Con esta base, Flexygo continúa modernizando todo su ecosistema, asegurando su futuro y adaptándolo a los estándares actuales de desarrollo empresarial.

docs.title: 🚀 ¿Cómo se despliega Flexygo?
docs.text:
Tienes varias opciones para ejecutar o desplegar tu solución Flexygo:

  • Instalador — Ideal para entornos Windows. Incluye modos IIS básico, IIS avanzado y Docker vía instalador. Automatiza toda la configuración.
  • Docker — Perfecto para despliegue en la nube, entornos Linux o soluciones automatizadas con contenedores.
  • Kestrel — Ejecutable directamente con dotnet run, ideal para entornos de desarrollo o soluciones con proxy inverso.

Consulta la sección Despliegue del menú para ver guías detalladas de cada opción.

docs.title: Tecnologías de Flexygo
docs.text: Flexygo está desarrollado sobre el framework .NET Core, proporcionando una base moderna, multiplataforma y de alto rendimiento. Su compatibilidad nativa tanto con bases de datos SQL Server como Oracle ofrece una gran flexibilidad arquitectónica.

docs.title: Front End
docs.text: Al desarrollar el front-end de un producto Flexygo podrás utilizar las propias herramientas de Flexygo, como los módulos y componentes predefinidos. Además, tendrás acceso a HTML, CSS, JS y Bootstrap.

docs.title: Back End
docs.text: Al estar desarrollado en .NET Core, Flexygo permite la creación de procesos DLL en C# o VB.NET, y también admite procedimientos almacenados tanto en SQL Server como en Oracle, tal y como se ha mencionado anteriormente.

docs.title: Objetos
docs.text:
Los objetos de Flexygo son los bloques fundamentales para la creación de aplicaciones en Flexygo. Cada objeto corresponde a un elemento principal de tu negocio —como un Cliente, Proyecto o Factura— e incluye todo lo necesario para gestionarlo: su estructura de datos, formularios de entrada, vistas de listado, informes y procesos relacionados.

Mediante la configuración de estos objetos reutilizables, puedes crear rápidamente aplicaciones web a medida sin necesidad de mucho código, garantizando la coherencia y ahorrando tiempo de desarrollo.

docs.title: Módulos
docs.text: Los productos Flexygo se construyen utilizando módulos, que son componentes fáciles de configurar con múltiples capacidades, como mostrar gráficos, crear un Kanban, mostrar mapas con ubicaciones y rutas, y muchas funcionalidades más.

docs.title: Creación de informes
docs.text: Flexygo también ofrece la posibilidad de crear tus propios informes en HTML, Power BI, DevExpress y Crystal Reports.

docs.title: Aplicación Offline
docs.text: Flexygo también ofrece la posibilidad de crear una aplicación móvil independiente a la que se puede acceder sin conexión, permitiendo continuar trabajando incluso en lugares remotos con baja conectividad.

docs.title: Tecnologías
docs.text: La aplicación Offline de Flexygo utiliza Ionic como base, junto con Capacitor y Stencil. También utiliza SQLite como sistema de almacenamiento de los datos que se sincronizan con tu proyecto Flexygo.

docs.title: Desarrollo
docs.text: El desarrollo de la aplicación Offline de Flexygo requiere un mayor conocimiento de programación, ya que las páginas deben construirse utilizando HTML, CSS, JS e Ionic.

docs.title: Seguimiento
docs.text: La aplicación Offline de Flexygo dispone de funcionalidad de seguimiento, que permite obtener los datos exactos de localización de los dispositivos configurados incluso cuando la aplicación está cerrada. Puede configurarse para realizar el seguimiento únicamente durante determinados periodos de tiempo.

docs.title: Más información
docs.text: Además de la documentación técnica recogida en Ayuda, este sitio incluye documentación específica sobre Despliegue, Desarrollo de producto, CI/CD y Solución de Problemas, así como la sección Más información, con contenido adicional sobre Flexygo: preguntas frecuentes, curiosidades ("¿Sabías que...?"), notas de versión, guías de seguridad y del ciclo de CI/CD, entre otros.

docs.title: Arquitectura de Flexygo 10.0+
docs.text:
Desde la versión 10, Flexygo funciona sobre .NET 9, la plataforma actual de Microsoft, en lugar de .NET Framework. Es más rápido y más seguro, y sigue recibiendo actualizaciones de Microsoft.

La aplicación se divide en tres piezas que pueden estar juntas en un mismo servidor o cada una en el suyo:

Pieza Qué hace Frontend Es lo que abre el navegador: las pantallas, los menús y la skin, y los asistentes de instalación y de versiones. No se conecta a la base de datos: le pide todo al backend. Backend Hace el trabajo: la lógica, la seguridad, los procesos, las tareas programadas y los informes. También atiende la WebAPI y el servidor MCP de las integraciones. SQL Server Guarda la configuración de la aplicación y los datos del producto.

Separarlas permite, por ejemplo, dejar el frontend en un servidor accesible desde fuera y el backend y la base de datos en la red interna, o dar más recursos solo a la pieza que más trabajo tiene.

docs.title: Dónde se puede instalar
docs.text:
• IIS, en Windows: el instalador lo hace todo. En modo IIS básico frontend y backend van en el mismo sitio; en IIS avanzado pueden ir en sitios o servidores distintos.
  • Docker: frontend y backend en contenedores, con la base de datos fuera de Docker en producción. Ver Despliegue con Docker.
  • Servicio independiente (Kestrel), en Windows o en Linux, normalmente detrás de un proxy inverso como nginx. No tiene instalador propio. Ver Despliegue con Kestrel y Proxy inverso.

Antes de instalar, revisa los requisitos del sistema.

docs.title: Actualizar
docs.text: Flexygo se actualiza desde la propia aplicación con el asistente de versiones, que comprueba los requisitos antes de empezar y puede deshacer una actualización. Ver Actualizador de Flexygo.

docs.title: Requisitos del sistema
docs.text: Esta página recoge los requisitos necesarios para instalar Flexygo en un entorno Windows con IIS.

docs.title: Requisitos previos
docs.text:
Antes de comenzar, asegúrate de que el entorno dispone de:

  • IIS instalado y configurado (el instalador puede instalarlo si no lo está)
  • SQL Server 2022 o superior (opcionalmente instalable también desde el instalador)
  • .NET Hosting Bundle (instalado automáticamente por el instalador si se detecta su ausencia)
  • Permisos de administrador en el equipo

docs.title: Instalación de IIS y SQL Server
docs.text:
En modo avanzado, el instalador ofrece opciones automáticas para:

  • Instalar IIS si no está presente en el sistema.
  • Instalar SQL Server Developer Edition si el usuario lo solicita (ideal para entornos de pruebas o instalaciones locales).

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
Para el correcto funcionamiento de Flexygo, es necesario habilitar WebSocket en las características de Windows:

Ve a Panel de control → Programas → Activar o desactivar las características de Windows y asegúrate de que WebSocket está habilitado bajo las características de IIS.

docs.title: SQL Server
docs.text:
Flexygo 10 requiere SQL Server 2022 o superior

A partir de Flexygo 10, la versión mínima de SQL Server es SQL Server 2022. Las bases de datos de la aplicación deben estar en un servidor SQL Server 2022 o posterior; si el servidor es anterior, actualízalo antes de instalar, actualizar o migrar la aplicación.

docs.title: Dimensionamiento orientativo
docs.text:
Para unos 100 usuarios simultáneos se recomienda separar la aplicación y SQL Server en máquinas distintas:

Máquina SQL Server Máquina de la aplicación (IIS) Sistema operativo Windows Server 2016 Standard o superior Windows Server 2016 Standard o superior Procesador Intel Xeon (referencia: E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz) Intel Xeon (referencia: E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz) Memoria 16 GB de RAM (ampliable) 8 GB de RAM (ampliable) Disco 500 GB 500 GB

El espacio en disco depende del proyecto; para una gestión documental o de imágenes de gran volumen se recomienda un NAS externo. Más usuarios se reparten con varias máquinas de aplicación tras un balanceador. Para bases de datos de más de 30 GB, consulta este artículo sobre memoria en SQL Server.

docs.title: Instalador: Modo Despliegue
docs.text:
El modo Despliegue del instalador de Flexygo permite configurar el entorno para producción o pre-producción.

Docker en producción

Para entornos de producción con Docker se recomienda usar la guía de Docker con docker-compose manual, que ofrece mayor control sobre la configuración.

docs.title: 1. Selección de producto
docs.text:
El primer paso es elegir qué producto quieres instalar. El instalador muestra las soluciones disponibles (Flexygo, SAT, CRM…) y la opción Personalizado, que permite especificar manualmente el paquete NuGet a instalar y su origen.

Si seleccionas Personalizado, deberás indicar el nombre del paquete NuGet y dónde buscarlo: una URL de feed remoto o una ruta física local. El nombre del paquete debe seguir la convención de nombres de Flexygo para que el instalador lo detecte correctamente.

docs.title: 2. Modo de instalación
docs.text:
Una vez seleccionado el producto, elige el modo de instalación según tu entorno:

IIS BásicoIIS AvanzadoDocker (vía Installer)

docs.title: Instalación básica
docs.text: Instala Frontend y Backend en el mismo servidor y sitio IIS. Ideal para pruebas, demos o entornos pequeños.

docs.title: Configuración del sitio
docs.text: Elige el nombre del proyecto, selecciona un sitio web existente o crea uno nuevo, establece el path virtual (si lo deseas) y el directorio físico donde se instalará la aplicación.

docs.title: Instalación avanzada
docs.text: Permite instalar Frontend y Backend en servidores distintos, o instalar solo uno de los dos componentes. Adecuada para instalaciones personalizadas en producción.

docs.title: Selección de componentes
docs.text: Elige si instalar solo Frontend, solo Backend, o ambos. También puedes instalar IIS y/o SQL Server si tu entorno aún no los tiene, y optar por instalar una versión específica del producto.

docs.title: Versión específica
docs.text: Si seleccionaste instalar una versión específica, indica el nombre del paquete y su origen (URL de feed remoto o ruta física). El asistente buscará las versiones disponibles para que elijas la que necesitas.

docs.title: Configuración de Frontend
docs.text: Elige el nombre del proyecto, sitio IIS, path virtual y directorio físico donde se instalará el Frontend.

docs.title: Configuración de Backend
docs.text: Elige el nombre del proyecto, sitio IIS, path virtual y directorio físico donde se instalará el Backend.

docs.title: Instalación Docker
docs.text:
Despliega Flexygo directamente sobre Docker Desktop. Orientado a entornos de demo, pruebas o desarrollo local con contenedores.

Requisito previo

Asegúrate de tener Docker Desktop instalado y en ejecución antes de continuar. Puedes descargarlo desde docker.com/products/docker-desktop.

docs.title: Configuración del despliegue Docker
docs.text:
Configura los parámetros del contenedor: puertos, volúmenes y opciones de despliegue para Frontend y Backend.

Resultado

Una vez confirmada la configuración, el instalador levanta los contenedores directamente en Docker Desktop. Puedes acceder a la aplicación desde el propio Docker Desktop o mediante el puerto configurado.

docs.title: 3. Progreso y finalización
docs.text:
(Solo modos IIS Básico e IIS Avanzado)

Verás el progreso de la instalación paso a paso. Una vez finalizada, el asistente muestra un resumen y ofrece abrir la aplicación directamente en el navegador.

docs.title: Instalador: Modo Desarrollo
docs.text:
El modo Desarrollo del instalador está orientado a desarrolladores que trabajan con proyectos Flexygo en Visual Studio o VS Code. Ofrece tres operaciones: crear un nuevo producto desde la plantilla oficial, crear un addon (en los productos que los admiten, como Flexygo) o gestionar productos ya existentes en el workspace.

Requisito previo para VS Code: Node.js en PATH global

Si vas a trabajar con el proyecto desde VS Code, necesitas tener Node.js instalado y disponible en el PATH global del sistema. Si no está en el PATH, la compilación del Frontend fallará. Consulta los requisitos de desarrollo.

Pantalla principal del modo Desarrollo Crear productoCrear addonGestionar productos

docs.title: Crear un nuevo producto
docs.text:
Esta opción genera la estructura completa de un producto Flexygo a partir de la plantilla oficial: proyectos Frontend, Backend y bases de datos, listos para abrir en Visual Studio o VS Code.

Formulario para crear un nuevo producto

Introduce el nombre del producto y la ruta donde se generará el proyecto. El instalador instala la plantilla (o la actualiza si ya está instalada) e instala o actualiza también las herramientas de desarrollo:

  • Flexygo Product Tools — permite generar NuGets y actualizar el proyecto desde línea de comandos o desde las extensiones de Visual Studio y VS Code
  • Flexygo MCP — servidor MCP para construir la aplicación con Claude Code y otros clientes de IA

Una vez completado, crea la solución a partir de la plantilla.

Producto generado — listo para abrir en Visual Studio o VS Code

Alternativa por línea de comandos

También puedes crear un producto usando la plantilla directamente con dotnet new. Consulta la guía de Plantilla de producto.

docs.title: Crear un addon
docs.text:
La opción Crear addon solo aparece en los productos que admiten addons, como Flexygo. Genera la solución de un addon con la plantilla de addon del producto: pide la carpeta del producto y el nombre del addon, que tiene que ser distinto del del producto. Si la carpeta está vacía, crea primero el producto y después el addon.

El proceso completo, desde la creación hasta el empaquetado como NuGet, está en Crear un addon.

docs.title: Gestionar productos existentes
docs.text: Esta opción escanea el workspace en busca de proyectos Flexygo y permite actualizar la versión del Core o generar los NuGets del producto.

docs.title: Carga del workspace
docs.text:
Al entrar, el instalador analiza el workspace en busca de soluciones Flexygo.

El instalador escanea el workspace en busca de proyectos Flexygo

docs.title: Lista de productos
docs.text:
Una vez cargados, los productos aparecen mostrando la versión actual instalada y la última versión estable disponible de Flexygo. Se puede alternar entre vista de lista y cuadrícula, y filtrar por nombre.

Vista de lista: versión actual → última versión estable disponible, con acciones por producto

Vista de cuadrícula con filtro activo

docs.title: Actualizar versión del Core
docs.text:
Pulsa Actualizar en el producto deseado para actualizar los paquetes NuGet del Core a la versión disponible. El instalador realiza el proceso y confirma el resultado.

Confirmación de actualización del producto a la nueva versión del Core

No actualices manualmente los paquetes NuGet

El actualizador realiza pasos adicionales (sincronización de recursos, sustitución de los appsettings conservando tus ConnectionStrings, DatabaseNuget y MailSettings…; ver Gestión de productos) que no ocurren con una actualización manual de NuGet desde Visual Studio o VS Code.

docs.title: Generar NuGets del producto
docs.text:
Pulsa Generar NuGets para empaquetar el producto. El instalador pide la versión con la que etiquetar los paquetes generados.

Introduce la versión con la que se generarán los paquetes NuGet del producto

Al completarse, se abre automáticamente el explorador de archivos con la carpeta donde se han generado los paquetes. Los paquetes resultantes (Frontend, Backend, Conf.Database, Data.Database) quedan disponibles para publicar en un feed NuGet o distribuir al instalador.

docs.title: Instalador de Flexygo
docs.text:
El instalador de Flexygo es la herramienta principal para gestionar el ciclo de vida completo de una instalación: desde el despliegue inicial hasta la migración desde versiones anteriores o la desinstalación.

Pantalla de inicio del instalador (modo oscuro) Pantalla de inicio del instalador (modo claro)

docs.title: Modos disponibles
docs.text:
El instalador cubre los siguientes escenarios:

  • Despliegue — Instalación en un entorno de producción o pre-producción. Disponible en tres variantes: IIS básico (sitio único compartido), IIS avanzado (sitios independientes por componente) y Docker vía installer.

  • Desarrollo — Instalación orientada a entornos locales de desarrollo, con opciones específicas para trabajar con el código fuente.

  • Migración — Migración de proyectos o aplicaciones existentes de .NET Framework a Flexygo (.NET moderno).

  • Desinstalar — Eliminación limpia de una instalación existente, incluyendo sitios IIS y bases de datos asociadas.

docs.title: Instalador: Modo Migración
docs.text:
El modo Migración del instalador permite trasladar proyectos y aplicaciones de .NET Framework a .NET Core (Flexygo). Ofrece dos variantes según el punto de partida.

El modo Migración ofrece 2 opciones

Flexygo 10 requiere SQL Server 2022 o superior

A partir de Flexygo 10, la versión mínima de SQL Server es SQL Server 2022. Antes de migrar, comprueba que el servidor SQL donde están las bases de datos de la aplicación cumple este requisito; si no, actualízalo primero. Consulta los Requisitos del sistema.

Migrar ProductosMigrar Aplicaciones

docs.title: Migrar proyectos
docs.text: Esta opción escanea el workspace en busca de soluciones .NET Framework de Flexygo y permite migrarlas a la estructura de Flexygo (.NET moderno).

docs.title: Migrar desde VS Code con Claude Code
docs.text:
Si abres un proyecto de Flexygo para .NET Framework en VS Code con la extensión de Flexygo, el panel avisa de que usa una versión obsoleta y ofrece Migrar a Flexygo Core. La ventana que se abre propone dos caminos:

  • Con IA (Claude Code): la extensión instala la skill flexygo-migrar-core, que hace toda la migración por ti: crea la rama, actualiza el NuGet de Flexygo, lanza este instalador, coloca la solución Core en el repositorio, la valida y la corrige, y deja un informe, con un commit por fase. Copia el comando /flexygo-migrar-core y pégalo en Claude Code abierto en la carpeta del proyecto, o pulsa Abrir Claude Code en un terminal.
  • Sin IA: descarga el instalador y migra el proyecto a mano con los pasos de este apartado.

La extensión de VS Code detecta el proyecto .NET Framework y propone migrarlo con la skill de Claude Code

docs.title: Carga del workspace
docs.text:
Indica la carpeta de trabajo donde se encuentran los proyectos y pulsa Escanear proyectos. El instalador analizará el workspace en busca de soluciones .NET Framework de Flexygo.

Especifica la carpeta de trabajo y pulsa Escanear proyectos

docs.title: Lista de productos
docs.text:
Los proyectos encontrados se muestran con su versión actual. Se puede alternar entre vista de lista y cuadrícula, y filtrar por nombre.

Vista de lista con los proyectos disponibles para migrar

Vista de cuadrícula con filtro activo

docs.title: Migrar
docs.text: Pulsa Migrar en el proyecto deseado. El instalador genera la nueva estructura de Flexygo a partir del proyecto existente.

docs.title: Migración completada
docs.text:
Al finalizar, el instalador ofrece abrir el proyecto migrado directamente en Visual Studio o VS Code.

El proyecto migrado puede abrirse directamente en Visual Studio o VS Code

Revisiones necesarias tras migrar el proyecto

Antes de compilar y probar el proyecto migrado, revisa los siguientes puntos:

Conf.Database

  • Abre el proyecto Conf.Database y revisa el fichero de configuración y la integridad del script postdeploy migrado.
  • Revisa también los scripts de staticdata para asegurarte de que se han migrado correctamente y no contienen referencias obsoletas.
  • Verifica también el fichero config.sql y comprueba su integridad. El migrador reemplaza automáticamente AutoUpdatePackageId por AutoUpdatePackageNamespace en este fichero, pero si tienes este valor configurado en algún otro script deberás reemplazarlo manualmente.

Carpetas de artefactos antiguos

Elimina manualmente las carpetas Properties, obj y debug que puedan haber quedado de la solución anterior en los proyectos Frontend, Backend y Processes (si existe). Estas carpetas pueden contener assemblies de .NET Framework incompatibles con la nueva solución. Se volverán a generar correctamente al compilar.

Namespaces obsoletos en Processes

Si los Processes están escritos en C#, es posible que hagan uso de namespaces que ya no existen en .NET moderno. Los casos más habituales son:

Namespace .NET Framework Equivalente en .NET System.Web Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http System.Web.HttpContext Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext System.Web.HttpRequest Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpRequest System.Web.HttpResponse Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResponse System.Web.HttpServerUtility Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHostEnvironment System.Web.SessionState Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.ISession

Revisa los using de cada Process y sustituye los obsoletos por sus equivalentes. Si hay casos no contemplados en la tabla, consulta la guía oficial de migración de ASP.NET a ASP.NET Core.

docs.title: Migrar aplicaciones IIS
docs.text: Esta opción detecta las aplicaciones Flexygo de .NET Framework desplegadas en IIS y las migra a .NET Core en su lugar.

docs.title: Aplicaciones encontradas
docs.text:
El instalador lista las aplicaciones IIS de Flexygo Framework detectadas en el sistema.

Aplicaciones Flexygo Framework encontradas en IIS

docs.title: Origen de paquetes NuGet
docs.text:
Antes de iniciar, el instalador solicita el namespace del producto y la URL del feed NuGet desde donde descargará los paquetes correspondientes a la aplicación que se pretenda migrar.

Indica el namespace del producto y el feed NuGet origen

docs.title: Confirmación — Leer antes de continuar
docs.text:
El instalador muestra un diálogo de confirmación con advertencias importantes:
